PGEN SystemVerilog Parser — Integration Reference

Welcome — PGEN SystemVerilog Parser Integration Reference

This book is the canonical AST reference for downstream consumers of PGEN’s systemverilog parser family. The intended primary audience is Nexsim and any other tool embedding the PGEN-generated SystemVerilog parser through the pgen::embedding_api host surface.

What this book covers

  • How to build the generated parser and wire it into your project. See Build Recipe and Public API Surface.
  • What the AST envelope looks like. See AST Envelope Structure, ParseContent Variants, and Walking the AST.
  • The shape every grammar rule produces in the AST dump. See Per-Rule Shape Reference. As the return-annotation campaign progresses, this section grows to cover every rule that has a stable typed shape.
  • Worked examples by SystemVerilog feature — what does the AST look like for a minimal module? An interface? A class? Each example chapter pins a current production AST so consumers can write their walkers against a concrete, tested reference.
  • Schema versioning policy. See Schema Versioning. ⛔ The live schema version is not restated here — it is held in docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md § SystemVerilog AST-dump schema version, which is authoritative. This sentence used to carry the number and published 13 while the contract carried 26.
  • A release-by-release index of what changed and why. See Changelog Index.

What this book is NOT

  • It is not a substitute for the integration contract docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md. The contract is the authoritative source of truth; this book documents what the contract describes. Where the book and the contract disagree, the contract wins. Please report any disagreement as a documentation bug.
  • It is not the IEEE 1800 LRM. The LRM is the authoritative SystemVerilog language reference; this book documents PGEN’s parser-side AST shape for the LRM-conformant inputs the parser accepts.
  • It is not a tutorial on SystemVerilog. It assumes you are already an embedded user of the language and need to walk PGEN’s AST output programmatically.

How to use this book

  1. First-time integrators: read Quickstart, then Build Recipe, then Public API Surface.
  2. Walking the AST: read AST Envelope Structure, then look up the per-rule chapters for the rules you consume.
  3. Pinning to a known shape: read Schema Versioning for the policy and Changelog Index for the per-release shape changes.
  4. Reporting issues: follow docs/contracts/PGEN_PARSER_ISSUE_REPORTING_PROTOCOL.md for the bug-report protocol; accepted released-parser bugs land in docs/contracts/PGEN_RELEASED_PARSER_BUG_LEDGER.md under the SV-NNNN ID family.

Status

⭐ The live answer is Status and Distance to Done — where this family stands against the three-leg Done bar, how much of its corpus passes, and against which denominator. Every figure on that page is derived by scripts/report_family_status.sh and held equal to the tree by its --check mode, so it cannot quietly go stale.

⛔ This section deliberately restates none of it, and the reason is measured. Until 2026-08-30 it carried three hand-written figures and every one of them was wrong: the AST-dump schema was published as 10 here and as 13 two paragraphs above while the contract carried 26, and the parser was described as “validated each release by the … external-corpus (14/14) … gates” while scripts/audit_done_bar.sh records the only gate reading that corpus as a triage gate — which is not a conformance gate, and leaves leg 3 of the bar unmet. A hand-maintained status paragraph rots (LIVE-MEANS-LIVE.1a measured 25 of 61 such fields simply wrong), so this one is now a pointer to a derived surface.

The formal trust statement remains docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md: it is authoritative for the shipped parser release, the AST-dump schema version, and what a consumer may rely on. Each shape-affecting change gets its own Schema Versioning row, a released-parser bug-ledger entry where it is a genuine bug, and an entry in the Changelog Index.

Status and Distance to Done

One question, answered by measurement: how far is this parser from Done, and how much of the corpus passes today?

A status label — Mostly Done, In Progress — says where a family sits on a ladder. It does not say how far it still has to climb, and a reader who only sees the label has no way to tell whether the remaining work is a week or a year. This page publishes the distance behind the label.

This page is DERIVED BY MEASUREMENT. The block below is produced by scripts/report_family_status.sh, which reads the done-bar audit and the corpus census rather than any hand-maintained note. Do not hand-edit it — re-run with systemverilog --markdown and republish; --check docs/systemverilog_parser_book/src/status-and-distance.md refuses when the two disagree. Every field, and the producer that answers it, is declared in rust/test_data/grammar_quality/family_status_block_v0.json.

The three-leg bar, and what it takes to clear it

Done here is not a feeling about maturity. It is a three-leg bar, defined in the main book’s Quality and Closure Model and audited by scripts/audit_done_bar.sh:

  1. Stimuli-generator proof — the family’s own generated samples close the loop with zero residual actionable-target debt.
  2. All our gates — every gate covering the family is green now and is actually invoked by something. A gate nothing invokes is indistinguishable from a gate that does not exist.
  3. All the external test corpus, passing — and a triage gate is not a conformance gate, a characterization is not a pass, and the absence of a corpus is an unmet leg, never an inapplicable one.

How to read the corpus table honestly

The denominator is every row of the SystemVerilog corpus adjudication manifests — not the subset that happens to have been looked at. That choice is deliberate and it is the whole point of the SV-CORPUS-DENOMINATOR doctrine: a defect count published without its denominator is not a claim about the corpus. A row carrying no verdict is not evidence of correctness; it is not evidence of anything, and unknown and clean are different words.

The dark rows are the sharpest edge in the table: the parse failed, and the row’s deferral reason is why nobody has looked at it since. Every one of them is a question the project has not yet asked.

What leg 3 actually demands of these rows. The table above is the raw lane — every file parsed on its own bytes. The bar’s assertion does not stop there, and since DONE-BAR.3f (2026-10-08) it could not honestly: three classes of no-verdict row are not parser gaps at all.

  • A chained row (a multi-file design, deferred:chained_only) is deferred by the raw lane by design and read under the preprocess→parse pipeline’s re-adjudication (stimuli/sv/characterization/pipeline_readjudication.tsv, the lane the pipeline chapter describes). The assertion reads it there.
  • A permanently unadjudicable row — a $readmemh memory image, a Verilog-AMS file, a test whose own suite marks the verdict implementation-dependent, a construct the upstream runner skips — can never carry a verdict about SystemVerilog, and the project said so in SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13f: each class states its argument and is held under a recorded ceiling the instruments refuse to exceed. The assertion names and counts these rows; it does not demand them, and it never relabels them as a pass — they stay in the table above as no-verdict rows.
  • Everything else with no verdict is burnable: a row the project still owes a verdict.

Before .3f the assertion was zero no-verdict rows on the raw lane, which demanded a verdict for the first two classes too — a bar no parser could meet. The counts under this reading are the Under the reading leg 3 asserts table inside the derived block above (DONE-BAR.3g): per lane, adjudicated + permanently unadjudicable + still awaiting a verdict = the denominator, with the unexplained and bar counts and full_pass itself. They are derived on every render from the register’s tracked assertion (stimuli/sv/corpus_conformance_compare.py --assert-tracked …), the same command the done-bar audit evaluates, and cross-checked against the tuple under the pipeline that bash scripts/check_sv_corpus_denominator.sh prints — so the book, the audit and the denominator doctrine cannot disagree about this reading.

How this page stays true

  • One producer emits both renderings — the brief form reported in the engineer’s completion messages and the thorough block above — so the two cannot tell different stories.
  • --check re-derives the block and diffs it against what is published here, refusing on any difference. Republishing is the only way to change a number on this page.
  • The block is derived from the tracked tree alone. Legs 1 and the green-now half of leg 2 rest on gate artifacts under rust/target/, which is never tracked, so publishing this machine’s reading of them would make the check fail on a fresh clone. Run bash scripts/audit_done_bar.sh to see what the gate artifacts in your tree say.

Release distance — one number, re-derived every release

The question the director asked (2026-09-17): how far is the SV parser from its release, as a number a reader can watch move?

The three-leg bar above says whether the family is Done; the release distance counts what still stands between this tree and that bar, and its history says how fast the count has been falling. items = legs_unmet + bar_rows + open_leaves:

  • legs unmet — the Distance to Done`` line of the derived block above (owned by FAMILY-STATUS-CURRENCY).
  • bar rows — divergence:unexplained_* rows in the three adjudication manifests: the rows the parser must clear on sv_2017, sv_2023 and verilog_2005 (the bar the director’s directive names — “the SV parser shall cleanly pass all of them”).
  • open leaves — todo / active leaves of docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md plus the todo leaves of docs/tasks/ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.md that SV-CORPUS-GRAD opened (engine work the SV parser owes). Read by the STATUS WORD — a heading that is not ✅-headed and carries todo or active — never by its decoration (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.49, 2026-10-09: the first census counted a heading only when it began with exactly one ⛔ / ⏳ and read 3 where 10 were open; the engine matcher now tolerates the opener’s session #N token), at every heading level from ### to ######, counting each open leaf ONCE: a heading whose own section holds an open heading is an umbrella and is counted through its children, never beside them (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.51, 2026-10-09: the #####-only form read 8 where 11 were open). --self-test drives both censuses on the real heading shapes.

Every figure is derived from the tracked tree by scripts/report_sv_release_distance.sh; nothing here runs a gate, so a fresh clone re-derives the same block. Each parser release appends one row to the history (--record) — and so does a commit outside a release that moves the distance (a leaf closed or opened), under the shipped release’s label, so rows can share a label and the trailing rate divides by distinct releases (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.23, 2026-09-24) — and the doctrine SV-RELEASE-DISTANCE-CURRENCY refuses a commit whose published block or whose history’s last row disagrees with the tree. The history’s commit column names the tree a row was DERIVED from: a row written at a release’s lockstep step carries the release commit’s parent (the release commit does not exist yet when the row is written), a back-filled row the release commit itself. ⛔ What the number is not. The ETA is a trailing-rate ESTIMATE over the last five recorded releases; a structural leg (a corpus conformance gate, the generator proof) is one item that costs more than a bar row; the 38 % of corpus rows with no verdict are an answer-key gap outside items; and an item can be opened by a release as well as closed — the history shows both.

Quickstart for Downstream Consumers

A minimal “compile this, walk that” recipe for embedding the PGEN SystemVerilog parser. Read Build Recipe and Public API Surface for the long-form versions of each step.

See also: parseability_probe CLI Reference — canonical reference for the verification tool used in CI / bug-repro flows.

1. Cold-clone build

git clone https://github.com/richarddje/pgen.git
cd pgen
make -C rust SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash sv_stimuli_quality_gate

The gate produces the generated parser at rust/target/sv_stimuli_quality_gate/work/systemverilog_parser.rs and runs it against the stimuli corpus to verify behavior.

2. Wire the generated parser into your downstream Cargo build

# In your downstream project, before invoking cargo:
export PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_PATH=/absolute/path/to/pgen/rust/target/sv_stimuli_quality_gate/work/systemverilog_parser.rs

cargo build --release --features generated_parsers,sv_2017

rust/build.rs discovers the parser via that environment variable. Both relative-to-rust/ and absolute paths work; absolute paths are the safest.

3. Parse and walk

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use pgen::embedding_api::{parse_grammar_profile_named, ParseStatus};

let outcome = parse_grammar_profile_named(
    "systemverilog",
    "sv_2017",
    "module m; endmodule\n",
);

match outcome.status {
    ParseStatus::Success => {
        // Outcome's `diagnostic` is None on success.
        // For the AST dump, call `parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named`
        // (see Public API Surface).
    }
    ParseStatus::Failure => {
        eprintln!("parse failed: {:?}", outcome.diagnostic);
    }
}
}

For typed AST output, use parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named instead. The AST dump is the JSON shape this book documents per-rule.

4. Write the AST walker

See Walking the AST for the recommended walker pattern. The short version:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use serde_json::Value as JsonValue;

fn walk(node: &JsonValue) {
    match node {
        JsonValue::Object(obj) => {
            // Typed-shape node; dispatch on `type` / `kind` fields.
            // See per-rule chapters for the field set per rule.
        }
        JsonValue::Array(items) => {
            // Sequence / un-typed shape; walk children.
            for item in items {
                walk(item);
            }
        }
        JsonValue::String(_) => {
            // Terminal text — no children.
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}
}

5. Track the contract version

Pin your downstream code to the parser-release version recorded in docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md § “Contract Identity”. When you bump to a new PGEN version, scan the Changelog Index for shape-change rows that affect the rules you consume.

Build Recipe

The PGEN SystemVerilog parser is not in the default cargo test --features generated_parsers build. It is produced on-demand by the sv_stimuli_quality_gate make target (and similar gates) into rust/target/<gate>/work/systemverilog_parser.rs and discarded after the gate run.

This is intentional — the generated SV parser is a large file (~MB scale) and regenerating it on every cargo build would be costly. Downstream consumers receive the parser via one of three mechanisms:

  1. Run the gate locally, copy the generated file to a stable location, and point PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_PATH at it (this is the recommended path for downstream development).
  2. Vendor the generated file under your downstream project’s source tree and check it into your VCS, tracked against the parser-release version recorded in the contract.
  3. Run the gate in CI as part of your downstream build pipeline.

Cold-clone build

From a fresh clone of github.com/richarddje/pgen:

git clone https://github.com/richarddje/pgen.git
cd pgen
make -C rust SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash sv_stimuli_quality_gate

The gate:

  1. Reads grammars/systemverilog.ebnf (and the per-profile wrappers).
  2. Generates the parser via PGEN’s codegen.
  3. Writes the parser to rust/target/sv_stimuli_quality_gate/work/systemverilog_parser.rs.
  4. Compiles it.
  5. Runs the SV stimuli corpus against it.
  6. Validates AST shape contract (rust/test_data/ast_shape_contract/systemverilog_v1.json).

Pinning the generated parser

Once sv_stimuli_quality_gate succeeds, the parser at rust/target/sv_stimuli_quality_gate/work/systemverilog_parser.rs is the version that matches the current source tree’s grammar + codegen. To pin it:

cp rust/target/sv_stimuli_quality_gate/work/systemverilog_parser.rs \
   /your/vendoring/location/systemverilog_parser.rs
sha256sum /your/vendoring/location/systemverilog_parser.rs

Record the SHA256 in your downstream project’s manifest. When you bump the PGEN version, re-run the gate and verify the SHA changed only because of expected grammar/codegen changes (cross-reference Changelog Index for the parser-release version).

Wiring into a downstream Cargo build

PGEN’s rust/build.rs discovers the generated parser via PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_PATH. Set it before invoking cargo:

export PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_PATH=/absolute/path/to/systemverilog_parser.rs
cargo build --release --features generated_parsers,sv_2017

The path is resolved relative to rust/ if not absolute. Use absolute paths to avoid surprises. The build.rs will complain at compile time if the path doesn’t exist or doesn’t point at a valid generated parser file.

Cargo features

The PGEN crate exposes these features relevant to SV consumers:

  • generated_parsers — required to enable any generated parser backend.
  • sv_2017 — enable the IEEE 1800-2017 profile.
  • sv_2023 — enable the IEEE 1800-2023 profile.

Both profiles share the same grammars/systemverilog.ebnf source; the profile distinguishes which top-level entry rule the parser starts at.

Verifying the build

After cargo finishes, verify the parser is wired in:

cargo run --release --features generated_parsers,sv_2017 \
    --bin parseability_probe -- \
    --parse systemverilog /path/to/input.sv \
    --profile sv_2017

If the probe reports parse_full passed for grammar 'systemverilog' on '/path/to/input.sv', the integration is good.

See the parseability_probe CLI Reference for the full flag set (--parse-dump-ast, --parse-dump-ast-pretty, --max-bytes, --trace, --trace-log-file, etc.) and the supported grammar / profile matrix.

Build / availability requirements

Per the integration contract:

  • Downstream consumers should treat the generated backend as required for real host integration.
  • Startup should inspect parser_embedding_api_contract().supports_systemverilog_generated_backend to verify the backend is available.
  • Build-time generated-parser discovery is mediated by rust/build.rs, not by direct use of internal parser modules.
  • The standard-library bundle is in the binary (embedding API 2.1.0, ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.73): the std:: predefined classes (process, semaphore, mailbox) are preloaded from parser_libs/sv_<profile>_std/package/std.facts.json embedded at build time, so no directory has to travel with the binary. PGEN_PARSER_LIBS_DIR=<dir> overrides it; a directory named there without the bundle refuses the parse by name. Before 2.1.0 a moved tree silently parsed with no stdlib and rejected mailbox m;.

See docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md § “Build / Availability Requirements” for the full list.

Public API Surface

The stable downstream contract is the pgen::embedding_api host surface, not internal generated-parser types. This chapter enumerates the entry points downstream consumers should call.

All entry points return Outcome types (NamedGrammarParseOutcome, GrammarAstDumpOutcome, etc.) that carry an api_version, grammar, profile, status, and diagnostic/ast_dump payload. The Outcome types are stable and source-compatible across patch / minor releases.

Convenience entry points

Since embedding API 2.0.0 (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.112) these live beside the family that owns them — pgen::families::systemverilog::embed — because the neutral API names no language; each is one line over the generic entry points below.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use pgen::families::systemverilog::embed::*;

// Parse-only (no AST dump):
pub fn parse_systemverilog_2017(input: &str) -> NamedGrammarParseOutcome;
pub fn parse_systemverilog_2023(input: &str) -> NamedGrammarParseOutcome;

// Parse + AST dump (the version this book documents per-rule):
pub fn parse_systemverilog_2017_ast_dump(
    input: &str,
    options: &AstDumpOptions,
) -> NamedGrammarAstDumpOutcome;
pub fn parse_systemverilog_2023_ast_dump(
    input: &str,
    options: &AstDumpOptions,
) -> NamedGrammarAstDumpOutcome;
}

Generic entry points

For tools that select the grammar family at runtime. GrammarFamily and GrammarProfile are RESOLVED values since 2.0.0: GrammarFamily::from_str("systemverilog")? and family.profile("sv_2017")? (every spelling comes from the grammar’s own @profiles / @profile_alias); the 1.x enum variants are gone.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn parse_grammar_profile(
    grammar: GrammarFamily,
    profile: GrammarProfile,
    input: &str,
) -> GrammarParseOutcome;

pub fn parse_grammar_profile_result(
    grammar: GrammarFamily,
    profile: GrammarProfile,
    input: &str,
) -> Result<(), ParseDiagnostic>;

pub fn parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump(
    grammar: GrammarFamily,
    profile: GrammarProfile,
    input: &str,
    options: &AstDumpOptions,
) -> GrammarAstDumpOutcome;
}

String-name overloads

For embedders that select grammar / profile by string name (e.g. plugin systems, cross-language bindings):

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn parse_grammar_profile_named(
    grammar: &str,        // "systemverilog"
    profile: &str,        // "sv_2017" | "sv_2023" | "verilog_2005" | "sv_2023_tolerant" (opt-in, since 1.0.249)
    input: &str,
) -> NamedGrammarParseOutcome;

pub fn parse_grammar_profile_named_with_limits(
    grammar: &str,
    profile: &str,
    input: &str,
    limits: &ParseLimits,
) -> NamedGrammarParseOutcome;
}

AstDumpOptions

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct AstDumpOptions {
    pub pretty: bool,                 // pretty-print the JSON
    pub max_ast_bytes: Option<usize>, // truncation cap (bytes); None = no cap
}
}

ParseLimits

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct ParseLimits {
    pub max_input_bytes: Option<usize>,  // input-size cap; None = no cap
    // (other fields may be added in minor releases)
}

impl Default for ParseLimits {
    fn default() -> Self;
}
}

Outcome types

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct NamedGrammarParseOutcome {
    pub api_version: String,
    pub grammar: String,
    pub profile: String,
    pub status: ParseStatus,
    pub diagnostic: Option<ParseDiagnostic>,
}

pub struct NamedGrammarAstDumpOutcome {
    pub api_version: String,
    pub grammar: String,
    pub profile: String,
    pub status: ParseStatus,
    pub diagnostic: Option<ParseDiagnostic>,
    pub ast_dump: Option<AstDumpPayload>,
}

pub enum ParseStatus { Success, Failure }

pub struct ParseDiagnostic {
    pub code: String,        // e.g. "E_PARSE_FAILURE"
    pub message: String,
    // (other fields)
}
}

Stable diagnostics

These diagnostic codes are stable across patch / minor releases:

  • E_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE — the generated parser backend is not present in this build.
  • E_PARSE_FAILURE — the input failed to parse.
  • E_INPUT_TOO_LARGE — the input exceeds the configured max_input_bytes limit.
  • E_INVALID_LIMITS — the supplied ParseLimits are not valid.
  • E_INVALID_ARGUMENT — the supplied grammar / profile / input is not valid.
  • E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE — the supplied profile is not supported by the selected grammar family.

Backend availability check

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn parser_embedding_api_contract() -> ParserEmbeddingApiContract;

pub struct ParserEmbeddingApiContract {
    pub supports_systemverilog_generated_backend: bool,
    // (other fields)
}
}

Embedders should check this at startup and refuse to operate (or fall back gracefully) if the SV backend is unavailable.

Stack robustness (embedding API 1.3.1)

Every SystemVerilog embedding parse runs its generated-parser work on a dedicated 256 MiB-stack thread (one short-lived thread per call — concurrent host threads never serialize on a shared worker). This guarantees the engine’s 4096-frame recursion ceiling fires as a clean E_PARSE_FAILURE diagnostic before the OS guard page can abort the host process: measured pre-fix (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.8c.3, 2026-07-22), a ~400-deep parenthesized expression — ≈4 KB of text — was enough to SIGABRT a release embedder at the default 8 MB main stack, because the ceiling needs ≈8 MB of real stack in release (≈70 MB in debug) to be reachable. A parser-worker panic likewise surfaces as E_PARSE_FAILURE, never a host abort. Host code needs no change; the guarantee holds on any caller thread, including small worker-pool stacks.

Standard-library bundle (embedding API 2.1.0)

Every SystemVerilog parse begins by preloading the IEEE 1800 §G.2 predefined classes (process, semaphore, mailbox) as type_name facts, so mailbox m; resolves without user code declaring the class. Since 2.1.0 (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.73) the bundle is embedded in the binary from the tracked parser_libs/sv_{2017,2023}_std/package/std.facts.json; no run-time path is involved. PGEN_PARSER_LIBS_DIR=<dir> substitutes <dir>/sv_<profile>_std/package/std.facts.json, and a directory named there that lacks the bundle makes the parse fail with a ParseDiagnostic whose message names the knob, the bundle and the expected path — it never falls back to an empty stdlib. Before 2.1.0 the bundle was resolved from a compile-time absolute path and its absence was silent: 15.4--mailbox-{blocking,non-blocking}.sv (both must_accept) were rejected on a moved tree.

Source pointer

The authoritative source for the public API is rust/src/embedding_api.rs. The contract document rust/docs/EMBEDDING_API_CONTRACT.md describes the stability policy in full.

The Preprocess→Parse Pipeline

Real SystemVerilog is never parsed raw. A design or verification file is littered with compiler directives — `include pulls in package and macro headers, `define / `ifdef select what is live, and libraries such as UVM are built almost entirely out of macros — so the text the parser must judge is the text that exists after preprocessing. PGEN’s deliverable for SystemVerilog is therefore a pipeline, not a parser alone:

source file(s) ──► SystemVerilog PREPROCESSOR ──► expanded, directive-free text ──► SystemVerilog PARSER ──► AST
                   (macros · `include · `ifdef)          (+ a byte-indexed SOURCE MAP)              (+ verdict)

This chapter describes that pipeline as it ships: what each stage is, the compilation context you hand it, how to run the whole thing in one command, how a rejection is mapped back to the line you wrote, and what the pipeline can and cannot yet do. (The bare parser — a grammar generated from grammars/systemverilog.ebnf — is documented in the rest of this book; the preprocessor’s directive grammar has its own book, the SystemVerilog Preprocessor Parser reference, which is a different deliverable from the expansion stage described here.)

The two stages

StageWhat it doesWhere it livesIts own CLI
Preprocessor (expansion)object-like and function-like macros with defaults, `" stringize, `` token paste, nested expansion, `undef, `__FILE__ / `__LINE__; `include with a search path, cycle and depth guards; `ifdef / `ifndef / `elsif / `else / `endif; a byte-indexed source map, an event log and diagnosticsrust/src/families/systemverilog/preprocessor.rs (the family’s component, behind the engine’s preprocessing_stage)ast_pipeline INPUT.sv --preprocess systemverilog
Parserthe generated SystemVerilog parser, profile sv_2017 / sv_2023 / verilog_2005generated/systemverilog_parser.rsparseability_probe --parse systemverilog FILE

The two compose through one type: PreprocessedOutput { text, source_map, events, diagnostics, included_files }. The parser reads text; the source map is what turns a byte offset in that text back into file:line:column of the source.

The compilation context

A preprocessor without a context is a guess. Three things a real front end always knows are the context the pipeline takes, and each has the same spelling on both CLIs:

ContextFlag (both ast_pipeline --preprocess systemverilog and parseability_probe --preprocess)Meaning
include search path--include-dir DIR (repeatable, ordered)where `include "x.svh" is looked for after the including file’s own directory
predefined macros--symbol NAME / --symbol NAME=VALUE (repeatable, ordered; alias --define)seeded into the macro table before the first line is read, exactly as if `define NAME TEXT stood at the top of the unit; NAME alone defines it with empty text (the meaning a bare `define NAME line has). A predefine is an ordinary definition: `ifdef, `undef and the redefinition policy treat it as one
the compilation unit--unit-file F (repeatable, ordered)the files preprocessed before the input, under the same macro table; the input is the unit’s last file
a formal inside a plain "…" string--stage-opt plain_string_substitution=standard|paste_delimited|all (default standard)what a formal’s name inside a plain string literal in MACRO TEXT means: standard — the string is opaque, IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5.1’s own `define H(x) "Hello, x" prints Hello, x; paste_delimited — only a formal marked by paste tokens on both sides ("…[``i``]…", OpenTitan’s idiom) is substituted; all — every formal substituted and every paste joined (Icarus’s reading). The same spelling on ast_pipeline --preprocess-systemverilog
a backtick that survives expansion--stage-opt undefined_macro_policy=error|keep (default error)what the stage does with a backtick left in its OUTPUT outside a comment or string literal — an undefined macro, a function-like macro without its argument list, a stray `" token, a vendor directive, and since SVPP-EXPANSION.6h a backtick that begins no name at all (before white space, a line end, a digit, punctuation); an escaped identifier is one token the scan steps over, a backtick inside it included: error refuses it with its clause (SVPP-EXPANSION.6f: the parser’s raw-lane residue would otherwise accept a top-level one), keep hands it on as written for a consumer that resolves the rest itself. The SV stimuli quality gate’s generated-text stages (the closed loop’s two preprocess stages and the per-sample stage) run under keep by the contract’s preprocess.generated_text_undefined_macro_policy, because the raw lane’s opaque residue is text the generator may emit and no definition can resolve (SVPP-EXPANSION.6g); the hand-written realistic cases and every corpus lane keep error

The spellings are the neutral engine’s (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.113, 2026-09-29): the family’s own knobs travel as --stage-opt KEY=VALUE — ast_pipeline INPUT.sv --preprocess systemverilog --list-stage-options lists them: include_max_depth, include_path_policy, macro_redefine_policy, conditional_symbol_policy, conditional_expr_policy, plain_string_substitution, strict_warning_codes, undefined_macro_policy — and the pre-.113 spellings (--preprocess-systemverilog, --sv-include-dir, --sv-define, --sv-unit-file, --sv-keyword-profile, the --sv-*-policy flags, --sv-disallow-macro-redefine, the three --sv-*-json outputs) are accepted through release 1.0.247, each rewritten to the neutral form with one deprecation line on stderr, and removed after it.

The unit flag is not a convenience. IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5.1 says: “Once a text macro name has been defined, it can be used anywhere in the compilation unit where it is defined. There are no other scope restrictions once inside the compilation unit”, and §3.12.1 makes “all files on a given compilation command line” one compilation unit. A macro defined in the first file of a unit is in force in the last; the pipeline keeps ONE macro table across the list and produces one expansion per file. What `resetall does to that table is nothing — §22.3: “Directives that do not have a default (e.g., `define and `include) are not affected by `resetall.”

One command

# preprocess, then parse — in one process, no scratch file
./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart.sv \
    --profile sv_2017 --preprocess \
    --include-dir hw/ip/prim/rtl --include-dir stimuli/sv/uvm/uvm-core-2020.3.1/src \
    --symbol SYNTHESIS
# parse_full passed for grammar 'systemverilog' on 'hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart.sv' [preprocessed]

# the AST of the EXPANDED text, same flags
./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse-dump-ast-pretty systemverilog top.sv out.json \
    --profile sv_2017 --preprocess --symbol UVM

# a compilation unit: defines.svh first, then the input, one macro table
./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog dut.sv --profile sv_2017 \
    --preprocess --unit-file defines.svh

--preprocess is SystemVerilog-only (--preprocess with json is refused by name), and the three context flags are refused without it — a context with nothing to apply it to is a typo, not a no-op. The library flags compose unchanged: --lib-out on a package file and --lib-in on the file that imports it work exactly as they do without --preprocess, so a multi-file design is bootstrap files with --lib-out, then the top with --lib-in, each file preprocessed in its turn.

Three outcomes, three exit codes

ExitMeaningWhat you see
0preprocessed and acceptedparse_full passed … [preprocessed]
1preprocessed and rejected by the parserparse_full rejected … [furthest_position=N, …] [origin=FILE:LINE:COL]
3the preprocessor refused the input — the parser never ranpreprocess_failed for grammar 'systemverilog' on '…': … on stderr

The third code exists so a corpus lane can tell “the language did not accept this” from “the input could not even be expanded” — an unresolved `include, an unterminated `ifdef, an illegal `define. Those are different populations with different owners.

A rejection names the line you wrote

The parser reports positions in the text it parsed — the expanded text, which exists nowhere on disk. Under --preprocess the probe maps the deepest position any branch reached (furthest_position=, the diagnostic that locates a defect; see the debugging chapter of the platform book) back through the preprocessor’s source map and appends [origin=FILE:LINE:COL]:

# a syntax error inside an INCLUDED file names that file and its line
parse_full rejected sample … : Parser did not consume full input at position 12
    [furthest_position=42, +30 bytes deeper than surface position] [origin=inc/bad.svh:3:11]

# a syntax error inside a MACRO EXPANSION names the line of the macro's USE
parse_full rejected sample … : … [furthest_position=38, …] [origin=macro.sv:4:13]

The rule behind the second line: the preprocessor emits one source-map chunk per output line, and an expanded macro’s chunk records the line the macro was used on — the expansion has no line of its own. The column is a character column (a two-byte é before the position counts once). Paths are printed relative to the working directory when they sit under it. A position the map cannot place (an empty expansion) reads origin=unknown rather than nothing.

An opt-in summary line describes the expansion itself:

PGEN_REPORT_PREPROCESS=1 ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog f.sv --profile sv_2017 --preprocess
# preprocess: input='f.sv' unit_predecessors=0 include_dirs=0 symbols=0 output_bytes=37 source_map_entries=1 included_files=1 events=5 warnings=0

It is opt-in for the same reason the stack-probe line is: PGEN’s corpus runner captures the probe’s stderr as a per-file measurement column, and an unconditional line would edit a tracked artifact.

What the pipeline does today, measured

The pipeline lane (stimuli/run_pipeline_lane.sh, joined against the raw lane by stimuli/sv/pipeline_vs_raw.py; the tracked report is stimuli/sv/characterization/pipeline_characterization.md, whose identity block names the probe, grammar, parser, context and dumps every number below depends on) parses every source file of a corpus suite through the chain under a context DERIVED from the corpus itself (stimuli/sv/pipeline_context.py: for every `include an includer’s own directory does not satisfy, the one directory that does — any file of the tree, whatever its suffix, since .4d; a tie between copies of one text resolved per file to the nearest copy; an ambiguous name is reported, never guessed, and a directory the derivation would emit that also holds an ambiguous name is refused (a suite directory) or withheld for its includer (a per-file one), since .4d — and, since .4c.1, the defines a file’s own driver passes for it: verilator’s t_x.py flags and sv-tests’ :defines: header, a literal value only, applied per file as --symbol; a value the driver computes at run time and a file several variant drivers configure differently are reported, not guessed. These are the test’s own configuration, not a tool identity: .6b.3 measured and declined the identity predefines — and, since .4c.2, the unit predecessors a file’s own harness compiles before it, applied as --unit-file in order: verilator’s source-file arguments, slang’s .f command files, sv2v’s explicit multi-file runs; a -f list, a glob, a --siloed run and an ordering conflict are reported, not applied — and, since .6d.6, the predecessors a suite’s whole FLOW compiles before every file, hand-curated with their source: OpenTitan’s dvsim builds one compilation unit that starts with UVM and compiles dv_utils_pkg.sv and the RTL before any DV package, so uvm_macros.svh, dv_macros.svh, prim_assert.sv and, since .6d.7, cip_macros.svh precede every OpenTitan row; and, since .6d.8, VeeR’s generated configuration header snapshots/default/common_defines.vh — the first source its Makefile compiles (tools/Makefile:167, :210), which no VeeR file includes by name — precedes every VeeR row, with the two other entries of the Makefile’s defines list after it for fidelity). The first measurement, on the two suites the raw lane cannot judge at all (every one of their rows is deferred:chained_only in the raw answer key), release probe, sv_2017, 45 s wall:

suiterowsraw lane passpipeline passpipeline failpreprocessor refusedΔ pass
OpenTitan3 9838171 0732 88030+256
UVM 2020.3.1 (file by file)17433281460−5

Read the transitions, not the delta. On OpenTitan 328 rows went fail → pass — RTL and DV files whose only barrier was a macro or an `include — and 69 went pass → fail; all 69 are hollow raw passes: the raw parse had accepted a file that only includes others because the directive is opaque to it, and the pipeline pulled the included text in and judged it (its rejection lands in the included file, not in the row’s own). The same holds for UVM’s six. Not one pass → fail lands in the row’s own file.

The 30 preprocessor refusals are the context, not the engine: 29 are `includes of a name that exists under several top_* variants or nowhere in the tree (a per-file context only a build system’s .core file supplies), and 1 is `include `REQUESTS_FILE — refused at that time by a ruling that read §22.4’s Syntax 22-1 ("filename" and <filename>) and not §22.5.1, which says in a sentence that “the `include directive can be followed by a macro, instead of a string literal”. The ruling was wrong and is retracted (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(m), 2026-10-02): the macro is now expanded first and what it yields is read as the filename. The engine’s own refusals in the first run of this lane — a `define whose formal list spans lines, a conditional directive inside a macro body used mid-line, `ifdef X // comment reading the comment as part of the symbol — were fixed the same day (SVPP-EXPANSION.5), and the re-run moved exactly the rows they had blocked: five refusals became parser verdicts and four rejections became accepts, none the other way.

What the rejections sit on once the macro barrier is gone. The origin line of every remaining rejection, read from the tree and bucketed by construct:

Every suite of the 16 336-row corpus through the chain (sv_2017; measured on the debug probe with a 600 s per-file deadline, 432 s wall — see the note on the host below — where the first reading used the release probe at 60 s and 155 s wall), each suite under its derived context — a name that exists under several directories resolved per file to the includer’s nearest candidate, a tie reported:
