The raw lane’s 5 693 match rows stay green through the pipeline (5 693 of 6 064 match rows pass; the 370 that do not are must_reject rows correctly rejected, and one refused). Of the 278 refusals, 170 are black-parrot’s: its sources include headers its build system generates and the vendored tree does not carry — a permanent gap of the corpus, not of the engine — and 32 are friscv’s hardfloat test includes of the same kind. Two raw passes became rejections in the row’s own file — a fragment whose whole expansion is a `__FILE__ string, and one owed — and 19 fixtures now refuse at the preprocess stage rather than reaching the parser: the :should_fail_because: chapter-22 tests, verilator’s _bad and sv2v’s error/ fixtures and the Surelog IncludeAndMacros tops, whose mode.vh transcribes the standard’s own “illegal, only one argument” line. Six of those had been passing in both lanes (an intended-fail fixture the parser accepted because the preprocessor bound a missing actual to nothing); the three 60 s timeouts of the first reading (a macro naming itself twice, expanded exponentially) are refusals in milliseconds; and four OpenTitan coverage interfaces are recognised that were not, because their `DV_FCOV_INSTANTIATE_CG had been mis-expanded for six months (below).

What the preprocessor refuses, and why. Since SVPP-EXPANSION.5(g)(h) the expansion stage raises its own errors — the single command reports them as preprocess_failed (exit 3) at the ORIGIN file and line, each carrying the standard’s sentence:

  • E_SVPP_MISSING_MACRO_ARGUMENT — the actual list is shorter than the formals and a formal it leaves unbound has no default (IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5.1: “… error if any of the remaining formal arguments does not have a default specified”; its example `MACRO1 ( 1 ) // ILLEGAL: b and c omitted, no default for c). An EMPTY actual is a different thing and stays legal: present and blank, it is “replaced by nothing” (`MACRO1 ( , 2, )) or takes the default.
  • E_SVPP_EXTRA_MACRO_ARGUMENT — more actuals than formals (“It shall be an error to specify more actual arguments than the number of formal arguments”; `D(,,)).
  • E_SVPP_RECURSIVE_MACRO — a macro expands, directly or through others, to a usage of itself; the message names the chain (`TOP -> `BOTTOM1 -> `BOTTOM -> `TOP). The standard’s exception — “an actual argument to a macro or a default may contain a usage of itself” — is decided by who wrote the usage: every byte of an expansion carries whether the caller wrote it (a source line, or text that came in through an actual or a default) or a macro body produced it. A caller-written usage starts its own expansion context; a body-produced one is checked against the stack of bodies being rescanned. That distinction is what lets OpenTitan nest a `DV_SPINWAIT inside the actual of another (its inner body re-enters a macro the outer expansion still holds) while `define A(x) `B(`A(x)) is still refused: the `A handed to B is A’s own body text.

What the expansion stage rewrites, and what it leaves. Four rules landed with SVPP-EXPANSION.6b.2, each one a sentence of the standard that a corpus row had been failing on:

  • A one-line comment in macro text is not substituted (§22.5.1: “the comment shall not become part of the substituted text”). `define N 21 */* foo */2//foo expands to 21 */* foo */2 — the block comment stays, it is white space to the parser; a string keeps its slashes; a continued line keeps its continuation even when the comment sat on it.

  • Nor is a one-line comment written inside an ACTUAL (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(l), 2026-10-02 — the same sentence, read of the text that gets substituted). `M(a == b // why, exactly<newline>) used to expand to if (!(a == b // why, exactly)) …: the comma inside the comment correctly did not split the argument, but the comment’s text was carried onto the expansion’s single line and commented out the rest of the call — silently (diagnostics=0). Now the comment is dropped up to its line feed when the actual is bound; a block comment stays, and a // inside a string literal is the string’s. OpenTitan writes this in its `DV_CHECK_RANDOMIZE_WITH_FATAL(req, … // TODO … ) calls and in RTL assertion macros: four corpus rows moved fail → pass under the pipeline and none the other way.

  • The paste token joins its sides in an object macro too (§22.5.1: *“A delimits lexical tokens without introducing white space"*): `define YUCK /* garbage */ `` expands to a comment, as a function macro’s substitution always did. In a source line the token stays for the parser to judge.

  • A well-formed `line directive is consumed (§22.12: *“the line directive shall set the line number and file name of the following line"*). The expansion stage is the tool that maintains the current file and line, so `` FILE and __LINE__ `` after it read the assigned location, the event log records the directive (line_directive), and the parser never sees it. A malformed one — a level other than 0, 1 or 2, a missing parameter, a comment on its line — is not this stage's to consume: it passes through, and the parser's own §22.12 production refuses it, so the answer key's must-reject rows on malformed `` line lines keep their verdict under the pipeline. Its parameters may be MACRO USAGES — line new_line_num foo(line) 1 `` — and are expanded first (IEEE 1800-2023 §22.2: *"Macro expansion shall occur within a compiler directive"*; 1800-2017 §22.5.1: a defined text macro *"can be used anywhere in the compilation unit where it is defined"*); the directive is consumed when what they yield is well-formed, and reads exactly as the literal form does (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(n); before, the macros were expanded on a pass-through line and a raw `` line `` reached the parser, which has no production for it inside a procedural block).

  • A comment between the formals of a `define is refused, and the refusal names the clause. §22.5.1 (both editions): “The formal argument names shall be simple_identifiers, separated by commas and optionally white space”; §5.3’s white space is spaces, tabs, newlines and formfeeds, and the standard writes “white space or a comment” where it admits one (§22.4, on the `include line). No sentence of either edition admits a comment there, so `define ARGPAR(a, /* c */ b) and a // after a formal are refused (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(o)); a NEWLINE between formals is white space and is accepted. Three corpus files write the comment form — counted by the lane itself, the rows whose refusal carries this reason — and all three are tool test suites probing the edge: verilator t_preproc.v:277 (its own comment reads “comments MIGHT not be legal”), iverilog macro_with_args.v:17 and sv2v macro_arg_comment.sv:1. No design file in the corpus writes it, so no opt-in tolerance is offered for it.

  • Three readings follow the EDITION of the profile the text will be parsed under (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(p); --profile sv_2023 and sv_2023_tolerant select IEEE 1800-2023, every other profile and the unprofiled reading select 1800-2017). They are the three places where 1800-2023’s clause 22 says more than 1800-2017’s:

    textunder the 2017 readingunder the 2023 readingthe sentence
    a block comment in macro text — `define Y(a) a /* c */ + 1the comment is part of the substituted textthe comment is NOT substituted (one space stands where it was)1800-2023 §22.5.1: “If a one-line comment or block comment (see 5.4) is included in the text, then the comment shall not become part of the substituted text”; 1800-2017 says it of one-line comments only
    a block comment that the macro text opens and the NEXT line closes — `define X 1 /* multi / line */ + 2REFUSED, naming the clause: the newline ended the macro text inside a comment (“shall not be split across … Comments”)the comment carries the `define across its newlines; X is 1 + 21800-2023 §22.5.1: “A newline character that is not contained in a triple-quoted string literal or in a block comment and is not preceded by a backslash shall end the macro text”
    a macro USAGE as the argument of `ifdef / `ifndef / `elsif / `undef — `ifndef `ID(HAVE)the argument is read as written (Syntax 22-6 takes a text_macro_identifier)the usage is expanded first and the directive reads what it yields1800-2023 §22.2: “Macro expansion shall occur within a compiler directive”
    a backslash-newline INSIDE a string literal of the macro text — `define MSG "two \ / lines"the continuation becomes a newline inside the literal, which the parser then rejects as a two-line string (§5.9) — the 2017 text has no exceptionboth the backslash and the newline are omitted: the literal reads "two lines"1800-2023 §22.5.1: “An exception to the previous sentence is that if the backslash-newline character sequence occurs in the middle of a string literal, both the backslash and the newline characters are omitted in the expanded macro” (docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-22-compiler-directives.md:182-184; SVPP-EXPANSION.5(u))

    The 2017 column is the strict reading of that edition, not a guess at tool behaviour: where the older text has no sentence the newer one adds, the older reading stays as it was. Each of the first two rows that changes a verdict is pinned as an edition twin — one file accepted under sv_2023, its byte twin rejected under sv_2017.

  • Include nesting is bounded by DEPTH, not by a file’s reappearance (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(q); §22.4: “The number of nesting levels for include files shall be finite. Implementations may limit the maximum number of levels to which include files can be nested, but the limit shall be at least 15”). A file that includes itself under a guard (`ifndef INCLUDED / `define INCLUDED / `include "self.sv" / `else …) nests once and is finite — sv2v’s file_line.sv and include_self.sv write that shape — and is read; an unguarded loop is refused when it passes the stage’s limit of 64 levels, and the refusal cites §22.4 and shows the chain’s last steps. Through 1.0.250 any file already on the include stack was refused as an “include cycle”, guarded or not.

  • An escaped identifier is a macro name (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(q); 1800-2017 Syntax 22-2’s text_macro_identifier is an identifier, which A.9.3 makes simple OR escaped; 1800-2023 §22.5.1 says it outright and gives `define \M@CRO3 (a=5, b=0, c="C") … / `\M@CRO3 ( 1 ) as its example). The name is read without its backslash — §5.6.1: “an escaped identifier \cpu3 is treated the same as a nonescaped identifier cpu3” — so `define \escaped is used as `escaped or `\escaped; one terminating white-space character is consumed, so a ( right after it opens the formal list (1800-2023: “only the single white space character terminating the identifier name … shall separate the opening parenthesis from the macro name”); a usage spelled with the backslash is recognised where the run up to white space IS a defined name, so the escaped-quote token `\`" of a macro string keeps its meaning. Through 1.0.250 such a `define was refused as “missing macro name” (iverilog escaped_macro_name.v).

  • A one-line comment inside macro text continues the text when its line ends in backslash-newline, and the comment is dropped — 1800-2023 §22.5.1 says it outright (“If a one-line comment is followed by a backslash and newline character, the comment ends before the backslash and the macro text continues on the next line”), and the 2017 text’s two sentences read together say the same; measured licensed under both profiles and pinned (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(r)). A backslash followed by white space before the newline does NOT continue the macro text on any profile: 2017 “preceded by a backslash”, 2023 “immediately preceded” — the macro ends at that line and the following lines are source. The corpus writes that shape at two sites, both tests (verilator’s own BSSPACE lint-error test is one); no stage option exists for it.

  • Macro text may not leave a string literal open (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(s); §22.5.1 “The text specified for macro text shall not be split across the following lexical tokens: Comments, Numbers, String literals, Identifiers, Keywords, Operators”, with the standard’s own illegal example `define first_half "start of string). The definition is refused, naming the clause; through 1.0.250 it was accepted and the use site glued one string. The scan is the stage’s own (comments and `"…`" macro strings skipped, \" an escape, a backslash-newline inside a string a continuation); a text cut at the end of a number, identifier, keyword or operator is not judged — a stated bound. A formal’s default argument may hold (, ) or , inside a string literal (.5(v)); the list closes at the parenthesis outside every string.

  • A compiler directive cannot be redefined as a macro name, and is a defined name (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(t); §22.5.1 “All compiler directives shall be considered predefined macro names; it shall be illegal to redefine a compiler directive as a macro name”). `define define "illegal" and `define include 1 are refused; `ifdef __FILE__ is true and `ifndef __FILE__ false, so a guarded redefinition is skipped (the ispras 22.13 test’s shape). The set is the edition’s own: IEEE 1364-2005 clause 19 lists nineteen directives; IEEE 1800 adds undefineall (§22.5.3) and __FILE__ / __LINE__ (§22.13), so under the verilog_2005 profile those three are ordinary macro names. Through 1.0.250 both were accepted and a directive name was undefined to the conditionals.

  • A backtick that survives expansion is refused, not handed to the parser (SVPP-EXPANSION.6f). The stage’s post-condition: outside a comment or a string literal, the expanded text carries no backtick except a directive the parser reads. An undefined name is refused as “neither a defined macro nor a compiler directive” (§22.5.1 gives a usage its meaning by substitution — no definition, no derivation; a vendor’s own directive falls under the same sentence), a function-like macro used bare or with an argument list the file never closes under “the parentheses are always required in the macro call” and Syntax 22-3, a `" / `\`" / outside macro text as no token of the language, and an end_keywords `` that closes no region under 1364-2005 §19.11 *"must be paired"*. Through 1.0.250the stage kept the leftover as written and the SV grammar'scompiler_directiveresidue — the RAW lane's design, an opaque backtick line accepted so an unexpanded file parses around its macro uses — accepted a top-level one: 38 pipeline rows readpassover text the stage never resolved (25 of them riscv-dv instruction files whose macros live in a package the lane refuses), and 318 failing rows carried one too.–stage-opt undefined_macro_policy=keep restores the passthrough — and the closed loop replays GENERATED raw-lane text under it by contract (SVPP-EXPANSION.6g`, 2026-10-08): the raw lane’s residue is what the generator derives, and refusing it there asked the stage to resolve what no definition can.

  • A backtick is a token only before a name (SVPP-EXPANSION.6h, 2026-10-08): §22.2 *“All compiler directives are preceded by the () character"* and Syntax 22-3 text_macro_usage ::= text_macro_identifier … give the character meaning before a directive name or a macro name and nowhere else — a backtick before white space, a line end, the end of the text, a digit or a punctuation character is refused, naming what follows it. Through 1.0.251 the scan tested only an identifier or a macro-string successor, so `, `+ and `9 reached the parser and the raw lane’s opaque residue accepted them. Two neighbours landed with it: an escaped identifier (§5.6.1, a backslash to white space, any printable character) is ONE token the scan steps over — wire \a`b ; had been refused as a usage of `b — and an escaped usage `\name is looked up by its name (\esc and esc are one macro), so an undefined one carries the undefined-name clause rather than the macro-string one. Measured on the corpus by an expanded-text census of every lane row before the change and by the three readings after it: no row moved.

  • A function-like macro may open its parentheses on the next line (§22.5.1 requires the parentheses; §5.3 lets white space, newlines included, separate the tokens): `FOO at the end of a line followed by (1, 2) on the next is one invocation.

Four more landed with SVPP-EXPANSION.6b.5, each named by a row of the disposition table:

  • $display is one token. A formal named display is not substituted inside the system task name (A.9.3 system_tf_identifier): `define MACRO_D(display) $display(display); expands to $display("hi"), not $"hi"("hi").
  • A block comment opened on an earlier line is comment text (§5.4), whatever it contains: a `else inside it is not a directive, and the text after an `include filename belongs to the next logical line, so a /* multi-line opened there keeps its close.
  • The coverage-control macros are predefined — IEEE 1800-2017 §40.3.1 says the tool defines `SV_COV_START … `SV_COV_PARTIAL (fifteen names, the clause’s values); a source `define of the same name supersedes.
  • A §34 protected envelope is consumed as opaque. From the `pragma protect line that carries begin_protected to the one that carries end_protected, every line is the envelope’s — key blocks, data blocks, their encoded payload — and none of it reaches the parser; the pragma lines outside the envelope pass through as before. An envelope with no end_protected is refused.

The same slice found a defect no parser could see: the formal-list scanner treated an apostrophe as a string quote — SystemVerilog has none (§5.9) — so `define DV_FCOV_INSTANTIATE_CG(NAME_, COND_ = 1'b1, ARGS_ = ()) had been read as two formals since the scanner’s first commit, a third actual dropped without a word and newARGS_ `` pasted into the legal identifier newARGS_. Only a rule that refuses (extra actuals) made it visible; the fix moved four OpenTitan files to pass.

The order around a paste (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(i)). A `` token “delimits lexical tokens without introducing white space, allowing identifiers to be constructed” (§22.5.1), and the identifier being constructed is very often a macro name: UVM’s `uvm_pack_TYPE(ARG, p) , OpenTitan’s `dv_SEV_(…) , Surelog's ```rname_ADR . Two rules decide what such a chain means, and both are Verilator’s measured readings (its own t_preproc.v goldens) and sv2v’s:

  • An operand that is a defined macro usage is expanded before the join. `AbC `` with `` `A `` = `a` and `` `C `` = `c` is `abc`; `` XXS_SOME with SOME `` = someisXXS_some; `` XTYPE_frame with `XTYPE = sonet is the identifier sonet_frame — and stays one even when a macro named sonet_frame exists, because the joined text is not looked up again.
  • An undefined usage joined by a paste is looked up as the whole constructed name, in place. `QAb with no `QA` and a `QA_b` is QA_b ``'s expansion; `` CHOICEFOO```SUFFIX with `SUFFIX = _MAGIC is `CHOICE_FOO_MAGIC’s — not `CHOICE_FOO followed by _MAGIC, which is what the engine produced until this slice (1_MAGIC, a token no parser accepts) because the substitution step had deleted the pastes before the rescan could see what they joined. A constructed function-like usage collects its argument list as written, so an actual’s own macro usage is still expanded “only after substitution into the outer macro text”, the order §22.5.1 gives every actual.

The reference is sv2v’s test/lex/macro_macro.sv, whose own macro_macro.v expects $display(3, 4):

`define SUFFIX _MAGIC
`define CHOICE_FOO 1
`define CHOICE_FOO_MAGIC 3
`define MACRO2(A, B) `CHOICE_``A```SUFFIX , `CHOICE_``B```SUFFIX
$display(`MACRO2(FOO, BAR));     // 3 , 4 — Verilator 5.050 and sv2v; the engine read 1_MAGIC , 2_MAGIC

⚠️ The tools do not all agree here, and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over: Icarus 13.0 reads 1_MAGIC (it looks the left side up as soon as it is joined) and, for a base name that is itself a defined macro, my_prefix_my_suffix where Verilator reads `PREFIX_my_suffix. The standard’s own sentence — a paste constructs an identifier — is the whole-name reading, which is also the one sv2v’s reference and Verilator’s goldens take, so it is the one shipped. Over the corpus the change moved exactly one expansion of the 188 files that carry a paste at all, the sv2v row above; the record, with the three-way comparison against both tools re-runnable (docs/tasks/artifacts/svpp_expansion/paste_order/probe.sh), is in docs/tasks/SVPP-EXPANSION.md. What that comparison also shows, and what is deliberately not decided by this rule: a macro usage substituted into a `"…`" string region is not expanded here while both tools expand it, and a formal inside a plain "…" string is substituted here (as Icarus does) while Verilator keeps the string verbatim — SVPP-EXPANSION.5(j) and (k), owned, next.

The string region (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(j)). §22.5.1 says what a `"…`" region is in one sentence: “the expansion shall include the quotation mark, substitution of actual arguments, and expansions of embedded macros” — three things. The engine did the first two, on one of its two paths: the renderer lived in the function-macro substitution step, so an OBJECT macro’s region was never rendered at all (OpenTitan’s `define SSCTRL_PATH `"`SSCTRL_HPATH`" reached the parser with its markers on and was refused inside {SSCTRL_PATH, “.”, signal}), and a usage embedded in a region — through an actual (`` stringify(name1) ``) or in the body (`` “SSCTRL_HPATH” ) — was never expanded because the rescan does not enter a string. The escaped quote \“ was mis-rendered too: the close scan matched its last two bytes, so the clause's own define msg(x,y) “x: \“y\”" `` came out as “left side: \"right side"”where the clause prints“left side: "right side"”`. One renderer now does all three, in the rescan, for both paths, and it applies to expansion text only:

`define SSCTRL_HPATH tb.dut.u_otbn_core.u_otbn_start_stop_control
`define SSCTRL_PATH  `"`SSCTRL_HPATH`"
return {`SSCTRL_PATH, ".", signal};   // {"tb.dut.u_otbn_core.u_otbn_start_stop_control", ".", signal}
`define msg(x,y) `"x: `\`"y`\`"`"
$display(`msg(left side,right side));  // $display("left side: \"right side\"");  — the clause's example
$display(`"standalone`");              // unchanged: the form is defined for macro text (sv2v string_macro.sv:9 is
                                       //   pinned must-reject on it); Verilator renders it, Icarus leaves it

An undefined usage inside a region, or a function-like one with no argument list, stays as written, backtick and all (Surelog’s own golden for its PreprocString test keeps the bare `message). A rendered literal is ONE line (§5.9): an embedded macro whose body spans lines — OpenTitan’s `DV_LC_TX_DIST inside a stringified `DV_CHECK_STD_RANDOMIZE_WITH_FATAL condition — has each newline rendered as a space, which is Verilator’s reading (its twoline golden "first second") and the only one a parser can read; Icarus leaves the raw newline, and so did this engine for a multi-line actual until now. With the region rendered, an empty argument list () inside one is read as the clause’s “An actual argument may be empty … substituted by … nothing if no default is specified” — one empty actual when the macro declares formals — where the engine had counted zero actuals and refused `thru() as missing (.5(j′)); both tools read it empty. Over the corpus the change moved 20 of the 483 expansions that carry a region and 7 of the 107 that carry an empty invocation — every one a rendering, three OpenTitan sequence files and four OpenTitan testbenches now carrying real hierarchical paths inside their strings, and exactly one verdict: the OpenTitan interface row above. What sv2v’s macro.sv does — closing a region with a bare " — is sv2v’s extension (Verilator refuses the file, the clause says a " “must have a terminating “”) and is left as written; the row is a pinned must-reject either way. The three-way comparison is re-runnable (docs/tasks/artifacts/svpp_expansion/string_region/probe.sh).

A plain string in macro text is opaque (SVPP-EXPANSION.5(k)). The same clause that defines the `" form says of a plain one: *“the use of “ always starts a string literal and must have a terminating “. Any characters embedded inside this string literal, including ", become part of the string in the replaced macro text"* — and its own worked example is `` define H(x) “Hello, x” , which *"will print: Hello, x"*. The engine had been substituting a formal there, which is Icarus's reading and which MANGLES a message whose prose happens to be a formal's name — the census read 66 such sites against 6 that rely on it: iverilog's define check(value, expected, error) `` printed “ 8’h5 %0h, got %0h“for“ expected %0h, got %0h“, OpenTitan's pwrmgr_base_vseq.svprinted“in %0d fast clock cycles_before_rst_lc_src”, UVM's field macros warned about “UVM_ALL_ON|UVM_HEX”instead of“FLAG”`. The six that rely on substitution are design code written for commercial simulators — OpenTitan’s "tb.dut.gen_classes[i].u_accu.u_prim_count.cnt_q[0]" , where the paste tokens MARK the formal — so the two tool readings are the named values of one policy, with the standard’s as the default:

--stage-opt plain_string_substitution=standard          "Hello, x"                         (the clause; Verilator 5.050)
--stage-opt plain_string_substitution=paste_delimited   "tb.dut.gen_classes[0]…" — only a ``formal`` is substituted, prose stays
--stage-opt plain_string_substitution=all               every formal substituted, every paste joined (Icarus 13.0)

Over the corpus the default moved 67 of 16 388 expansions and every changed line sits inside a plain string; the paste-order probe now agrees with Verilator on all fourteen of its rows. ⚠️ A consumer feeding OpenTitan-style DV code names paste_delimited; nobody is served by all except a reproduction of Icarus, which is why it is spelled out rather than left as an unnamed default.

`begin_keywords regions are rendered, not ignored (SVPP-EXPANSION.8). IEEE 1800-2017 §22.14 lets a block of source select which identifiers are reserved as keywords, from a version of IEEE 1364 or IEEE 1800: inside `begin_keywords "1364-2001" … `end_keywords, logic is an ordinary name. A generated parser reserves one set per PROFILE and cannot switch mid-file, so the expansion stage renders the difference as TEXT — every token the parse profile reserves and the region’s version does not is re-emitted as an ESCAPED identifier:

`begin_keywords "1364-2001"     // the source, as its author wrote it
module top;
  reg [63:0] logic;             // OK: `logic` is not a keyword in 1364-2001
endmodule
`end_keywords

`begin_keywords "1364-2001"     // what the parser is handed
module top;
  reg [63:0] \logic ;           // §5.6.2: "A SystemVerilog keyword preceded by an escape
endmodule                       //  character is not interpreted as a keyword"
`end_keywords

§5.6.1 makes the two spellings the same identifier (“an escaped identifier \cpu3 is treated the same as a nonescaped identifier cpu3”), so nothing about the design changes — only which words the parser may bind as names. What decides the rendering:

  • The profile. --profile reaches this stage on both commands (ast_pipeline --preprocess systemverilog --profile P; --sv-keyword-profile accepted through 1.0.247); under verilog_2005 the parser never reserved logic, so the same region renders nothing. Omitted, the parser’s unprofiled reading is used, which reserves IEEE 1800-2017 Table B.1.
  • The version tables are the LRM’s own — Table 22-1 … Table 22-6 and §22.14.4’s “1364-2001-noconfig” exclusion list — derived from the in-repo standard text and held equal to it on every commit by the SV-KEYWORD-VERSIONS doctrine, never typed by hand.
  • Regions nest (“Each nested pair is stacked”) and run “even across source code file boundaries, until the matching `end_keywords directive or the end of the compilation unit”, so the stack is carried between the files of a --unit-file unit exactly as the macro table is. sv2v’s test/lex/begin_keywords.sv turns on exactly this: inside a "1364-2005" region nested in a "1364-1995" one, task automatic bar; keeps automatic as a keyword while logic becomes a name.
  • It is lexical. A keyword named in a comment, a string literal, a numeric literal, a $-name or an escaped identifier is not a token of the design and is left exactly as written; the source map is re-indexed by the exact byte delta of each rendering, so a rejection still names the line its author wrote.
  • What it cannot do it reports. Text can unreserve a keyword; it cannot reserve a non-keyword. A region naming a version that reserves MORE than the profile raises W_SVPP_KEYWORDS_VERSION_ABOVE_PROFILE and is applied only in the direction text can express; one naming a specifier the profile’s own edition does not define raises W_SVPP_KEYWORDS_VERSION_NOT_IN_EDITION (the parser then refuses the directive); an unpaired `end_keywords raises W_SVPP_UNMATCHED_END_KEYWORDS; and a specifier no version of the standard defines is E_SVPP_UNKNOWN_KEYWORDS_VERSION — §22.14’s own “It shall be an error if an implementation does not recognize the version_specifier”.

The event log records each directive (keywords_region) with its specifier, how many words the region unreserves and how many tokens it actually rendered.

The deferred population, re-read. The raw answer key is honest about what a one-file parse cannot decide: a must-accept file whose raw parse stops on a macro use, a conditional or an `include is explained by a position test, and a multi-file design file carries no verdict at all. The tracked stimuli/sv/characterization/pipeline_readjudication.md (with its per-row .tsv; SVPP-EXPANSION.6a) joins those rows with what the pipeline actually did to them. Of the 1 434 explained-away must-accept rows, 1 199 parse once preprocessed — the explanation held and the row now testifies for the parser — while 223 still fail in their own text: the explanation was wrong, and each is a defect candidate awaiting a disposition (103 of them are a class header whose base class lives in uvm_pkg). Of the 4 927 chained-only rows, 1 530 are accepted under their derived context, 2 936 still reject in their own file (1 924 on a class … extends header whose base is declared elsewhere — the cross-file fact the library flags exist for), 236 land in an included file and 225 are refused. A chained: outcome is not yet a match: the answer key holds no expected verdict for those rows, and one is derived from the suite’s own convention before the coverage tuple moves. A refuted row keeps that label until someone has looked at it and written down what it is: the tracked stimuli/sv/characterization/refuted_dispositions.tsv carries one line per row looked at — the disposition and its evidence, in the answer key’s own style — and the report splits the refuted rows by it. The dispositions are a closed vocabulary: the base class lives in another file (the library design’s rows), the file’s portable branch is a vendor’s own error stub behind its identity macro, a macro the suite’s driver defines on its command line, a macro a predecessor file of the unit defines, a parser question routed to the corpus tree (legal-looking text the parser refuses, with the clause), a key question (the parser is right to refuse and the row’s expectation is what needs a ruling), an expansion-stage rule not yet implemented. A disposition for a row that has since moved is refused, so the table cannot carry a stale claim. Every refuted row carries one; the report’s refuted_awaiting_disposition is the count still to be looked at.

The rows the raw key deferred to this lane by design (.6c.3, 2026-10-06). The raw answer key files a sv-tests test whose header says :type: preprocessing as deferred:svpp_owned — “conformance owned by the preprocessor lane” — and the preprocess→parse lane IS that lane. Its re-adjudication now reads those rows’ expectation the way the raw key reads every other sv-tests row, through the key’s own function in its pipeline mode: a :should_fail_because: header means must_reject, its absence means must_accept. Of the 94 such rows on the 2026-10-06 reading, 86 positive tests parse once preprocessed (svpp_owned: corroborated), 4 should-fail tests are refused by the preprocessor with a clause-cited code (E_SVPP_*: the rejection the header expects, at the expansion stage), 2 are rejected in their own text as expected — and 2 should-fail tests the pipeline ACCEPTS: the standard’s own illegal example of a macro text split across a string literal (22.5.1--define-expansion_21.sv, §22.5.1 “shall not be split across the following lexical tokens: … String literals”) and the redefinition of a compiler directive as a macro name (22.5.1--define-expansion_23.sv, `define define "illegal", §22.5.1 “it shall be illegal to redefine a compiler directive as a macro name”). Both were over-acceptances of the preprocessor, on the bar under the pipeline (its fifth number read 2) until SVPP-EXPANSION.5(s) and (t) landed the same day: both tests are now refused at the expansion stage with the clause, the bar reads 0, and the two rows testify as must_reject:refused_engine. Since .6c.4 verilator’s and sv2v’s svpp-owned rows are judged the same way, through the key’s own functions in a pipeline mode: verilator’s driver rule with the preprocessor’s error vocabulary read off its goldens (fails=True + a preprocessor- or parse-stage golden → must_reject; a lint-only golden → must_accept; a -E driver’s success → the preprocessor must not refuse, and the parse of the expanded text is no claim), sv2v’s error/ as must_reject by contract — 27 more rows testify, two carry a key_question disposition (an 1800-2023 keyword specifier under the 2017 reading), and the only svpp-owned rows still without a verdict are two accepted (Surelog’s PreProcMacro, sv2v’s `define MACRO() — an empty formal list the standard does not derive and every tool accepts, recorded as a tolerance candidate), seven fragments and 31 refusals with no convention to read. The other suites’ svpp-owned rows (22 accepted, 28 rejected, 25 refused) have no header convention derived yet and keep no verdict.

The file’s own configuration (.4c.1). A test suite’s driver does not run a file bare: verilator’s t_x.py passes +define+NAME[=VALUE] / -DNAME[=VALUE], sv-tests’ header carries :defines:. The derived context now includes them per file (stimuli/sv/pipeline_context_defines.tsv, 55 rows on 48 files: 52 verilator, 3 sv-tests — a name the same command line -Us again is not one of them), applied as --symbol before the suite’s rows. The deriver emits a LITERAL value only and reports the rest instead of guessing — 3 files whose driver computes the value at run time ("+define+SIM_CYCLES=" + str(test.cycles)), 24 files that several variant drivers configure differently (t_time_sc_ns.py … t_time_sc_sec.py), and it skips the spans whose -D reaches the C++ compiler or iverilog (-CFLAGS, make_flags=[CPPFLAGS_ADD=…], iv_flags) and the *_common.py helpers that are not drivers — the first, permissive scan had emitted 94 rows, 38 of them C++ defines or a helper’s conditional flags; the strict scan emits 56. Re-run on the whole lane, exactly 5 rows moved, all among the files with defines: 3 fail → pass (sv-tests preprocessor-macro_0/1.sv under TEST_VAR / VAR_1=2 VAR_2=5, verilator t_assert_inside_cond.v under T_ASSERT_INSIDE_COND) and 2 pass → fail. 🔎 A driver’s define can select a vendor-extension branch: t_vpi_module.v and t_vpi_public_depth.v are standard SystemVerilog only WITHOUT their driver’s +define+USE_DOLLAR_C32 — with it, the selected branch is `systemc_header / extern "C" int mon_check(); / `verilog, Verilator’s directives (not among clause 22’s) around C++ text no production derives; the row is right to reject under its own configuration and is pinned must_reject with a reproducer/control measured on both profiles, as is t_gen_missing.v, whose define selects the branch above its `error stub and exposes a bare begin … end inside a generate region (the .3.56 ruling, A.4.2) — a row the driver_define disposition had been hiding. Six driver_define rows remain, each now naming why its define cannot be derived (computed, or a tie).

The file’s own unit (.4c.2). A harness also decides what is compiled BEFORE a file in the same compilation unit, and §22.5.1 makes a macro unit-wide once defined. The derived context now carries those predecessors per file (stimuli/sv/pipeline_context_units.tsv, 44 rows on 17 files), applied as --unit-file in order, from three declaration dialects: verilator’s source-file arguments in the driver’s SV flag lists (the harness puts them before the top file), slang’s tests/unittests/data/*.f command files (-F expanded, -v library files skipped, the units unioned in declaration order), sv2v’s test/*/run.sh explicit multi-file convert / runAndCapture lines (sv2v lexes its inputs as one unit unless --siloed). A -f list (Verilator’s own option-file syntax), a glob, a --siloed run and a pair two declarations order differently are reported, not applied. Re-run on the whole lane, exactly 3 rows moved, all fail → pass, all among the files with predecessors, none the other way: sv2v siloed/module.sv after package.svh, slang test2.sv after test.sv, verilator t_hier_block_import.v after its _def.vh. The fourth cross_file_define row stays: 🔎 its .6b.4 disposition had inferred a pairing from the file names (file_uses_define_in_file_with_no_eol.sv after file_with_no_eol.sv) — no declaration in the vendored slang tree makes it, so the deriver reports nothing for it; hand-given, the pair accepts on both profiles, and the row’s basis now says exactly that.

A suite’s build-wide symbol (.6d.4). One kind of define no driver carries per file: the symbol a whole flow compiles with. OpenTitan’s dvsim passes +define+UVM to every DV build (hw/dv/tools/dvsim/common_sim_cfg.hjson:65), and three DV files guard their include "uvm_macros.svh" on it — without the symbol dv_utils_pkg.sv left every `uvm_* and `DV_* macro below the guard unexpanded and rejected at :215:24 on a raw `uvm_fatal, with 36 packages importing it rejecting behind it. The deriver reserves a hand-curated row kind for exactly this (HAND_DEFINES, one row opentitan define UVM hand <source> in stimuli/sv/pipeline_context.tsv, the source cited), applied as --symbol UVM to every OpenTitan row. Re-run on the whole lane: ten OpenTitan packages fail → pass, zero the other way, and the library pass publishes 264 packages (was 256).

A suite’s unit predecessors (.6d.6). IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5.1 makes a macro unit-wide once defined, and OpenTitan’s dvsim builds one unit: {UVM_HOME}/src/uvm_pkg.sv first (it includes uvm_macros.svh), then dv_utils_pkg.sv (which includes dv_macros.svh), the RTL (prim_assert.sv) and only then the DV env and test packages — which therefore use `uvm_object_utils, `DV_CHECK_*, `gfn, `ASSERT_I without including anything. Parsed one file at a time, 15 of the 38 packages still rejecting after .6d.4 stopped at exactly such a raw macro call. The deriver now carries hand-curated suite-wide unit predecessors (HAND_UNITS, three rows opentitan unit_file <path> hand <source> in stimuli/sv/pipeline_context.tsv), applied as --unit-file in order to every OpenTitan row — about 0.37 s per row. Re-run on the whole lane: 195 OpenTitan rows fail → pass, zero the other way, zero outside OpenTitan; the library publishes 273 packages (368 of OpenTitan’s 396); the members read through their unit accepted_in_unit 999 → 1 287 and unreached_in_unit 846 → 566; the tuple under the pipeline 11053/2606/2677/1391/0. The membership table shrank from 5 130 to 2 392 rows while naming the same 2 058 files: the rows that went were macro headers a predecessor had already brought into the unit, whose guarded `include in the package now expands to nothing.

The library pass (.6d.1). A design is not a bag of files. A file of OpenTitan, black-parrot, VeeR, scr1, friscv or UVM imports typedefs, classes and parameters that a package in another file declares, and the parser only admits such a name where its grammar is fact-gated (a typedef name as a port type, a class name after extends, a parameter name in a range — the store gate of SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13w) once the package’s facts are in scope. The grammar already exports and imports those facts (@export_to_library on package_declaration, @import_from_library on package_import_item; --lib-out DIR / --lib-in DIR). The lane now builds that library before any per-file row runs (stimuli/sv/pipeline_library.py): every package file of the design suites, its import X:: edges read from its preprocessed text, a topological order, each file parsed with its own derived context, the library so far as --lib-in and a private --lib-out, and a passing file’s exports published — at once for a package one file declares, and for a package several files declare (prim_pkg has four, one per vendor) only when every declaring file passed and their fact sets agree; a disagreement is reported, not resolved by guessing which variant the build meant. A rejecting file exports nothing: the engine writes no facts for a rejected parse, so every package importing it stays dark on its names, and the report’s “The library the lane built” table says how many. Then every row runs with --lib-in of the result.

Since 1.0.247 the UVM library is in it (SVPP-EXPANSION.6d.3): uvm_pkg.sv exports uvm_pkg and uvm_polling_pkg, uvm_compat_pkg.sv exports beside it, and 142 of the 168 class files uvm_pkg.sv includes are accepted in their unit (none were before). The OpenTitan DV packages that import uvm_pkg had mostly been accepted earlier, by the fact-gate escapes that admit a uvm_* name without its facts; 48 still rejected at their own first barrier — an unexpanded `uvm_fatal behind an `ifdef UVM the derived context did not satisfy. With the UVM symbol in OpenTitan’s context (SVPP-EXPANSION.6d.4, below) ten of them pass and 121 more members are accepted in their unit; with the three macro headers the flow compiles first as unit predecessors (.6d.6, below) 13 more packages and 195 rows pass. The 25 that remain are three populations, each named per row: 8 stop at a construct 1800-2023 admits and 1800-2017 does not (unsized parameter arrays, an indexed event trigger — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.38, a 2023 reading of the pipeline), 8 at a per-IP build define whose value differs between the IP’s simulation configurations (SVPP-EXPANSION.6d.5, parked: a variant disagreement is reported, not guessed), and 9 at a grammar construct past every macro — randomize() with { … local::x … } (admitted by 1.0.248, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.39: a local::-qualified method receiver), a lifetime in a method prototype (extern function automatic, pure virtual task automatic), a hierarchical name as a cross item, a macro argument carrying a line comment into its stringized text — the SV lane’s work. Since then 1.0.248 and SVPP-EXPANSION.5(l) took three packages out of that last group (i2c_agent_pkg, spi_agent_pkg, alert_esc_agent_pkg); 22 remain: the 8 for the 2023 reading, 9 behind per-IP defines (core_ibex_test_pkg joined them: past its comment it stops at 32'h`BOOT_ADDR), and 5 grammar constructs.

The lane has a second reading, under sv_2023 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.38, 2026-10-02). A reading is one run of the whole lane — the library pass and every row — under one edition profile. PGEN_PIPELINE_PROFILE=sv_2023 stimuli/run_pipeline_lane.sh all produces the second one into _sv2023-suffixed dumps, so the two never share a path, and every run now leaves a provenance sidecar beside its dump (the profile, the binary’s digest, the dumps’ digests) — the record of which run wrote it. The two-edition census (docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/pipeline_sv2023_lane/census.md) joins the readings per file and refuses unless both came from one binary. Measured: 40 rows pass under 2023 only (2023_only_pass) and none under 2017 only (2017_only_pass = 0: the newer edition loses nothing the older accepts, now measured through the preprocessor and the library); 3 more package files pass — the three rstmgr_env_pkg.sv, whose parameter string LIST_OF_LEAFS[] = { is 1800-2023’s unsized parameter dimension — and 51 member files the 2017 reading leaves unreached are reached behind them. The primary reading stays sv_2017: the verdict-coverage tuple is defined over it and did not move. Of the 8 packages that stop at a 2023 construct under 2017, only those 3 pass; the other 5 clear the construct and meet a second barrier — foreach (prv_read[i][j]) (three files), solve … before inside a foreach constraint, and one more per-IP define. Under the 2023 reading 19 OpenTitan packages still rejected. Read one by one (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.41): 10 behind per-IP defines, 1 behind a per-target include (riscv-dv’s riscv_core_setting.sv), 1 behind a macro header the build makes unit-wide (cip_macros.svh), and 7 at a tool tolerance.

The fourth unit predecessor (SVPP-EXPANSION.6d.7, 2026-10-02). cip_macros.svh is a guarded, macro-only header that cip_base_pkg.sv includes INSIDE the package every CIP env imports; OpenTitan’s build compiles that package first, so `DV_MUBI8_DIST and the header’s other macros are unit-wide there and were a raw backtick in a per-file parse. With the header as a sourced suite-wide predecessor, 38 OpenTitan DV rows moved fail → pass under BOTH readings (37 of them testbench tops, tb.sv) and none the other way; csrng_env_pkg passes and publishes. OpenTitan package files still failing: 21 under sv_2017, 18 under sv_2023. Five testbench tops advanced without passing — each now stops at a per-IP define (`EN_MASKING, `SRAM_TYPE, `INSTR_EXEC, `SEC_VOLATILE_RAW_UNLOCK_EN).

Tool tolerances: five spellings the big simulators accept and this parser rejects, under both editions. Each was asked of the standard’s TEXT, not only of Annex A, and each has a reproducer pin that must keep rejecting (stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/), so a widening can only happen as a decision. All five are accepted by the opt-in profile below — the first four since 1.0.249, the fifth since 1.0.250 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.45):

Since 1.0.249 there is an opt-in profile that accepts exactly these spellings: sv_2023_tolerant (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.43, by director decision; the fifth row joined in 1.0.250 by a call the director delegated, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.45 — it is the reference form of the third row, the only way a select expression can name a dotted cross item). It is sv_2023 plus the five spellings and nothing else; the edition profiles are unchanged and remain the default. Ask for it by name — --profile sv_2023_tolerant on the probe, PGEN_PIPELINE_PROFILE=sv_2023_tolerant for a reading of the lane — and each tolerated spelling comes back under its own AST kind (The Json Carrier, The Opt-In Tolerance Profile). Measured on release 1.0.250’s own reading (PGEN_PIPELINE_PROFILE=sv_2023_tolerant, the census at docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/pipeline_sv2023_tolerant_lane/census.md): 18 rows and 7 OpenTitan package files pass under the tolerant profile that sv_2023 rejects (sec_cm_pkg, tl_agent_pkg, adc_ctrl_env_pkg, sysrst_ctrl_env_pkg, flash_ctrl_env_pkg on three tops), five more packages publish (283 against 278), 337 of the 498 members unreached under the primary reading are reached, and nothing sv_2023 accepts is lost (2023_only_pass = 0).
