Under the tolerant reading 11 OpenTitan package files still reject: 10 behind per-IP defines and 1 behind a per-target include — context the corpus does not supply, not syntax.

What the preprocessor REFUSES on the primary reading is a census too, not a residue (SVPP-EXPANSION.4d, 2026-10-06, the lane’s own reason column): 263 (268 before the slice) rows. 168 of them are black-parrot files whose first `include names BaseJump STL (bsg_defines.sv, bsg_noc_links.svh, bsg_cache.svh), a library the corpus does not vendor — honestly absent on the volume, and left so. The rest are top-specific files OpenTitan and HardFloat select with a build target (riscv_core_setting.sv in twelve copies of eleven texts; the xbar autogen pair; HardFloat_specialize.vi in three texts, equidistant from every source/*.v that includes it), build outputs, and error tests by name — unbalanced conditionals, macro-arity and recursion tests, the four include loops, two unquoted include paths. The derivation that supplies the context (stimuli/sv/pipeline_context.py) was itself wrong in two places the census exposed: its include-candidate population was the source files only (.sv / .svh / .v / .vh), so a .vi or .vams header the tree held exactly once was reported absent (IEEE 1800-2017 §22.4 constrains neither the filename nor its suffix); and a tie between copies of one text was reported ambiguous, when the choice cannot change the expansion. Both are fixed — every file is a candidate, an identical tie resolves per file to the nearest copy — and the fix came with the guard it needed: a directory the derivation would emit that also holds an AMBIGUOUS name would let the preprocessor resolve that name by the side door, so a suite directory in that position refuses the derivation and a per-file one is withheld for its includer. The guard fired on its first real run, on the fix’s own first cut (OpenTitan’s darjeeling pwrmgr sequence library, one text for pwrmgr_vseq_list.sv, holds a pwrmgr_base_vseq.sv that differs per top), and the rule was redesigned before anything was measured. Measured on the three readings after the fix: five rows left the refused class under each — two HardFloat specialize.v files and two iverilog .vams tests now parse, the friscv testbench now reaches the parser and stops there — none moved the other way, and twenty HardFloat source rows now stop at the honest three-way tie behind the header the fix resolved. The tuple under the pipeline reads 11173/2606/2557/1270/0.

Measured on the whole lane (the same debug probe, 689 s wall): 425 rows fail → pass and none the other way — OpenTitan 1 077 → 1 444 accepted of 3 983, VeeR 23 → 81 of 102 (its 58 rows had all stopped in el2_param.vh:182, a typedef of el2_pkg). The library: 407 package files, 230 accepted, 170 rejected, 7 refused by the preprocessor, 166 packages published (31 of them declared by several files whose exports agree). What still rejects is measured, not hidden: 🔎 164 of OpenTitan’s 168 rejecting packages import uvm_pkg directly — and uvm_pkg.sv rejects at uvm_transaction.svh:443 on the const local qualifier order the standard does not derive (the director’s .5(d) call), so it exports nothing and the whole DV chain (cip_base_test, dv_base_env_cfg, …) waits on that one ruling; 🔎 six register packages are declared per top and DISAGREE (clkmgr_reg_pkg, gpio_reg_pkg, otp_ctrl_reg_pkg, ast_reg_pkg, ibex_pmp_reset_pkg, pwrmgr_pkg: earlgrey and darjeeling have different register maps), so they are not published and the two RTL packages that need one (otp_ctrl_part_pkg.sv, both tops) still reject — the build declaration (.core) picks the variant, and reading it stays priced, not built; 🔎 44 imported packages are declared by no file in the tree (*_ral_pkg, the generated register-abstraction packages OpenTitan’s flow emits at build time).

The unit-membership reading (.6d.2). An `included class file has no import of its own, so per file it rejects on its first cross-file name whatever the library holds — yet the library pass parsed every one of its bytes inside its package unit. The pass now records which files each unit’s preprocessed text came from (the preprocessor’s source map), and the re-adjudication reads a member’s verdict through its unit: accepted_in_unit when a unit including it passes, the per-file verdict kept when the unit’s rejection lands in this very file, unreached_in_unit when every unit including it rejects elsewhere — the member’s bytes were never judged, and the unit’s origin is named rather than the member’s first cross-file name. An accepted member counts as adjudicated in the design suites, exactly as a file accepted under its context does; an unreached member stays dark, with its reason. Measured: 2 060 distinct member files across the design suites (OpenTitan 1 906); of the 2 059 members the answer key routes, none is accepted in a unit today and 1 923 are unreached (OpenTitan 1 783, UVM 140), 89 are the file their unit’s rejection lands in. 🔎 The reason is one ruling: every OpenTitan and UVM package that `includes class files imports uvm_pkg, and uvm_pkg.sv exports nothing until the const local question is ruled — the reading is in place and idle, and the same run converts the 1 923 the day the ruling lands. The dark population is now named by its unit’s origin (clkmgr_base_test.sv:5, uvm_transaction.svh:443) rather than by each member’s first cross-file name.

The denominator, read twice. The platform book’s verdict-coverage tuple (adjudicated/routed/no-verdict/dark/axis-2-bar) now carries two readings of the same rows, published together and held by the same gate: the raw lane’s 7486/2606/6244/4037/9, and 9135/2606/4595/3312/14 under the pipeline. The second is the first with the re-adjudication table applied: 1 218 explained-away rows corroborated, 1 704 design-corpus files accepted under their derived context and library (must-accept by the suite’s own convention — a shipping design compiles), 448 must-reject rows rejected where the raw lane never reached the construct (28 of them the key questions of the disposition table, pinned with the clause and a reproducer each, 3 the rows a file’s own driver define reaches — .4c.1, and 11 the pipeline-routed parser questions re-read at the furthest token — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.12b.1), and 5 must-accept rows still refused in their own text (three of .12b.1’s four grammar families shipped: the spaced @ ( * ) as 1.0.228 — nine pipeline rows fail → pass — and the $-indexed receiver with the sv_2023 +%- range as 1.0.229, whose streaming-slice row proved the standard’s own refusal and is pinned) — the bar’s members, each with its clause, until the corpus tree rules them. 2 935 rows are dark under the pipeline on a declaration another file holds; that is the library design’s population. The report also re-reads every row the key expects rejected — including a pin the raw lane could not cash because its parse stopped on a macro use above the construct: 34 verilator rows (a typedef reaching a type through two or more hierarchical steps, a type named through an interface instance in a type assignment, an enum with a range but no base type) reject at the pinned line under the pipeline on both profiles, and no row the standard cannot derive is accepted beyond the two the raw lane already knew. The report is held to a fresh derivation on every commit, like the lane’s.

⛔ A note on the host, not the engine. The reading above was taken on the debug probe because no release build of the crate could be completed on the development host that day: a per-process memory watchdog independent of the repository’s own guard kills any process above 14 GB, and the release build’s compile now peaks just past it (the operations chapter of the platform book records the numbers). A build profile cannot change a verdict; the deadline was widened to 600 s so the slower probe could not manufacture a timeout (the slowest non-timeout row of the release reading was 5.75 s), and the identity block of the tracked report names the debug binary.

Two thirds of the residue was one fact when that reading was taken: the base class of a class … extends lives in another file of the compilation unit (a package the row imports, or a sibling .sv), and the parser’s store gate refuses a base it has not seen declared — the strict reading SV-PARSE-STRICT.2 escaped for net types and not for class bases. That is a cross-file DECLARATION barrier, exactly the one the library flags (--lib-out / --lib-in) exist for.

Since SVPP-EXPANSION.6e (2026-10-06) the residue is a census, derived and tracked — docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/rejects_own_file_census/census.md, re-derived after every lane reading, its identity held by the PIPELINE-LANE-CURRENCY doctrine’s fourth arm. Every row the re-adjudication files as rejected in its own file is re-expanded under the lane’s own context and classed by what the parser actually SAW, not by the source line the stop maps back to. On the reading of 2026-10-06 the 310 rows fall as follows: 143 are the base-class barrier above (126 of them files only ever read through the package that includes them); 47 stop at a raw backtick in the expanded text — an undefined macro reached the parser, a CONTEXT gap that happened one stage late; since .6f the stage refuses such a leftover before the parser can meet it and the class is EMPTY, kept as a tripwire (OpenTitan’s per-IP build defines such as EN_MASKING and RNG_BUS_WIDTH, which live in the IPs’ *_sim_cfg.hjson build options; VeeR’s RV_* configuration macros, whose common_defines.vh the VeeR Makefile compiles first — supplied since .6d.8, three rows now pass; two BlackParrot and one friscv header chain); 55 are include fragments of a module, testbench or package whose standalone reading is not a claim about the parser (riscv-dv’s riscv_core_setting.sv, the xbar autogen pair, VeeR’s el2_dec_csr_equ_*.svh); 11 are the same declaration barrier in data position (mubi4_t sel_mux; — the type is declared in a file the row did not see); 7 are the 2023 text’s (a parameter’s unsized [], which 1800-2023’s param_assignment admits and 1800-2017’s does not; `begin_keywords "1800-2023") and 5 the tolerant profile’s; 16 are error tests by name, verilator preprocessor tests whose own driver runs -E, and verible module-body fragments that declare themselves so. The 26 that remain are adjudicated one by one in SVPP-EXPANSION.6e: invalid SystemVerilog the standard does not derive (a ~& b, a modport inside a generate, a trailing comma in a parameter list, a do port name under an SV profile, an if arm of two statements without begin/end, a module named after a synthesis cell $_DLATCH_P_), three more cross-file declaration barriers the mechanical shape test could not see, three non-SystemVerilog test inputs, one preprocessor question routed to .5(r) (a `define whose // comment line ends in a backslash), and five spellings the ecosystem accepts that the census read as derived by no edition — $fatal("…") without its finish number, #(.Param) without parentheses, static task before the keyword outside a class, a size with a leading zero (01'b0), #a.b as a delay — recorded as candidates for the opt-in tolerance profile. None was admitted: SV-CORPUS-GRAD.46 measured them against the two tools on this host (static task refused by both — withdrawn; three accepted by one tool only — out), and the one every tool accepts, 01'b0, turned out to be DERIVED by IEEE 1800-2023 (size ::= unsigned_number; SV-CORPUS-GRAD.47, release 1.0.251): it parses under sv_2023 as standard text, not as a tolerance, and friscv’s rtl/friscv_alu.sv passes under that reading.

  • The seven curated real-design cases of the external-corpus triage gate (UVM’s two packages, scr1, friscv, VeeR) run through the single command with the manifest’s include directories: the expansion of uvm_pkg.sv (166 included files) matched the shell gate’s byte for byte until SVPP-EXPANSION.6b.5, which found the gate’s reference (3 022 806 bytes) wrong in 98 lines — all inside block comments: the preprocessor of 2026-08-24 had honoured `define lines inside a /* … */ (uvm_tlm_imps.svh keeps older macro versions in one) and expanded macro uses inside others. The expansion is now 3 020 226 bytes, every changed hunk audited inside a comment, and scr1 / friscv / VeeR accept on both profiles.
  • UVM’s uvm_pkg.sv — the unit-level reading of that suite — parses on both profiles since 1.0.247 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.37, ledger SV-0132, 2026-10-01). From the 2026-09-04 release that made local a reserved word until then it rejected at src/base/uvm_transaction.svh:443, const local uvm_event_pool events = new("events");: IEEE 1800-2017 A.1.9 gives a const-first class property only const { class_item_qualifier } data_type const_identifier [ = constant_expression ] ;, and new(…) is not a constant_expression (the local const … order is derivable through data_declaration, which admits a class_new initializer). Every commercial simulator accepts the UVM spelling, and §8.19’s prose describes it as a constant with an initial value. Recorded deviation (tool extension, on by default): class_property’s const arm admits a class_new initializer — ( assign ( class_new | constant_expression ) )? — under the director’s standing ruling that a change must not make the parser reject what the ecosystem writes; the typed shape is the one the arm always declared. The policy record: docs/tasks/SVPP-EXPANSION.md (.5(d), closed).

Boundaries

  • The expansion engine is hand-written Rust (rust/src/families/systemverilog/preprocessor.rs — the SystemVerilog family’s own component since ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.113, published to the engine as one neutral preprocessing stage, rust/src/preprocessing_stage.rs, which knows nothing of the backtick), not a grammar; its directive structure is separately described by the systemverilog_preprocessor grammar, whose parser does not expand anything. The two are different deliverables and this chapter is about the first.
  • The pipeline preprocesses one compilation unit at a time and parses its last file; a multi-file design still needs the library flags for cross-file declarations.
  • Nothing yet reads a build system’s own context (.core, .f, +incdir+); on the command line the context is what you pass, and in the corpus lane it is derived from the corpus — a shared directory per suite, the nearest candidate per file for a name that exists in several, and a reported tie where the tree cannot decide (a tie between copies of one text is not one); and a directory that would resolve an ambiguous name by the side door is never emitted (.4d).

AST Envelope Structure

The PGEN SystemVerilog parser produces a JSON AST through parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named. This chapter documents the top-level structure of that JSON.

The envelope

The AST-dump host entry points (the generic parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump* family and the named-result form parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named) return — on success — an AstDumpPayload, defined in rust/src/embedding_api.rs (the authoritative API contract is rust/docs/EMBEDDING_API_CONTRACT.md). It is a canonical-JSON payload string plus truncation metadata — it has exactly four fields:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct AstDumpPayload {
    pub dump_json: String,    // canonical (key-sorted) JSON encoding of the typed AST
    pub truncated: bool,      // true if max_ast_bytes was exceeded
    pub full_bytes: usize,    // byte length of the full encoded AST (pre-truncation)
    pub emitted_bytes: usize, // byte length actually placed in dump_json
}
}

dump_json is a JSON string you must parse (e.g. serde_json::from_str) to obtain the systemverilog_file root object that this book’s per-rule chapters describe. There is no root / schema_version / grammar / profile field on AstDumpPayload itself: the AST-dump schema version is the 1 tracked in Schema Versioning (pinned from the contract, not a payload field); the grammar/profile are fixed (systemverilog / sv_2017 | sv_2023).

When truncated is true, dump_json is not the AST — it is a deterministic truncation diagnostic envelope carrying pgen_dump_contract_version (currently 1), kind: "pgen_ast_dump_truncation", truncated: true, dump_kind: "parser_return_ast", max_bytes, full_bytes, and reason. Consumers must check truncated (or, equivalently, the presence of pgen_dump_contract_version / kind == "pgen_ast_dump_truncation" in the parsed dump_json) before treating dump_json as a SystemVerilog AST. If max_ast_bytes is too small to fit even the diagnostic envelope, the API returns E_INVALID_LIMITS. The downstream integration contract docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md (“Contract Identity” + “Schema Versioning”) is the authoritative restatement of this for consumers.

The parsed dump_json is what this book’s per-rule chapters describe.

The root rule

The SystemVerilog grammar root is the systemverilog_file rule (the parser-generation default and the embedding-API entry). It is typed — it wraps the source_text body:

systemverilog_file := trivia source_text trivia
                   -> {type: "systemverilog_file", source_text: $2}

{ "type": "systemverilog_file", "source_text": [ /* source_text_item shapes */ ] }

Dispatch on root["type"] == "systemverilog_file", then iterate root["source_text"] (a flat array of typed source_text_item shapes, each carrying a kind discriminator).

Two carrier kinds: typed and recursive-envelope

Per-rule, the AST dump produces JSON in one of two shapes:

Typed shape (rules with return annotations)

When a grammar rule carries a -> {...} return annotation, the rule produces a typed JSON object:

{
  "type": "<rule-family>",
  "kind": "<specific-shape>",
  "...": "..."
}

Examples (from the regex parser, for shape illustration; SV typed shapes will land per-slice):

{"type": "atom", "kind": "literal", "value": "a"}
{"type": "anchor", "kind": "start_of_line"}
{"type": "escape", "kind": "shorthand", "char": "d"}

The annotation campaign (see Changelog Index) lands these typed shapes one rule at a time.

Recursive envelope shape (rules without annotations)

When a grammar rule has no return annotation, the rule produces a JSON value derived from its grammar shape:

  • A terminal literal produces a JSON string of the matched text.
  • A regex literal produces a JSON string of the matched text.
  • A rule reference produces whatever shape that rule produces.
  • A sequence produces a JSON array of the per-element shapes.
  • An alternation produces the matched branch’s shape directly.
  • A quantified rule (e.g. expr*, expr+) produces a JSON array of the per-iteration shapes.
  • An optional rule (expr?) produces either the matched shape (if matched) or [] (if un-matched).

For a 3-element sequence rule like a b c, the envelope shape is [<a-shape>, <b-shape>, <c-shape>].

Mixing typed and envelope shapes

Until the annotation campaign covers every rule, the AST tree carries a mix of typed objects and recursive arrays. Consumers need to handle both:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn walk(node: &serde_json::Value) {
    match node {
        serde_json::Value::Object(obj) => {
            // Typed shape — dispatch on `type` / `kind`.
            // See per-rule chapters.
        }
        serde_json::Value::Array(items) => {
            // Recursive-envelope shape — walk children.
            for item in items {
                walk(item);
            }
        }
        serde_json::Value::String(text) => {
            // Terminal text — no children.
        }
        _ => {
            // Bool / Number / Null — produced by typed annotations using
            // `BooleanLiteral` / `NumberLiteral` / `NullLiteral`.
        }
    }
}
}

See Walking the AST for the full walker pattern.

Determinism

The AST dump is deterministic for a given input + parser-release version:

  • Object keys are emitted in canonical (alphabetical) order.
  • Number formatting is canonical (no trailing zeros for integers, etc.).
  • Whitespace is configurable via AstDumpOptions.pretty (compact vs pretty-printed) but the underlying JSON value is the same.

Any non-determinism in the dump is a bug — please report via docs/contracts/PGEN_PARSER_ISSUE_REPORTING_PROTOCOL.md.

Truncation

If AstDumpOptions.max_ast_bytes is set and the encoded JSON exceeds it, the dump is truncated and truncated: true is set on the payload. The truncated payload is still valid JSON (the truncation happens at a node boundary). Consumers should check the truncated flag and either bail or note the truncation.

ParseContent Variants

This chapter documents the ParseContent variants that the generated parser produces internally, and how each maps to the public AST-dump JSON shape consumers receive.

Note: ParseContent is the internal AST-pipeline representation used by PGEN’s parser hooks and codegen. Downstream consumers do not call ParseContent directly — they call parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named and walk the resulting JSON. This chapter is included as reference for tooling that introspects PGEN’s behaviour or for downstream maintainers debugging shape issues.

The variants

PGEN’s ast_pipeline::ParseContent enum has these variants:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub enum ParseContent {
    Terminal(String),                      // matched literal text
    Sequence(Vec<UnifiedReturnAST>),       // ordered children (e.g. from `a b c`)
    Quantified(Vec<UnifiedReturnAST>),     // iterations of `expr*` / `expr+`
    Or(Box<UnifiedReturnAST>),             // matched branch of an alternation
    Alternative(Box<UnifiedReturnAST>),    // boxed inner shape (per-branch wrap)
    Json(serde_json::Value),               // typed JSON value (from annotations)
    // (other variants for internal codegen use)
}
}

How each variant lands in the AST dump JSON

ParseContent variantJSON shape consumers see
Terminal(text)"<text>" (string)
Sequence(children)[<child0_json>, <child1_json>, ...]
Quantified(iters)[<iter0_json>, <iter1_json>, ...]
Or(inner)<inner_json> (transparent)
Alternative(inner)<inner_json> (transparent)
Json(value)<value> directly (typed object/string/number/bool/null)

So at the JSON layer, consumers see either:

  • A JSON string (from Terminal), or
  • A JSON array (from Sequence / Quantified), or
  • A JSON object / number / bool / null (from typed Json annotations).

Or and Alternative are transparent — they pass their inner shape through.

When you’ll see each shape

In a fully-annotated grammar (the goal of the campaign), most rules produce typed Json(object) shapes and consumers walk a tree of typed objects with occasional arrays for ordered children.

In a partially-annotated grammar (the current state of the SV parser), un-annotated rules produce recursive Sequence / Quantified arrays — JSON arrays of strings and other arrays, walked by structural recursion. Annotated rules produce typed objects in the middle of those arrays.

The annotation-system is designed so you can walk either shape with the same dispatch:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
match node {
    JsonValue::Object(obj) => { /* typed shape */ }
    JsonValue::Array(items) => { /* recursive-envelope shape */ }
    JsonValue::String(text) => { /* terminal */ }
    JsonValue::Bool(_) | JsonValue::Number(_) | JsonValue::Null => {
        /* annotation-produced scalar */
    }
}
}

See Walking the AST for the recommended walker pattern.

Why two shapes coexist

The annotation campaign types rules incrementally. Each slice annotates one rule (or a small family of related rules) and bumps the schema version. At any point in time the grammar has a mix of annotated rules (typed shape) and un-annotated rules (envelope shape). The downstream AST is the natural composition of both.

The schema version 1.0.0 milestone (see Schema Versioning) lands when every rule is either annotated or has a deliberate “stay un-annotated” decision — at which point the AST shape is fully locked.

The Json Carrier

This chapter is a flat reference table of every systemverilog.ebnf rule that carries a -> ... return annotation, and the JSON shape that annotation produces.

Note: The systemverilog return-annotation campaign is in early phase. Most rules are currently un-annotated and produce the recursive-envelope shape described in AST Envelope Structure. This table grows as the campaign progresses.

Currently annotated rules

RuleAnnotationJSON shape produced
systemverilog_file-> {type: "systemverilog_file", source_text: $2}{"type": "systemverilog_file", "source_text": <source_text-shape>} — root JSON object for any sv_2017 / sv_2023 parse. source_text field is a flat array of source_text_item shapes (since SV-Slice-2).
systemverilog_parseable_file-> {type: "systemverilog_parseable_file", items: $2}{"type": "systemverilog_parseable_file", "items": <parseable_source_item*-shape>} — alternative entry rule for the parseable-source profile. items field carries the array of parseable source items in their raw envelope shape.
source_text-> [$1**][<source_text_item-typed-shape>, ...] — flat array of typed source-text items via flatten-spread. Each item is a {kind: "<name>", body: <envelope>} typed object (per SV-Slice-3).
source_text_item (7 branches)per-branch {kind: "<name>", body: $1} (or {kind: "semi"} for branch 6)Typed object with kind discriminator: "description", "local_parameter_declaration", "parameter_declaration", "package_import_declaration", "timeunits_declaration", "compiler_directive", "semi". The body field carries the matched sub-rule’s raw envelope OR a typed sub-rule shape if that sub-rule is itself annotated. For kind: "description", body is now itself typed (per SV-Slice-4). The semi branch carries no body since it’s just a stray ;. Trailing semi dropped in branches 1 and 2 (annotation references $1 only). **The former 8th branch comment_only_source_region was removed (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.5.3): it was engine-shadowed-dead — the layout skipper consumes comments as leading trivia before this rule’s branch is tried, so a comment-only region is always absorbed as layout and the comment_only_source_region kind was never emitted in any AST (a comment-only file parses to an empty source_text). Removing it is accept-identical — no schema/release bump — and narrows the declared union to the kinds that can actually occur.
description (8 branches)per-branch {kind: "<name>", body: $1} for single-element branches; {kind: "<name>", attributes: $1, body: $2} for multi-element branches with attribute_instance* prefixTyped object with kind discriminator: "module_declaration", "udp_declaration", "interface_declaration", "program_declaration", "package_declaration", "package_item", "bind_directive", "config_declaration". The attributes field (only on package_item / bind_directive branches) carries the leading attribute_instance* iteration. The body field carries the matched sub-rule’s raw envelope (per-rule typing of module_declaration, etc. is a follow-up slice).
compiler_directive (2 branches; schema 29)passthrough / {kind: "opaque", text: $2}Since parser release 1.0.217 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.39) the body is a TYPED node. Branch 1 passes through one of the thirteen *_directive nodes below ({kind: "timescale", unit, precision}, {kind: "line", number, filename, level}, …); branch 2 — any other backtick line at file top level (`include, `define, the conditional family, a text-macro use, a vendor directive) — is {kind: "opaque", text: "<the line>"}. ⚠️ Through 1.0.216 body was the directive LINE as one string ("`timescale 1ns / 1ps"); a consumer that read it as a string must now switch on body.kind, and body.kind == "opaque" carries the old string as text. The thirteen typed names are refused when their arguments do not match the clause’s syntax box (`timescale frump no longer parses). See Typed Compiler Directives.
in_scope_compiler_directive (7 branches; schema 29)passthroughThe in-scope whitelist (.3.14b) as the same typed nodes: celldefine, endcelldefine, undefineall (SV-only), undef, timescale, pragma, line. No opaque branch in scope, by design. non_port_module_item and class_item wrap it as {kind: "compiler_directive", body: <typed node>} — the same node the top-level container carries. ⚠️ A consumer that exhaustively matches module-item or class-item kinds must carry a compiler_directive arm (since 1.0.178).
resetall_directive / celldefine_directive / endcelldefine_directive / nounconnected_drive_directive / end_keywords_directive / undefineall_directive (schema 29)-> {kind: "<name>"}The argument-less directives (IEEE 1800-2017 §22.3, §22.10, §22.9, §22.14, §22.5.3). undefineall_directive is @profiles: ["sv_2017", "sv_2023"]; under verilog_2005 the same text is a text-macro use and lands as {kind: "opaque"}.
undef_directive (schema 29)-> {kind: "undef", name: $2}name is an identifier node ({body}; simple or escaped — §22.5.2 Syntax 22-4).
timescale_directive (schema 29)-> {kind: "timescale", unit: $2, precision: $4}Both slots are directive_time_literal nodes {value: "1" | "10" | "100", unit: {kind: "s" | "ms" | "us" | "ns" | "ps" | "fs"}} (§22.7 Syntax 22-6; the magnitude is SYNTAX here — “the valid integers are 1, 10, and 100” — while timeunit 2ps; stays derivable through Annex A’s own production). unit.unit reuses the time_unit node kinds. The precision-ordering rule (“at least as precise”, §22.7 prose) is NOT judged: `timescale 1ps/1ns parses.
directive_time_literal / directive_time_magnitude (schema 29){value: $1, unit: $2} / -> $2value is the magnitude text; white space between magnitude and unit is admitted (1 ns, the clause’s own example).
default_nettype_directive / default_nettype_value / default_nettype_none_word (schema 29){kind: "default_nettype", value: $2} / per-branch {kind: "<value>"}value.kind is one of §22.8 Syntax 22-7’s eleven: wire tri tri0 tri1 wand triand wor trior trireg uwire none — deliberately NOT net_type (no supply0 / supply1).
unconnected_drive_directive / unconnected_drive_value (schema 29){kind: "unconnected_drive", value: $2} / {kind: "pull0"} | {kind: "pull1"}§22.9: “takes one of two arguments — pull1 or pull0”. nounconnected_drive_directive takes none.
pragma_directive (2 branches, @branch_policy: ordered; schema 29){kind: "pragma", name: $2, expressions: [] | $3}name is the pragma_name string (a simple_identifier, keywords admitted — `pragma protect begin has begin as a pragma_keyword). Branch 1 is the bare-name form bounded to its LINE (pragma_line_end), so `pragma once followed by an identifier-led item on the next line does not eat that item; branch 2 is the comma-separated pragma_expression_list (§22.11 Syntax 22-8). Ordered choice because the grammar’s default longest-match tournament would have picked branch 2 whenever the next line began with an identifier.
pragma_expression_list / pragma_expression / pragma_keyword / pragma_name (schema 29)[$1, $2::2*] / per-branch {kind: "assignment", keyword, value} | {kind: "keyword", name} | {kind: "value", value} / passthrough stringsA bare identifier is a keyword (the LRM lists pragma_keyword first); pragma_value’s identifier arm is therefore reached only on the right of = (key_method = RSA).
pragma_value (4 branches; schema 29)per-branch {kind: "group", items} | {kind: "number", body} | {kind: "string", body} | {kind: "identifier", body}group.items is a nested pragma_expression_list; number.body is the number node ({kind: "integral" | "real", body}); string.body a string_literal node ({kind: "double_quoted", body} with the quotes).
line_directive / line_number / line_level / line_end (schema 29){kind: "line", number: $2, filename: $3, level: $4} / -> $2 / -> $2 / (regex, no node)§22.12 Syntax 22-9: number a positive integer ([1-9][0-9]*, as text), filename a string_literal node, level "0" | "1" | "2"; line_end is the empty-matching regex that asserts “only white space may appear on the same line … comments are not allowed” — the one directive the clause binds to its line.
begin_keywords_directive / keywords_version_specifier (+ _sv_2017 / _sv_2023 / _v2005) (schema 29){kind: "begin_keywords", version: $2} / {kind: "double_quoted", body: $2}version carries the quoted literal exactly as string_literal does. One profiled token per edition holds that edition’s list: IEEE 1800-2017 Syntax 22-10’s eight, IEEE 1800-2023’s nine (adds "1800-2023"), IEEE 1364-2005 Syntax 19-10’s four — so `begin_keywords "1800-2023" parses under sv_2023 and REJECTS under sv_2017 (“it shall be an error if an implementation does not recognize the version_specifier”).

net_type_declaration_sv_2017 / nettype_declaration_sv_2023 (2 branches each; schema 31)data-type form -> {data_type: $2, name: $3, with_clause: $4} (sv_2017) / -> {kind: "data_type", data_type: $2, name: $3, with_clause: $4} (sv_2023); ALIAS form -> {kind: "nettype", scope: $2, base: $3, name: $4} (both editions)A user-defined nettype declaration, IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.1.3 / §6.6.7. Since 1.0.219 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.45) the ALIAS form nettype wTsum nettypeid2; — another name for an existing nettype — wins its tie in both edition twins, typed on sv_2017 too, with its base store-gated. Through 1.0.218 it was SHADOWED: both alternatives succeed on the LRM’s own example (a declared nettype is a type_name fact, so the data-type form reads wTsum as a known_unscoped_data_type) and the longest-match tie went to declaration order, so the alias alternative never won and the AST called the base nettype a data type. 1.0.219 breaks the tie in the LRM’s favour by a NEGATIVE LOOKAHEAD on the data-type alternative — it refuses a text that reads as an alias head, [ scope ] <declared nettype> <identifier> ; — with the ORDER left as shipped, and routes the alias base net_type_identifier (a bare declaration_identifier through 1.0.218, one ungated twin per edition) to checked_nettype_identifier | wildcard_escape_nettype_identifier (a declared nettype, or an undeclared name under import pkg::* — how net_declaration reads a net of a user-defined nettype, SV-PARSE-STRICT.2 / SV-0037). Two spellings were refuted before this one: reordering the UNGATED alternative read nettype T wT; (T a typedef) as an alias — the two-sided corpus sweep caught it on one file — and reordering the GATED one broke the certificate’s own nettype prelude (the generator renders an unplanned declaration with the first of two equally cheap alternatives, so the prelude became an alias with an undeclared base and the union certificate read UNKNOWN=2). The alias alternative now wins exactly the alias declarations. ⚠️ One NARROWING: nettype undeclared_t x; with no wildcard import in scope — accepted through 1.0.218 down the ungated alias alternative, LRM-illegal (the base must be an existing nettype) — now REJECTS on both SV profiles; the corpus census read 0 accepting files down that alternative, and the pin invalid_nettype_alias_undeclared_base.sv holds it. scope is [] or the nettype_scope_prefix node, base the existing nettype’s identifier node, name the new one. The data-type form is byte-identical across the release (kind absent on sv_2017). See Typed Partial Alternatives. The optional with-clause resolution-function reference may be package/class-scoped (with pkg::f); its scope element is the clean nettype_scope_prefix shape. ⚠️ Schema 11 → 12 (1.0.157, ledger SV-0019): at releases 1.0.0–1.0.156 the double-nested with-clause ( non_typedef_package_scope | class_scope )? corrupted the AST — nettype logic n with pkg::f; emitted three <invalid_sequence_access> in the with_clause inner scope element (the data_type/name/with_clause slots) when the self-annotated non_typedef_package_scope branch won. 1.0.157 lifts the alternation into the shared named nettype_scope_prefix rule; the with_clause inner scope is now clean. The scoped-base nettype pkg::base nt; (br1) form was already clean. See Schema Versioning.

The vector form was the most common block declaration in the corpus without one: 712 nodes in 259 accepting files per SV lane, 130 in 73 on the 1364-2005 lane, every one moved by 1.0.220 and nothing else. ⛔ Removed in 1.0.245 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.32, schema 34 unchanged): the permissive twin provisional_unscoped_block_class_type (branch 13, gated on has_fact(type_name) alone) — kept at the block site “for class-internal scoped types” since 2026-05-30, which a --trace-rules reading shows take scoped_block_type_identifier (branch 9), and whose only unique admissions were T #(int) x; / T::P x; on a typedef’d int; the corpus liveness census read it committing in 357 files of the sv_2017 lane, in 72 of them alone, every one a bare typedef’d type that branch 10 wins, so no accepted tree passed through it (measured: every sweep ast_moved=0). The node a declared class renders is unchanged — known_unscoped_block_class_type’s {head, params, scope_chain}.
class_scoped_call_prefix_head-> $1 (un-annotated named rule; scoped_class_scoped_call_prefix_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scoped_call_class_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scoped_call_interface_class_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scoped_call_type_parameter_identifier)Since 1.0.158 (SV-0020, SV-AST-SHAPE-FIDELITY.2.7). Passthrough of whichever class-scoped-call-prefix head matched: scoped_class_scoped_call_prefix_identifier {scope, name} (a package-scoped class, pkg::C) or a bare class / interface-class / type-parameter identifier {body:…}. This named rule was introduced to fix an AST-shape corruption — see class_scoped_call_prefix.
class_scoped_call_prefix (pkg::C::foo(); 2 arms, ordered, since 1.0.243)-> {head: $1, params: $2, scope_chain: $4} (both arms)The <pkg>::<class>:: prefix of a class-scoped static method call. Since 1.0.243 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.31) a LAST arm, tried only where the known arm fails, is the wildcard escape: an unresolved parameterized class under an open import pkg::* (uvm_config_db#(T)::set(…)) renders the same {head, params, scope_chain} object, the head the bare class_identifier node, measured byte-identical to a declared class’s; the escape consumes the parameter list, so a bare ident :: never takes it. head: is the clean class_scoped_call_prefix_head shape ({scope, name} for a package-scoped class, {body:…} for a bare one); params: the optional parameter_value_assignment ([] when absent); scope_chain: the further ::class hops ([] when none). ⚠️ Schema 12 → 13 (1.0.158, ledger SV-0020): at releases 1.0.0–1.0.157 head: bound an inline 4-way alternation directly, corrupting the AST — pkg::C::foo() (reachable in statement + assignment-RHS context) emitted two <invalid_sequence_access> in the params/scope_chain slots (the self-annotated scoped_class_scoped_call_prefix_identifier branch’s {scope,name} re-recursed the rule’s own {head, params, scope_chain} annotation onto the branch result). 1.0.158 lifts the alternation into the named class_scoped_call_prefix_head rule (mirroring the in-file class_scope_type_head); params/scope_chain are now the clean []. SV-0013 gated the alt’s branches but did not lift it — this completes that rule. Consumers reading a class-scoped call’s params/scope_chain must adopt the clean [] shape. See Schema Versioning.
class_scope_type_head-> $1 (un-annotated named rule; scoped_class_scope_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scope_class_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scope_interface_class_identifier | known_unscoped_class_scope_type_parameter_identifier)Since 1.0.155 (SV-0017, SV-AST-SHAPE-FIDELITY.2.3). Passthrough of whichever class-scope-head form matched: scoped_class_scope_identifier {scope, name} (package-scoped, pkg::B) or a bare class_identifier {body:…}. This named rule was introduced to fix an AST-shape corruption — see class_scope_type.
class_scope_type (and, since 1.0.243, its escape twin wildcard_escape_class_scope_type, class_scope’s ordered last alternative)-> {head: $1, params: $2, scope_chain: $3}The scoped class-scope head of a C::D::E chain (via class_scope). Since 1.0.243 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.31) class_scope is ordered with the escape as its LAST alternative, tried only where the known arm fails: a declared class keeps the known arm and its tree (the same span on both arms), an unresolved parameterized class under an open wildcard import takes the escape and renders the identical {body: {head, params, scope_chain}} object; the four type-position prefixes (scoped_type_scope_prefix, nettype_scope_prefix, the two ps_type_identifier_scope twins) reference class_scope_plain — the first alternative alone — because at a module item’s start ident #( … ) is also an instantiation head. head: is the clean class_scope_type_head shape; params: / scope_chain: are the optional parameter-value-assignment / trailing ::class chain ([] when absent). ⚠️ Schema 9 → 10 (1.0.155, ledger SV-0017): at releases 1.0.0–1.0.154 head: bound an inline 4-way alternation directly, corrupting the AST — a scoped type reference emitted <invalid_sequence_access> in params/scope_chain (when the self-annotated scoped_class_scope_identifier branch won). 1.0.155 lifts the alternation into the named class_scope_type_head rule (mirroring the in-file class_type_head/base_class_type_head); params/scope_chain are now clean. See Schema Versioning.
scoped_type_scope_prefix-> $1 (un-annotated named rule; class_scope | non_typedef_package_scope)Since 1.0.155 (SV-0017, SV-AST-SHAPE-FIDELITY.2.3). Passthrough of whichever scope prefix matched for a scoped type identifier: class_scope {body:…} (C::D::) or non_typedef_package_scope (pkg::). This named rule was introduced to fix an AST-shape corruption — see scoped_data_type_identifier. Since 1.0.246 (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.111) it is the prefix of scoped_data_type_identifier and of dpi_result_data_type’s scoped arm ONLY, and class_scope carries the .31 wildcard escape (1.0.243 had put class_scope_plain here and this row lagged); the block twin below has its own prefix.
scoped_block_type_scope_prefix-> $1 (un-annotated named rule; class_scope_plain | non_typedef_package_scope)Since 1.0.246 (SV-0131, ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.111). The prefix of scoped_block_type_identifier alone: the BLOCK site keeps the escape-free class_scope_plain, because block_data_type’s own last arm (the .30 block escape) already renders an unresolved parameterized or scoped class under a wildcard import as {head, params, scope_chain}, and a prefix with the escape let the scoped arm (branch 9) win that text first and move the tree ({scope, type, dims}) — caught by the release’s interpreter A/B. Renders exactly what scoped_type_scope_prefix renders for a declared class scope or a package scope.
scoped_data_type_identifier / scoped_block_type_identifier-> {scope: $1, type: $2, dims: $3}A package/class-scoped type reference (C::D::E), in data_type (scoped_data_type) and block_data_type contexts respectively (since 1.0.246 through scoped_type_scope_prefix and scoped_block_type_scope_prefix respectively). scope: is the clean prefix shape; type: is the trailing type_identifier {body:…}; dims: is the (possibly empty) packed-dimension list. ⚠️ Schema 9 → 10 (1.0.155, ledger SV-0017): at releases 1.0.0–1.0.154 scope: bound the inline alt `( class_scope

IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.6 gives the production two forms — the NON-ported [ interface_identifier . | class_scope ] function_identifier ; with tf_item_declaration items, and the PORTED … function_identifier ( [ tf_port_list ] ) ; with block_item_declaration items — each with an optional out-of-block prefix, hence four branches. No kind: a consumer discriminates the LRM form by KEY PRESENCE — ports is present exactly on the ported branches (2, 4; [] for f()), scope exactly on the out-of-block branches (3, 4; the out_of_block_tf_scope node — the pair [<interface_identifier>, {kind: "dot"}] or the class_scope node). items holds tf_item_declaration nodes ({kind: "block_item" | "tf_port", body}) on the non-ported branches and BARE block_item_declaration nodes on the ported ones, exactly as the standard’s two productions read; return_type is the matched function_data_type_or_implicit; name a clean identifier node; end_label [] or the [{kind: "colon"}, <identifier>] pair. Drops semi, lparen / rparen, kw_endfunction. ⚠️ Through 1.0.217 branches 2–4 arrived as the RAW Sequence envelope (a positional array of 10 / 8 / 11 elements) — measured over the corpus at 2 211 of 3 411 bodies, the ported form being the most common function in any corpus; branch 1 is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the release. See Typed Function and Task Bodies.

The corpus writes no body of branch 3 (an out-of-block, non-ported task) on any lane — its shape is held by the pin control_tf_body_task_out_of_block_class.sv and the AST-shape contract sample task_body_out_of_block_interface.

net_strength (NEW; 2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "drive" (body is the matched drive_strength shape) / "charge" (body is the matched charge_strength shape). Helper rule extracted from inline ( drive_strength | charge_strength )? to dodge task #38.
net_vector_scalar (NEW; 2 branches)per-branch {kind} (no body)Kind labels: "vectored" / "scalared". Helper rule extracted from inline ( kw_vectored | kw_scalared )? to dodge task #38. Bare {kind} shape — each branch matches a single keyword token.
class_item_sv_2017 (8 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "property" / "method" / "constraint" / "class" / "covergroup" (first 5 with attribute_instance* prefix as attributes) / "local_parameter" / "parameter" (drop trailing semi via body: $1) / "semi" (bare, no body). Reached from class_declaration_sv_2017.items[].
class_item_sv_2023 (9 branches)per-branch typedSame 8 kinds as sv_2017 plus "interface_class" (with attribute_instance* prefix) — LRM 2023 allows nested interface-class declarations.
class_item_qualifier (3 branches)per-branch {kind} (bare)Kind labels: "static" / "protected" / "local". Same bare-{kind} pattern as assignment_operator / inc_or_dec_operator.
class_constraint (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "prototype" / "declaration". Reached from class_item.kind == "constraint".
class_property (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "decl" ({qualifiers, body} — standard form property_qualifier* data_declaration; body is the typed data_declaration shape from SV-Slice-25) / "const" ({qualifiers, data_type, name, init} — kw_const-prefixed form; qualifiers is the typed class_item_qualifier* slot, init is [] when no initializer or [<assign, expr>] when present).
class_method (6 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "task" / "function" ({qualifiers, body} — body is typed task_declaration / function_declaration from SV-Slice-25) / "pure_virtual" ({qualifiers, prototype} — prototype-only, no body; qualifiers is typed class_item_qualifier* slot) / "extern" ({qualifiers, prototype} — prototype-only, kw_extern-prefixed) / "constructor" ({qualifiers, body} — class_constructor_declaration with full body) / "extern_constructor" ({qualifiers, prototype} — extern class new).
method_qualifier (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "virtual" ({pure} — pure is [] for bare virtual, [<kw_pure>] for pure virtual) / "class_item_qualifier" ({body} — body is typed class_item_qualifier shape: static/protected/local). Reached from class_method.qualifiers[].
property_qualifier (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "random" (body is typed random_qualifier: rand/randc) / "class_item_qualifier" (body is typed class_item_qualifier: static/protected/local). Reached from class_property.qualifiers[].
random_qualifier (2 branches)per-branch {kind} (bare)Kind labels: "rand" / "randc". Same bare-{kind} pattern as class_item_qualifier.
concurrent_assertion_statement (5 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "assert_property" / "assume_property" / "cover_property" / "cover_sequence" / "restrict_property". Reached from concurrent_assertion_item.kind == "statement" body.
assert_property_statement-> {spec, action}Drops kw_assert, kw_property, parens. spec is the property_spec; action is the action_block (assert can branch on pass/fail).
assume_property_statement-> {spec, action}Parallel to assert.
cover_property_statement-> {spec, statement}Cover uses statement_or_null instead of action_block (no pass/fail branching).
cover_sequence_statement-> {clocking, disable_iff, sequence, statement}Different from cover_property: covers a sequence_expr with optional clocking_event prefix and optional disable iff (...) clause.
sequence_expr (+ 11 seq_* cascade rules)sequence_expr := seq_or_expr -> $1; operator layers -> {kind, lhs, rest}; seq_unary branches -> {kind: "expression"/"instance"/"paren"/"first_match"/"clocking", …}; seq_delay_expr -> {kind: "delay_head"/"delay_binary", …}; seq_throughout_expr -> {kind: "throughout", condition, body}Since 1.0.148 (SV-0010, H.12.5.8.3.1.1) sequence_expr is an IEEE 1800 §16 (Table 16-3) precedence cascade, replacing the flat directly-left-recursive form that could not parse the infix operators. Loosest→tightest or > and > intersect > within > throughout > ## > unary: each operator layer (seq_or_expr/seq_and_expr/seq_intersect_expr/seq_within_expr) is inner inner_tail inner_tail* emitting {kind:"or"/"and"/"intersect"/"within", lhs, rest:[first_tail, …more_tails]}, or its sole-element passthrough -> $1; seq_throughout_expr is right-assoc expression_or_dist throughout seq_throughout_expr -> {kind:"throughout", condition, body}; seq_delay_expr carries the ## cycle-delay forms (delay_head/delay_binary); seq_unary carries the leaf forms (expression/instance/paren/first_match/clocking). Carrier compatibility: a single-operand sequence (a [*2], first_match(a), x throughout a) is byte-identical to pre-1.0.148 because each cascade level unwraps via -> $1; only the previously-REJECTED infix forms gain the new {kind, lhs, rest} shapes (schema stays 6 — strictly-more-permissive).
property_expr (dispatch + 5 prop_* cascade rules per profile)property_expr := property_expr_sv_2017 -> {kind:"sv_2017", body} | property_expr_sv_2023 -> {kind:"sv_2023", body}; each profile property_expr_sv_<p> := prop_until_sv_<p> -> $1 over prop_until > prop_iff > prop_or > prop_and > prop_primary; infix layers -> {kind:"until"/"s_until"/"until_with"/"s_until_with"/"iff"/"or"/"and", lhs, rhs}; prop_primary branches the unary/base kinds (sequence/strong/weak/paren/not/nexttime*/always*/eventually*/accept_on-family/if/case/imp_minus/imp_assign/sequence_or_assign/instance/clocking)Since 1.0.149 (SV-0011, H.12.5.8.3.2) the per-profile property_expr_sv_2017/property_expr_sv_2023 are an IEEE 1800 §16 (Table 16-3) binary-infix precedence cascade (the property-layer dual of the 1.0.148 sequence cascade), replacing the flat directly-left-recursive form that could not parse the property infix operators until/s_until/until_with/s_until_with/iff (and or/and over property operands). Loosest→tightest until-family > iff > or > and > primary, all right-associative inline head op self (so e.g. a until b iff c → until(a, iff(b,c)); a and b or c → or(and(a,b), c)). Carrier compatibility: every previously-VALID property parse is byte-identical — each cascade level unwraps via -> $1, the nested {kind:"sv_2017"/"sv_2023"} dispatch wrapper is preserved (prop_primary bodies still reference property_expr), and prop_primary is byte-identical; the newly-parsing infix forms reuse the EXISTING {kind, lhs, rhs} carriers (schema stays 6 — strictly-more-permissive, no carrier change). Documented limitation: the tight prefix ops not/nexttime/s_nexttime (level 6) keep pre-fix dispatch-body precedence, so not a until b → not (a until b) (unchanged from pre-fix).
restrict_property_statement-> {spec}No action — restrict prunes formal traces but doesn’t branch on outcome.
expect_property_statement-> {spec, action}Same shape as assert.
constraint_block-> {items: $2}Drops braces. items is the constraint_block_item* iteration.
constraint_block_item (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "solve_before" ({before, after} — drops kw_solve / kw_before / semi) / "expression" ({body} — wraps a constraint_expression).
constraint_declaration_sv_2017-> {static_keyword, name, block}static_keyword is [] or [<kw_static>].
constraint_declaration_sv_2023-> {static_keyword, dynamic_override, name, block}Adds dynamic_override slot per LRM 2023, parallel to function/task.
constraint_expression (6 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "expression" ({soft, expr} — soft is [] or [<kw_soft>]) / "uniqueness" ({body}) / "implies" ({condition, body} — expression implies constraint_set) / "if" ({condition, then_body, else_clause} — else_clause is [] or [<kw_else, set>]) / "foreach" ({array, loop_vars, body}) / "disable_soft" ({target}).
constraint_prototype_sv_2017-> {qualifier, static_keyword, name}qualifier is the optional ( constraint_prototype_qualifier )? (typed).
constraint_prototype_sv_2023-> {qualifier, static_keyword, dynamic_override, name}Same as sv_2017 plus dynamic_override.
constraint_prototype_qualifier (2 branches)per-branch {kind} (bare)Kind labels: "extern" / "pure".
constraint_set (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "single" ({body} — wraps a single constraint_expression) / "block" ({exprs} — brace-delimited list of constraint_expressions).
deferred_immediate_assertion_item-> {label, body}label is the optional ( block_identifier colon )? prefix per LRM A.6.10 (parallel to concurrent_assertion_item.label from SV-Slice-24).
deferred_immediate_assertion_statement (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "assert" / "assume" / "cover".
deferred_immediate_assert_statement (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "zero_delay" ({expression, action} — assert #0 (expr) action_block; LRM 1800-2017 §16.3.1 Re-NBA evaluation) / "final" ({expression, action} — assert final (expr) action_block; end-of-simulation evaluation).
deferred_immediate_assume_statement (2 branches)per-branch typedSame 2 kinds and shape as deferred_immediate_assert_statement (with kw_assume instead of kw_assert).
deferred_immediate_cover_statement (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "zero_delay" / "final" (parallel to assert/assume). Uses statement (statement_or_null) instead of action since cover has no pass/fail branching.
action_block (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "always" ({body} — runs unconditionally; LRM A.6.3 single statement_or_null form) / "with_else" ({pass, fail} — [statement] else statement_or_null form; pass is [] if pass-statement omitted, like assert (x) else $error(...)).
statement-> {label: $1, attributes: $2, body: $3}label is optional ( block_identifier colon !colon )? — the !colon lookahead distinguishes block label from :: package-scope-resolution. body is a typed statement_item.
statement_or_null (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "statement" ({body}) / "null" ({attributes} — bare ; with optional preceding attribute_instance*).
function_statement_or_null (2 branches)per-branch typedSame shape as statement_or_null but for function bodies.
tf_item_declaration (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "block_item" / "tf_port". Reached from function_body_declaration.items[] and task_body_declaration.items[].
statement_item_sv_2017 (20 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "blocking_assignment" / "nonblocking_assignment" / "procedural_continuous_assignment" (each drops trailing semi) / "case" / "conditional" / "inc_or_dec_expression" (drops semi; sv_2017-only) / "subroutine_call" / "disable" / "event_trigger" / "loop" / "jump" / "par_block" / "procedural_timing_control" / "seq_block" / "wait" / "procedural_assertion" / "clocking_drive" (drops semi) / "randsequence" / "randcase" / "expect_property". Reached from statement.body.
statement_item_sv_2023 (19 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Same 19 kinds as sv_2017 except "inc_or_dec_expression" is removed — LRM 2023 subsumes the semantics into blocking_assignment with ++/-- operators.
block_item_declaration (4 branches)per-branch {kind, attributes, body}Kind labels: "block_data" / "local_parameter" / "parameter" / "let". Each preserves leading attribute_instance* prefix. Reached from tf_item_declaration.kind == "block_item".
disable_statement (3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "task" ({target}) / "block" ({target}) / "fork" (bare). Reached from statement_item.kind == "disable".
jump_statement (3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "return" ({value} — value is [] for bare return; or [<expr>] for return expr;) / "break" (bare) / "continue" (bare).
wait_statement (3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "wait" ({condition, body}) / "wait_fork" (bare) / "wait_order" ({events: [$3, $4::2*], action} — wait order(e1, e2, …, eN) action_block; flat array of hierarchical_identifier values per slice 58 audit).
event_trigger (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Dispatches the active profile’s event-trigger rule: "sv_2017" / "sv_2023" / "verilog_2005". (SV-0023 / schema 16: was 2 branches — the verilog_2005 body is new.)
event_trigger_sv_2017 (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels (IEEE 1800-2017 §15.5 / A.6.5): "blocking" ({name} — -> name;, the blocking named-event trigger) / "non_blocking" ({control, name} — ->> [delay_or_event_control] name;, the nonblocking trigger; control is [] for ->> name;). SV-0023 / schema 16 corrected the previously SWAPPED labels and added the ->> token.
event_trigger_sv_2023 (2 branches)per-branch typedSame 2 kinds as sv_2017 plus a trailing select field per branch (IEEE 1800-2023 Annex A nonrange_select extension) — so -> e[0]; / ->> e[0]; carry the array index.
event_trigger_verilog_2005 (1 branch)typedKind "blocking" ({name, select} — IEEE 1364-2005 A.6.5 -> hei { [ expression ] } ;; select is the bit_select array-index chain, [] for a plain -> e;). No ->> (SystemVerilog-only). New at SV-0023 / schema 16 — closes the 1364-2005 event-array-trigger accept-gap.
procedural_timing_control_statement-> {control: $1, body: $2}Standard timing-controlled statement form: <control> statement_or_null. Reached from statement_item.kind == "procedural_timing_control".
procedural_timing_control (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "delay" (#N delay) / "event" (@(…) event) / "cycle" (##N cycle delay).
subroutine_call (5 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "class_scoped_tf" ({body}) / "tf" ({body}) / "system_tf" ({body} — $display etc.) / "method" ({body}) / "randomize" ({std_scope, body} — std_scope is [] for plain randomize, [<kw_std, ::>] for std::randomize).
subroutine_call_statement (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "call" ({body} — wraps subroutine_call with trailing ;) / "void_cast" ({body} — void'(func_call); discards return value).
seq_block-> {label, declarations, statements, end_label}Drops kw_begin / kw_end. label is optional ( colon block_identifier )? (e.g., begin : my_block).
par_block-> {label, declarations, statements, join, end_label}Same as seq_block plus join field carrying the typed join_keyword (discriminates join / join_any / join_none per SV-Slice-7).
case_statement (3 branches; schema 31)plain -> {unique_priority, keyword, expr, items: {first, rest}}; matches -> {kind: "matches", unique_priority, keyword, expr, items: {first, rest}}; inside -> {kind: "inside", unique_priority, keyword: {kind: "case"}, expr, items: {first, rest}}IEEE 1800-2017 A.6.7’s three productions. Drops kw_endcase and parens. keyword is the typed case_keyword (case/casez/casex); on the inside form — which A.6.7 admits only with the case keyword — it is the literal {kind: "case"} node. items.first / items.rest hold case_item nodes on the plain form, case_pattern_item nodes on matches, case_inside_item nodes on inside. Since 1.0.219 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.45) the matches and inside forms are typed; through 1.0.218 they were the raw nine-element envelope (16 + 15 in the sv_2017 corpus). The plain form is byte-identical (kind absent = plain). unique_priority is [] or the typed unique_priority node.
case_keyword (3 branches)per-branch {kind} (bare)Kind labels: "case" / "casez" / "casex".
case_item (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "expr_list" ({exprs: [$1, $2::2*], body} — flat array of case_item_expression labels per slice 58 audit) / "default" ({body} — drops kw_default and optional colon).
property_case_item (2 branches; schema 31)expression arm -> {expressions: [$1, $2::2*], body: $4}; default arm -> {kind: "default", body: $3}IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.10, the arms of a case property expression (property_expr’s {kind: "case", expr, items}). Since 1.0.219 (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.45) the default arm is typed — the shape case_item / case_pattern_item / case_inside_item_sv_2017 already give theirs; through 1.0.218 it was the raw four-element envelope. The corpus writes no property case item on any lane; the two control_property_case_*.sv pins and the shape-contract sample hold the rule. The expression arm is byte-identical (kind absent).
case_pattern_item (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "pattern" ({pattern, condition, body} — condition is the optional &&& expression guard per LRM A.6.7.1) / "default" ({body}).
case_inside_item_sv_2017 (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "range_list" ({ranges, body} — ranges is open_range_list) / "default" ({body}).
case_inside_item_sv_2023 (2 branches)per-branch typedSame kind labels as sv_2017; ranges field uses LRM 2023 range_list (simplified naming).
loop_statement (6 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "forever" ({body}) / "repeat" ({count, body}) / "while" ({condition, body}) / "for" ({init, condition, step, body} — each of init/condition/step is [] when omitted) / "do_while" ({body, condition}) / "foreach" ({array, loop_vars, body} — body is a typed statement, not statement_or_null since bare ; not allowed).
conditional_statement-> {unique_priority, condition, then_body, else_body}Drops kw_if / lparen / rparen / kw_else. condition is typed cond_predicate (raw envelope still). then_body is a typed statement_or_null. else_body is a typed conditional_else_branch (helper rule). The rule preserves a &kw_else positive lookahead before consuming kw_else — PEG idiom from the source grammar.
conditional_else_branch (NEW; 2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "elseif" (recursive — body is itself a typed conditional_statement; supports else if (...) ... chains) / "else" (terminal — body is a typed statement_or_null). Helper rule extracted from inline ( conditional_statement | statement_or_null ) to dodge task #38.
nonblocking_assignment-> {lvalue, control, value}Drops <=. control is [] for a <= b;, [<delay_or_event_control shape>] for a <= #1 b;.
procedural_continuous_assignment (6 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "assign" ({body} — kw_assign + variable_assignment) / "deassign" ({target}) / "force_variable" ({body}) / "force_net" ({body}) / "release_variable" ({target}) / "release_net" ({target}). The split between force/release variants reflects the grammar’s separate variable_assignment vs net_assignment / variable_lvalue vs net_lvalue branches.
clocking_drive-> {lvalue, cycle_delay, value}Drops <=. cycle_delay is the optional ( cycle_delay )? slot (clocking-block specific delay).
randcase_statement-> {items: {first: $2, rest: $3}}Drops kw_randcase / kw_endcase. Mini-mixed-array on items.
randcase_item-> {weight: $1, body: $3}Drops colon. weight is the relative selection weight expression.
procedural_assertion_statement (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "concurrent" (typed in SV-Slice-29) / "immediate" (typed in this slice — bridges to immediate_assertion_statement) / "checker_instantiation" (raw envelope still).
immediate_assertion_statement (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "simple" (raw envelope still — simple_immediate_assertion_statement to be typed in a future slice) / "deferred" (typed in SV-Slice-30 — deferred_immediate_assertion_statement).
variable_assignment-> {lvalue, value}Drops assign. Reached from procedural_continuous_assignment.kind == "assign" and from force_variable.
blocking_assignment_sv_2017 (4 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "delay_assign" ({lvalue, delay, value} — lvalue = #N expr;) / "dynamic_array_new" ({lvalue, value} — lvalue = new[size];) / "class_new" ({scope, name, select, value} — [scope.]name[select] = new(args);; scope uses NEW helper rule) / "operator" ({body} — wraps operator_assignment for += / *= / etc.).
blocking_assignment_sv_2023 (5 branches)per-branch typedSame 4 kinds as sv_2017 plus "inc_or_dec" ({body} — LRM 2023 folds ++ / -- into blocking_assignment; in sv_2017 these were a separate inc_or_dec_expression semi statement_item branch).
class_or_package_scope (NEW; 3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "instance" ({handle} — implicit_class_handle dot prefix, typically this. / super.) / "class_scope" ({body} — ClassName::) / "package_scope" ({body} — pkg::). Helper rule extracted from inline ( implicit_class_handle dot | class_scope | package_scope )? to dodge task #38. 4th use of the helper-rule extraction pattern.
randsequence_statement_sv_2017-> {start, productions: {first, rest}}Drops kw_randsequence, parens, kw_endsequence. start is [] for randsequence () ..., [<production_identifier>] for randsequence (top) .... productions is mini-mixed-array (first + rest).

production_sv_2017-> {return_type, name, ports, rules: [$5, $6::2*]}Drops colon and trailing semi. return_type is the optional data_type_or_void prefix. ports is the optional ( lparen tf_port_list rparen )? slot. rules is a flat array of rs_rule shapes (slice 58 audit dropped the bitwise_or separators).
production_item_sv_2017-> {name, args}args is the optional ( lparen list_of_arguments rparen )? slot — [] for plain reference, [<arg list>] when invoking with arguments.
rs_case-> {expr, items: {first, rest}}Drops kw_case / kw_endcase / parens.
rs_case_item_sv_2017 (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "expr_list" ({exprs: [$1, $2::2*], body} per slice 58 audit) / "default" ({body}).

rs_if_else_sv_2017-> {condition, then_body, else_body}else_body is [] for if-without-else, [<production_item>] when present.
rs_if_else_sv_2023-> {condition, then_body, else_body}Parallel; uses rs_production_item.

rs_production_list_sv_2017 (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "productions" ({items: {first, rest}} — simple rs_prod sequence) / "rand_join" ({join_count, items: {first, second, rest}} — rand join [(expr)] prod1 prod2 [prod3...]; per LRM A.6.13 at least 2 production_items required).
rs_production_list_sv_2023 (2 branches)per-branch typedSame kinds; rand_join uses rs_production_item.
rs_repeat_sv_2017-> {count, body}Drops kw_repeat / parens.
rs_repeat_sv_2023-> {count, body}Parallel; uses rs_production_item.

rs_weight_specification_sv_2023 (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "number" (integral_number) / "identifier" (ps_identifier) / "expression" (parenthesized expression).
simple_immediate_assertion_statement (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "assert" / "assume" / "cover". Reached from immediate_assertion_statement.kind == "simple".

simple_immediate_assume_statement-> {condition, action}Parallel to assert.
simple_immediate_cover_statement-> {condition, statement}Uses statement_or_null instead of action_block (cover has no pass/fail branching).
inc_or_dec_expression (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "prefix" ({op, attributes, lvalue} — ++a / --a) / "postfix" ({lvalue, attributes, op} — a++ / a--). The attributes slot carries inline attribute_instance* (LRM allows attributes between operator and operand).
weight_specification_sv_2017 (3 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "number" / "identifier" / "expression". Parallel to rs_weight_specification_sv_2023.
data_type (15 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "integer_vector" ({base, signing, dims} — bit/logic/reg with optional signing + packed dims) / "integer_atom" ({base, signing} — byte/shortint/int/longint/integer/time) / "non_integer" ({base} — shortreal/real/realtime) / "struct_union" ({header, packed_signing, members: {first, rest}, dims} — Category C, kept as-is) / "enum" ({base_type, names: [$4, $5::2*], dims} — slice 58 audit applied to the enum_name_declaration list) / "string" / "chandle" / "event" (bare; no body) / "virtual_interface" ({interface_keyword, name, params, modport}) / "scoped_data_type" / "known_unscoped_data_type" / "class_type" / "provisional_class_type" / "covergroup" / "type_reference" (each {body}).
data_type_or_implicit (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "data_type" / "implicit".
data_type_or_void (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "data_type" ({body}) / "void" (bare).
data_type_or_incomplete_class_scoped_type_sv_2023 (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "data_type" / "incomplete_class_scoped".

unpacked_dimension / unpacked_dimension_size_sv_only (since 1.0.222, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.50){kind: "range", body: $2} on the range alternative; the size alternative passes the helper’s {kind: "expression", body: $2} through (-> $1)An unpacked dimension: [ a : b ] on every profile ({kind: "range"}); the IEEE 1800 SIZE form [ N ] ({kind: "expression"}) on sv_2017 / sv_2023 alone — the helper unpacked_dimension_size_sv_only is @profiles-gated, so under verilog_2005 (IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.5 dimension / range are [ a : b ] alone) the size form REJECTS at the [. The node a consumer reads is unchanged by the split: the dispatcher adds no wrapper.

integer_type (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "vector" / "atom".

expression_base (3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "tagged_union" ({body}) / "operand_chain" ({first, rest} — the operator chain: rest is one expression_chain_step per operator, in source order; precedence is the consumer’s, per IEEE 1800-2017 Table 11-2) / "paren_op_assign" ({body}).
expression_chain_step (2 branches, unannotated)passthroughOne step of the operand chain. A BINARY step passes through as the three-element array [<binary_operator {kind}>, [<attribute_instance …>], <expression_operand>] (unchanged since SV-Slice-46); an INSIDE step is the inside_operator object. A consumer discriminates by JSON type — array = binary operator with its right operand, object = the set-membership operator with its set — and applies Table 11-2 to the flat sequence, where inside { … } is a postfix operator on the relational row (< <= > >= inside): [b, &, a, inside{…}] groups as b & (a inside {…}), [a, +, b, inside{…}] as (a + b) inside {…}.
expression_operand (3 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "unary" ({op, attributes, primary}) / "inc_or_dec" ({body}) / "primary" ({body}).

constant_expression_operand (2 branches)per-branch typedKind labels: "unary" ({op, attributes, primary}) / "primary" ({body}).
inside_operator (2 branches)per-branch {kind, body}Kind labels: "sv_2017" / "sv_2023" — the profile arm that parsed the set. Schema 27 (release 1.0.213): replaces inside_expression ({expr, ranges}, whose expr grouped the WHOLE left chain — b & a inside {…} read as (b & a) inside {…}, against Table 11-2). The left operand is now the chain to the element’s left, so the node carries no expr.
inside_operator_sv_2017 / inside_operator_sv_2023-> {kind: "inside", ranges}The inside { range_list } set per LRM A.8.3 inside_expression ::= expression inside { open_range_list } (2023: range_list). sv_2017 ranges is the typed open_range_list; sv_2023 the typed range_list. The kind: "inside" discriminator is what the pins’ arm claim operand_chain>inside reads.
conditional_expression-> {predicate, attributes, then_expr, else_expr}Ternary ? : form. The &question positive lookahead is preserved unchanged from source grammar.

paren_operator_assignment_operand / expression_chain_operand (since 1.0.224, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.53){kind: "paren_op_assign", body: $2} on the operand; expression_chain_operand passes its alternative through (-> $1)A parenthesised operator assignment (IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.3 ( operator_assignment ), §11.4.2) wherever an expression operand stands: at the base of an expression it is the expression_base node it has been since schema 26; since 1.0.224 it also appears as the first slot of an operand_chain ((i = i - 1) + 1) and as the third element of a chain step’s [operator, attributes, operand] triple (1 + (i = i - 1)). SV profiles only: IEEE 1364-2005 has no assignment inside an expression, so under verilog_2005 the form rejects at its =. The expression_chain_operand dispatcher is ordered (a primary first, the assignment form only where the primary fails — the two are disjoint) and adds no node.
string_literal / string_literal_sv_2017 / string_literal_sv_2023 / string_literal_v2005 (since 1.0.221, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.47){kind: "double_quoted", body: $2} on every double-quoted twin; {kind: "triple_quoted", body: $2} on the sv_2023 twin’s """…""" alternativeThe string literal, one twin per edition (the SELECTION-dispatcher pattern) because the three standards disagree: IEEE 1800-2017 / 1800-2023 §5.9 admit a \ + newline CONTINUATION inside a string and refuse a bare newline; IEEE 1364-2005 §3.6 / A.8.8 refuse both; IEEE 1800-2023 §5.9 adds the TRIPLE-QUOTED string ("""…""", any character except \ inside — a bare " and a bare newline included, escapes as \ + any character). body is the SOURCE TEXT verbatim, quotes excluded, continuation included: §5.9 says the backslash and the newline are ignored, which is the consumer’s reading, not a rewrite of the source. Through 1.0.220 one terminal served every profile and REJECTED the continuation (the regex crate’s . cannot match a newline) while ADMITTING a raw newline; the triple_quoted kind is an addition reachable only on text no earlier release accepted, so schema 32 is unchanged.
integral_number / integral_number_leading_zero_size_sv_2023 (since 1.0.251, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.47)the terminal’s text, carried by number as {kind: "integral", body} on every alternative — the twin returns -> $1, so a leading-zero size yields the SAME node shapeThe SIZE token split by edition: IEEE 1800-2023 §5.7 Syntax 5-2 / A.8.7 read size ::= unsigned_number (docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-5-lexical-conventions.md:213, docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:3200; the edition defines no non_zero_unsigned_number), so 01'b0 / 007'h5 parse under sv_2023 and sv_2023_tolerant; IEEE 1800-2017 §5.7 / A.8.7 and 1364-2005 §3.5 / A.8.7 read size ::= non_zero_unsigned_number, so sv_2017 and verilog_2005 reject them. A ZERO size (0'b1, 0_'b1) is rejected on every profile — 1800-2023’s §5.7.1 prose keeps it “a nonzero unsigned decimal number”. body is the source text, leading zeros kept; the value is the same number. Not a member of the opt-in tolerance list: standard text under its edition.
parameter_port_list / parameter_port_list_sv_only / parameter_port_list_v2005 / parameter_port_declaration_v2005 (since 1.0.252, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.48)the dispatcher passes its twin through (-> $1); the sv_only twin is the shipped rule’s six kinds (mixed_string / mixed / type_only / declarations / list_then_decls / empty); the verilog_2005 twin renders {kind: "declarations", items} only, each item the shared parameter_port_declaration node (-> $2 behind a parameter lookahead)The parameter port list split by edition: IEEE 1364-2005 A.1.3 module_parameter_port_list ::= # ( parameter_declaration { , parameter_declaration } ) (docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:38; A.2.1.1 :126-128) against IEEE 1800-2017 A.1.3 (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md:231-243). Under verilog_2005 a declaration without parameter, a localparam in the list and #() are refused from 1.0.252 (ledger SV-0137); a legal tree is byte-identical to 1.0.251’s.
