The release ceremony — every gate a grammar revision runs on its final bytes

⭐ Why this list lives here. Until 2026-09-04 the ceremony existed only as the previous release’s task-leaf record, copied forward — and a list copied from the previous record copies its omissions. sv_syntax_closure_gate was missing from two consecutive ceremonies (1.0.207 and 1.0.208); the contract it guards was left diverging by 1.0.207 and its staleness budget (twenty commits touching declared inputs) was crossed at 1.0.208, which is how SV-CORPUS-GRAD.16 found it. The gates below are the durable list; a release record cites this section and runs every item on the FINAL bytes, each under the memory guard, sequentially.

  1. Grammar, before a byte is generated: ast_pipeline --lint-grammar rc 0; --report-sample-parity defects=0; the interpreter on every reproducer pin (defect pins flip, controls do not); typed AST byte-identity on the controls where the change is shape-neutral.
  2. Regenerate and build: make focus_systemverilog, the debug ast_pipeline, the release parseability_probe (≈20 min, peak ≈12 GB — in the background, under the guard). ⛔ Then, the moment they are built, bash scripts/sv_ceremony_binaries.sh snapshot rust/target/svNN: the three binaries are copied into the scratch directory with their digests and parser fingerprints (bin/identity.tsv, sha_final.txt). Later items REBUILD the published paths — verilog_2005_conformance_gate the release probe, the parity / equivalence gates and the lib suite the debug pair — and a rebuild is not byte-reproducible on this host, so a tracked report would name a binary that no longer exists (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.52, 2026-10-09: the debug probe the three pipeline readings named was gone and the readings had to be re-run; the lowmem copy saved the release identity). The chain therefore runs … restore rust/target/svNN before every measuring step that follows such a gate and as its LAST step, and … verify rust/target/svNN at the end — the RED arm: the copies, the published paths, every tracked report’s parse binary row and the store-gate memo must all name the ceremony’s bytes (.53). ⛔ The published paths stay the ONLY paths a tracked artifact may name: the lane runner adopts the recorded probe path on its next run, and a scratch path is gone within a week.
  3. Pins: python3 stimuli/sv/run_adjudication_repros.py → failures=0, with every class=defect row flipped to fixed the day it parses.
  4. Corpus, all three lanes, per path and two-sided: stimuli/run_external_corpus.sh sv 60 8 0, sv2005 60 8 0 and sv2023 60 8 0 — pass → fail 0, every moved row named; the adjudicator’s manifests for all three lanes (adjudication_manifest{,_v2005,_sv2023}.tsv), their summaries and the store-gate memo (its key: file sha, binary sha, instrument digest — its binary column is held to the lane report by store_gate_explanations.py --check-identity, the store-gate bank’s A13 arm on every commit, and a run that publishes anything but the tracked manifest writes its memo beside its own manifest, never the tracked one, .53). ⛔ Run the adjudicator, then the parity derivation (docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/sv2023_lane/production_parity.py --write), then the adjudicator AGAIN: the sv_2023 lane’s carry-over of a NEW 2017 clause pin reads the parity artifact, and the parity artifact reads the manifest’s new citation — one pass leaves the row re-read is owed for a commit (.53 found three such rows from .52; CORPUS-KEY-INTEGRITY tier A5 holds the pair to agree on every commit, .54); the sv_2017 × sv_2023 verdict census (docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/sv2023_lane/census.py, an identity carrier — 2017_only_pass must stay 0: nothing legal under 2017 may be lost under 2023). And the PIPELINE lane, both readings, whenever the parser or the preprocessor moved: stimuli/run_pipeline_lane.sh all (the primary sv_2017 reading, its report and re-adjudication), then the same command under PGEN_PIPELINE_PROFILE=sv_2023 and the two-edition pipeline census (docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/pipeline_sv2023_lane/census.py, an identity carrier too — it refuses unless both readings came from one binary, and its 2017_only_pass must stay 0 as well).
  5. Certificates: sv_cert_recognized_union_gate and verilog_2005_conformance_gate on the adjudicated contracts (counts by name in rebaseline_note / baseline_note; each re-stamps its identity when GREEN).
  6. Syntax closure: sv_syntax_closure_gate — the entry-scoped unreachable-rule SET must equal the contract’s allow-list; a rule newly unreachable is adjudicated (dead → delete it in a grammar slice, or list it with a measured reason), never suppressed.
  7. Shape and reproducibility: ast_shape_contract_gate; check_generated_reproducibility.sh --rebaseline (every family re-derives byte-identically); clippy_on_rust_change when Rust moved.
  8. Parse cost: sv_parse_cost_family_share FIRST, then sv_parse_cost_rebaseline, then sv_parse_cost_ratchet; a rise is accepted only under a coded invariant with a row in accepted_rises.tsv, and the LR-family share’s anchors move with the share.
  9. Downstream derivations: dark audit + dark worklist, verdict coverage, key provenance, the two keyword censuses (--write), check_corpus_key_integrity.sh, check_identity_carriers.sh, sv_ceremony_binaries.sh verify rust/target/svNN (item 2’s RED arm, after the last restore), check_sv_corpus_denominator.sh, report_family_status.sh --check-all (re-splice the derived blocks), report_grammar_certification.sh --markdown (re-splice the per-grammar certification table — GRAMMAR-CERT-CURRENCY refuses when its inputs lead the table by more than ten commits, which is how 1.0.209’s commit found two ceremonies had skipped it), systemverilog_parser_book_gate (rebuilds the tracked HTML). ⛔ And the RULE-FIRE CENSUS: when the release moved the grammar’s rule inventory (ast_pipeline --dump-rule-profiles’s rule_count, a rule added or deleted), tier 2 of the partition doctrine is re-derived on the final bytes — make -C rust SHELL=/bin/bash sv_rule_fire_partition (corpus census ~3 min + certificate pass ~5 min) — and every rule the certificate pass leaves unwitnessed is adjudicated with a measured construct before the commit; check_sv_rule_fire_partition.sh’s tier 1 refuses a census whose rule set is not the inventory’s, so a census taken on an older grammar cannot ride a release (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.22: the tracked census had named rules deleted 23 releases earlier and lacked 218 the grammar defined, and the doctrine stayed green).
  10. Ceremony documents, in lockstep: the revision register row (digest → release → ledger id), the released-parser bug ledger row, the integration contract (current-state note, version, history, digest), this book’s changelog, the platform book’s anchors, the task leaf with its acceptance checklist, docs/TASK_TREE.md, MEMORY.md, CHANGES.md. ⛔ The register row of the commit being made is written PENDING — the ONE row that may say so — and the FIRST thing the commit after a release does is back-fill the previous row with its sha: tier A of scripts/check_sv_contract_currency.sh refuses a committed PENDING row from the next doctrines run on (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.23, 2026-09-24; it had read only (pending) and never fired). ⛔ The digest those rows carry is ONE command’s output — bash scripts/check_baseline_identity.sh --digest ebnf_raw_ast grammars/systemverilog.ebnf — because the identity carriers, the keyword-faithfulness census and the register’s back-fill tripwire all read that digester; a hand-rolled sha256 over an --emit-raw-ast-json dump serializes the same envelope differently and does not match it (.3.66 drafted such a digest and the carriers refused it before it was published). ⭐ And the release’s LAST lockstep step is the distance: bash scripts/report_sv_release_distance.sh --record <release> appends the release’s row to the history and --markdown republishes the block on the status page, so the SV-RELEASE-DISTANCE-CURRENCY doctrine reads the tree it describes (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.25).
  11. The family umbrellas, on the same final bytes (since 1.0.243, in post chain A2; recorded here by SV-CORPUS-GRAD.24, 2026-09-24): annotation_differential_parity_gate, return_parity_gate, stimuli_module_parity_gate, rtl_const_expr_cert_gate, regex_formal_exhaustive_closure_gate, vhdl_formal_exhaustive_closure_gate, sv_formal_exhaustive_closure_gate, sv_preprocessor_formal_exhaustive_closure_gate, sv_preprocessor_reachability_closure_gate, sv_preprocessor_syntax_closure_gate, and — since SV-CORPUS-GRAD.35, 2026-09-29 — sv_stimuli_quality_gate (≈ 30 min: the closed-loop residual ratchet whose pin of 0 nothing had run against between 2026-08-08 and 2026-09-29, during which the census it reads counted parser assertions as generation targets and would have read 20 / 20 on both profiles) — the SV done-bar’s SECOND leg reads gates green and invoked over exactly these, and .24 found three of them RED for months because no release chain ran them. A RED here is one of two things and the record says which: a condition already owned by name (today: none — ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.119 and the SV register row (DONE-BAR.5e) were the two routed by 1.0.247’s run and both closed on 2026-10-02 with the SV formal umbrella reading ✅ … passed on ad6e02a45; the umbrella’s external-corpus surface on UVM’s const local … = new(…) was the owned condition from 2026-09-04 until 1.0.247; the envelope divergence GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.20.3 named on 2026-09-24 closed the same day), or a NEW defect, routed the same day with its measured line. A RED that is neither blocks the release.
  12. Before the commit: bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh (every registered doctrine, incl. BASELINE-IDENTITY, which refuses a contract whose declared inputs moved beyond its budget) and bash scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh.
  13. The library test suite under the full feature set, on the same final bytes (since SV-CORPUS-GRAD.34, 2026-09-29; in post chain A2, beside the family umbrellas): cd rust && cargo test --features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run" --lib — every unit test, ≈ 4 min once the test binary is built (1 310 tests today), under the memory guard. ⛔ Why a release gate and not a developer courtesy: several unit tests pin the REAL grammar — the class-B reach-plan test witness_branch_plan_forces_quantifier_on_real_systemverilog_class_b_target names a rule, a node path and a branch of grammars/systemverilog.ebnf so that a restructure which moves the site fails there rather than silently in a gate stage — and no other gate runs them. Measured: that test was red from 1.0.215 (.3.42 lifted the inline group it named into nonrange_lvalue_scope) through 1.0.246 — twenty releases, each ceremony green, found by an engine leaf’s own suite run 22 days later. A red test blocks the release. A test that no longer describes the grammar is re-derived on the measurement (the two vintages’ --emit-raw-ast-json dumps, PGEN_REACH_PATH_DUMP=1’s REFUSED: line naming the node that stands at the path), never re-pinned by hand; a red test that describes the grammar correctly is a grammar defect and is fixed in the grammar.

Future major version

A schema 1.0.0 milestone will land when the SV annotation campaign completes — that is, when every rule in grammars/systemverilog.ebnf carries either a return annotation or a deliberate decision to remain raw envelope. At that point all shape definitions move to Tier 2 (locked) and no further default fall-through changes are expected.

The campaign is in early phase; reaching schema 1.0.0 is on the order of months of slice work.

Glossary

Terms used throughout this book.

AST envelope

The JSON tree that parse_grammar_profile_ast_dump_named returns. See AST Envelope Structure.

AST shape contract manifest

The file rust/test_data/ast_shape_contract/systemverilog_v1.json. Records per-rule expected JSON shape for each entry in the test corpus. Drift in the AST dump fails a cargo test regression-lock test, surfacing the change.

Annotation campaign

The systematic effort to add return annotations (-> ...) to grammar rules in grammars/systemverilog.ebnf. Each slice annotates one rule (or a small family) and bumps the schema version. The regex parser campaign (42+ slices) is the model for the SV campaign.

ParseContent

The internal AST-pipeline representation used by PGEN’s parser hooks and codegen. Variants include Terminal, Sequence, Quantified, Or, Alternative, Json. See Parse Content Variants.

parseability_probe

The CLI wrapper around pgen::embedding_api used for terminal-side verification, AST inspection, and bug-report reproducers. 4 sub-commands: --supports, --parse, --parse-dump-ast, --parse-dump-ast-pretty. See the parseability_probe CLI Reference for the full flag set, exit codes, output formats, and registered grammars.

Profile

A named configuration of the grammar that selects which top-level entry rule to start parsing from, and which profile-gated rules are active. SV profiles: sv_2017, sv_2023, verilog_2005, and — opt-in, since 1.0.249 — sv_2023_tolerant (sv_2023 plus a closed list of five simulator-tolerated spellings — four since 1.0.249, the fifth since 1.0.250; see Tool tolerance). The three edition profiles are strict; nothing selects the tolerant one unless the caller names it. The accepted request spellings on top of the canonical names (2017/ieee1800-2017/ieee_1800_2017 → sv_2017, the 2023 group → sv_2023, the 1364-2005 group → verilog_2005) are declared by the grammar itself via @profile_alias in grammars/systemverilog.ebnf (since PROFILE-ALIAS.2, 2026-07-07) — the generated parser carries them in its GRAMMAR_PROFILE_ALIASES constant and resolves them case-insensitively inside set_grammar_profile, so every entry point (CLI, registry, embedding) accepts the same spellings. An undeclared spelling passes through un-coerced and simply matches no @profiles list.

verilog_2005 (aliases 1364-2005 / ieee1364-2005 / ieee_1364_2005; introduced parser-side by VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.2, embedding API 1.3.0) is a strict IEEE 1364-2005 (Verilog) parsing profile on the SystemVerilog grammar: shared core constructs ride the sv_2017 baseline, and SystemVerilog-only constructs are rejected. It is realized purely by @profiles: [...] gating on the one grammar — no separate parser. The profile is built to wellformedness coherence (--lint-grammar reports 0 verilog_2005 profile-orphans): the Verilog-2005 core is admitted to the sv_2017 baseline variants, the SV-only surface (classes, packages, interfaces, programs, assertions, covergroups, constraints, clocking, checkers, DPI, typedef, ++/--, jump statements, final, SV-only integer atom types, unique/priority, …) is whole-rule gated out, and keyword reservation is profile-faithful (the IEEE 1364-2005 Annex B keyword set is reserved under verilog_2005, while SV-only reserved words such as logic/class/typedef/int parse as ordinary identifiers). So module m; endmodule and wire logic; (a net named logic) parse under --profile verilog_2005 while class C; endclass, int x;, logic x;, initial assert (1);, always_comb q = 1'b0;, do … while (…);, foreach (a[i]) …, shortreal r;, interconnect w;, wait fork;, task t (ref integer a);, and -> #5 e; are rejected (each still accepted under sv_2017/sv_2023). The bare-keyword SV-only alternatives inside shared core rules are gated via shape-preserving named lifts (always_keyword_sv_only, loop_statement_sv_only, integer_vector_type_sv_only, non_integer_type_sv_only, net_port_type_interconnect_sv_only, interconnect_net_declaration_sv_only, port_direction_sv_only, tf_port_direction_const_ref_sv_only, wait_statement_sv_only, event_trigger_control_sv_only), plus a whole-rule gate on interface_port_header — the sv_2017/sv_2023 ASTs are byte-identical to before, so no release/schema bump. The profile’s repo-standard conformance surface (landed by VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.4.3) is make -C rust SHELL=/bin/bash verilog_2005_conformance_gate: against the tracked contract rust/test_data/grammar_quality/verilog_2005_conformance_contract_v0.json it asserts the --lint-grammar 0-profile-orphan lock, the curated 12-accept + 34-reject corpus (rust/test_data/grammar_quality/verilog_2005_conformance/) as a full per-file × per-profile matrix (138 checks across all three profiles + 2 alias-normalization probes), and the profiled certificate-coverage baseline (--grammar-profile verilog_2005: total=1138 proof=2 witness=826 UNKNOWN=310, sample_parse_failures=0, deterministic at seeds 0/7/42 — a baseline pin, not a closure claim: 277 of the 310 are NO-reach-path candidates under the profile, i.e. the gated SV-only surface being profile-unreachable by design). The downstream write-up is § “Dialect Profile — verilog_2005” in docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md; tracker status Mostly Done. Two pre-existing all-profile grammar defects bounding today’s reject surface are ledgered as SV-0023 (event-trigger ->>/delay-form LRM fidelity) and SV-0024 (un-braced multi-identifier port expressions — the bare module m (interconnect w); form still accepts under verilog_2005 until it lands; the corpus pins the ANSI form).

Reading (of the pipeline lane)

One run of the whole preprocess→parse corpus lane — its library pass and every row — under one edition profile. There are two: the primary sv_2017 reading, over which the verdict-coverage tuple is defined, and the sv_2023 reading (PGEN_PIPELINE_PROFILE=sv_2023). Each run leaves a provenance sidecar beside its dump: the profile, the parse binary’s digest and the dumps’ digests. See The Preprocess→Parse Pipeline.

Recursive envelope

The default JSON shape produced by un-annotated rules — a recursive composition of arrays (for sequences and iterations), strings (for terminals), and matched-branch passthroughs (for alternations). See AST Envelope Structure.

Return annotation

A -> ... clause appended to a grammar rule definition that overrides the default envelope shape with a typed JSON value. Example: simple_identifier -> {type: "identifier", name: $1}. See docs/contracts/PGEN_RETURN_ANNOTATION_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md.

Schema version

Tracks the AST output shape. Bumped only when the output shape changes in a way consumers may need to adapt to. Currently 1. See Schema Versioning.

Slice

The unit of work in the annotation campaign. One slice = one rule (or a small family of related rules) annotated, the manifest updated, the contract bumped, the book amended, and a regression-lock test landed.

Stable surface

The set of public entry points downstream consumers can rely on across patch / minor releases. Defined in docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md § “Stable Integration Surface”.

Stress sample

A test input designed to exercise edge cases of the grammar — e.g. deeply nested structures, large modules, full LRM Annex-A coverage. Lives in rust/test_data/grammar_quality/systemverilog_* corpora.

Tool tolerance

A spelling the commercial simulators accept that neither IEEE 1800-2017 nor 1800-2023 derives and whose clause text speaks against it (for example foreach (a[i][j]), or a lifetime in a method prototype). The edition profiles sv_2017, sv_2023 and verilog_2005 reject it, by the strict-LRM default. Since 1.0.249 the OPT-IN profile sv_2023_tolerant accepts a closed list of such spellings and nothing else beyond sv_2023 — four since 1.0.249, a fifth since 1.0.250 (a hierarchical name of three or more parts inside binsof(…), the reference form of the dotted cross item; ruled by SV-CORPUS-GRAD.44, admitted by .45); each is pinned from both sides (rejected under the strict profiles, accepted under the tolerant one) and yields its own AST kind, so a consumer can tell a tolerated spelling from a standard one. The list, the standard’s rewrite for each, and the kinds are in The Json Carrier (The Opt-In Tolerance Profile); a spelling joins the list only by a ruling, never because a file failed to parse.

Typed shape

The JSON shape produced by an annotated rule. Always a JSON object with at least a type field and usually a kind discriminator. Consumers walking typed shapes dispatch on obj["type"] / obj["kind"].

Changelog Index

This chapter is an index — pointers into other docs that carry the full changelog detail. Use it to find what changed in a given release.

✅ THE GAP IS CLOSED — 2026-08-21, SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2z. This index jumped from 1.0.183 to 1.0.193, omitting 1.0.184–1.0.192 (ledger SV-0054…SV-0065, nine releases, four of which REPLACE an AST shape a consumer was already reading). All nine are now published below, authored from docs/contracts/PGEN_SYSTEMVERILOG_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md and docs/contracts/PGEN_RELEASED_PARSER_BUG_LEDGER.md — the authoritative per-release and per-bug records — rather than paraphrased. schema-versioning.md’s missing rows 21–25 are back-filled in the same change.

⛔ The back-fill is the smaller half. The same table silently skipped schemas 17–19 once before and was hand-reconstructed then too; a hand-fix plus a prose warning bought exactly one cycle. Nothing in the repository compared a family book’s newest published release against the family’s actual release, which is why the gap could grow from three releases to nine unseen. That check now exists — scripts/check_parser_book_currency.sh, doctrine PARSER-BOOK-CURRENCY — and it fails in both directions for every family that has a book.

1.0.252 / Contract 1.0.252 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.48 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0436, 2026-10-09), ledger SV-0137 (Released), schema 34 unchanged:

THE PARAMETER PORT LIST IS SPLIT BY EDITION — under verilog_2005 a module’s #(…) list is parameter-led declarations, at least one, and nothing else; sv_2017 / sv_2023 / sv_2023_tolerant unchanged. IEEE 1364-2005 A.1.3 module_parameter_port_list ::= # ( parameter_declaration { , parameter_declaration } ) (docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:38) and A.2.1.1 parameter_declaration ::= parameter [ signed ] [ range ] list_of_param_assignments | parameter parameter_type list_of_param_assignments (:126-128), against IEEE 1800-2017 A.1.3 parameter_port_list ::= # ( list_of_param_assignments { , parameter_port_declaration } ) | # ( parameter_port_declaration { , … } ) | #( ) with parameter_port_declaration ::= … | local_parameter_declaration | data_type list_of_param_assignments (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md:231-243). Through 1.0.251 ONE parameter_port_list rule served every profile with the 1800 production, so module a #(A = 1);, #(integer A = 1), #(parameter real A = 1.0, integer B = 2) (ivtest parameter_omit1/2/3.v, each headed “In Verilog this is not allowed and should result in an error”), #() and #(parameter X = 1, localparam Y = 2) parsed under verilog_2005. 1.0.252 gives the production a pass-through dispatcher over the 1800 rule (parameter_port_list_sv_only, verbatim, for the SV profiles) and a verilog_2005 twin (parameter_port_list_v2005: each declaration admitted behind a parameter lookahead, the shared parameter_port_declaration node) — the declarations kind and the same items, so every tree the profile still accepts is byte-identical, by construction and measured. The sibling parameter_value_assignment (mod #() m1(…), 1364-2005 A.4.1.1) stays admitted and is routed (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.50, watched by a pin).

1.0.251 / Contract 1.0.251 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.47 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0432, 2026-10-07), ledger SV-0136 (Released), schema 34 unchanged:

THE SIZE TOKEN IS SPLIT BY EDITION — a sized literal whose size begins with 0 parses under sv_2023; sv_2017 and verilog_2005 keep rejecting it. IEEE 1800-2023 §5.7 Syntax 5-2 and A.8.7 read size ::= unsigned_number (docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-5-lexical-conventions.md:213, docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:3200) and the edition defines no non_zero_unsigned_number; 1800-2017 §5.7 / A.8.7 and 1364-2005 §3.5 / A.8.7 read size ::= non_zero_unsigned_number. Through 1.0.250 one size terminal served every profile with the older production, so sv_2023 rejected text its own edition derives (01'b0; friscv rtl/friscv_alu.sv, 27 sites) — a REJECTS-VALID defect since 1.0.235, whose record had read 1800-2023 as agreeing with 2017 (SV-0120, corrected forward). The 2023 prose keeps the size “a nonzero unsigned decimal number”, so a ZERO size (0'b1) stays rejected on every profile. GRAMMAR: ONE terminal twin, integral_number_leading_zero_size_sv_2023, gated to sv_2023 (and the tolerant profile, which inherits every sv_2023 rule), returning the strict shape — the literal arrives as {kind: "integral", body} with the source text as body, no new kind. ⛔ Not a tolerance. The 2026-10-06 session had designed this spelling as the opt-in profile’s sixth member on an ecosystem reading (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.46: every tool on this host accepts it); the pins’ citations, checked against the 2023 text, refuted the design during the recovery from a host crash, and the release was re-run as an edition split. The opt-in list is unchanged at five.

1.0.250 / Contract 1.0.250 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.45 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0431, 2026-10-05), ledger SV-0135 (Released), schema 34 unchanged:

THE OPT-IN PROFILE sv_2023_tolerant GAINS ITS FIFTH SPELLING — a hierarchical name of three or more parts inside binsof(…); the edition profiles unmoved. binsof(cfg.vif.sig) intersect {1} is the reference form of the dotted cross item the profile has admitted since 1.0.249: a select expression has no other way to name an implicitly covered cross item, and every OpenTitan statement that writes it — all eight — names an item of its own cross. The boundary 1.0.249 left was an accident of token shape (a two-part name is cover_point . bin by syntax and parsed everywhere; a three-part name did not), written on adjacent lines of one select expression in core_ibex_pmp_fcov_if.sv. The standard’s text is against the spelling (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.44: §19.6.1, “either a coverage point … or a coverage point bin”), which is what a member of this list is; the admission is a call the director delegated (2026-10-05, “yours to make but better be sota, signoff and production-grade”) and is recorded with its reasons in the decision record. GRAMMAR: ONE rule gated to the tolerant profile, tolerated_bins_expression_hierarchical, as bins_expression’s third alternative — a two-dot lookahead, then a standard hierarchical_identifier; kind tolerated_hierarchical, shape {body: {path}}, the cross item’s own. A two-part name keeps the standard cover_point reading under every profile; an expression, a trailing select and a call inside binsof stay rejected.

IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.4 primary ::= [ class_qualifier | package_scope ] hierarchical_identifier select, class_qualifier ::= [ local :: ] [ implicit_class_handle . | class_scope ], A.9.3 ps_type_identifier ::= [ local :: | package_scope | class_scope ] type_identifier (footnote 43; 1800-2023 footnote 48), §18.7.1, Annex B (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md, docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:3097). class_qualifier is an Annex A NONTERMINAL, and the markdown the grammar extractor read prints its production head with ONE colon — class_qualifier := [ local ::43 ] … where every other head prints ::= (one such head per edition, 1 against 717 in 2017 and 1 against 734 in 2023) — so the extractor appended the whole line to primary’s null alternative, tokenised the footnote superscript, and emitted a literal keyword class_qualifier that three scope-prefix copies then carried as their first arm. Through 1.0.243 the parser therefore ACCEPTED y = class_qualifier m; (both SV profiles; on an integer carrier under verilog_2005 too), y = null class_qualifier:=; and the LRM’s own production text y = null class_qualifier:=local::43; (under sv_2017 alone) / …::48; (under sv_2023 alone) — nine pinned arms, none derivable from Annex A — while local::T'(1) inside randomize() with { … } was REJECTED because the type-scope twins demanded the superscript after local ::. From 1.0.244 the three token rules, the four welded null class_qualifier := … alternatives and the literal arm of primary_hier_scope_prefix / split_callable_receiver_scope / method_call_receiver_qualifier are gone (1738 → 1735 rules), primary_hier_scope_prefix is SV-gated (the literal was its only verilog_2005-satisfiable arm; its hosts read an empty optional there, as on every legal 1364-2005 text), and ps_type_identifier_scope_sv_2017 / _sv_2023 render local :: as {kind: "local_qualifier"} with the package / class scopes passed through byte-identically. ⛔ Three kinds that only the LRM’s own production text could produce leave the schema — "null_class" (the receiver twins), "null_class_assign" (the primary twins), "class_qualifier" (the prefix) — a branch removed is a schema bump by this book’s rule, although no legal text ever produced any of them; "local_qualifier" gains a second producer (the type position). Every previously accepted tree is byte-identical: no corpus file carries the literal or a footnote digit after ::, and class_qualifier / randomize as ordinary identifiers parse before and after (pinned). The leaf’s two owed measurements land with it: (b) the over-rejection half of local:: was closed by 1.0.211 at the primary and closes here at the type name; (c) a census of every kw_<name> token against the three keyword annexes reads 318 = 248 Annex B keywords + 68 LRM literals + two residual names — this weld and randomize (A.8.4’s own literal, not reserved, steals no identifier).

1.0.243 / Contract 1.0.243 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.31 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0412, 2026-09-23), ledger SV-0128 (Released), schema 33 unchanged:

⭐ The wildcard escape at the class scope — the UVM uvm_config_db#(T)::set(…) idiom parses under an open wildcard import. IEEE 1800-2017 A.1.9 class_scope ::= class_type ::, A.8.4 primary ::= [ class_qualifier | package_scope ] hierarchical_identifier select, A.8.5 variable_lvalue, A.8.6 tf_call, A.9.3 ps_or_hierarchical_tf_identifier ::= [ package_scope | class_scope ] tf_identifier / ps_parameter_identifier, §8.24 out-of-block declarations, §18.5.1 extern constraint blocks (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md); §26.3 / §26.4 make every declaration of a wildcard-imported package a candidate for the importing scope. 1.0.239 admitted an unresolved name at type positions and 1.0.240 / 1.0.242 an unresolved parameterized class as a type, but every class-scope head — class_scope_type_head, reached by class_scope from twenty-three sites, and class_scoped_call_prefix_head — is fact-gated on a declared class (🚫 Rule 'known_unscoped_class_scoped_call_class_identifier' rejected by post predicate 'fact_attribute_equals [type_name, uvm_config_db, declaration_family, class]'), so a static call, a static member, a class-scoped parameter, an enum id, an array through the scope, a scoped new, a method-call receiver, and the out-of-block method / constructor / extern constraint of an unresolved parameterized class were refused on both SV profiles through 1.0.242 while the same text with the class declared parsed (found by 1.0.242’s design probes; the dark worklist’s CROSS-FILE-FACTS rows demanding uvm_config_db are the corpus carriers). From 1.0.243 wildcard_escape_class_scope_type re-spells class_scope_type with the 1.0.240 head (import-gated, typedef-excluded, the parameter list CONSUMED — a bare ident :: never takes it) and is the LAST alternative of class_scope itself under an ordered policy — tried only where the known arm fails, which a declared class never lets happen on the same span, so the choice is provably the tie longest_match gave the first arm — and class_scoped_call_prefix gains an ordered last arm with the same head (1736 → 1738 rules). ⛔ The first spelling — a passthrough twin class_scope_escapable at nineteen sites under longest_match — read the lanes clean and was refused by the parse-cost ratchet: entries +1.43 % (the dispatcher entered 3.6 M times on the pinned sample, the escape’s asks paid at every class-scope evaluation, including where the known arm had won); costs are rejected, not traded, and the ordered in-rule alternative pays the escape only where the known arm fails. ⛔ The four type-position prefixes (scoped_type_scope_prefix, nettype_scope_prefix, the two ps_type_identifier_scope twins) take class_scope_plain, the first alternative alone: at a module item’s start ident #( … ) is also an instantiation head, and an escape that consumes the list there re-parses it on the instantiation route after the rollback (1.0.240’s first candidate, entries +5.18 %) — the module-scope C#(int)::t x; stays refused, pinned and routed to ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.111; inside class bodies and blocks the same type already parses. Under longest_match a declared class ties the escape on the same span at every site and wins by declaration order, so every accepted tree is byte-identical (measured: an escaped and a declared C#(int)::count render the same kind: "class_scope" node). verilog_2005 untouched by construction.

IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.8 block_item_declaration ::= { attribute_instance } data_declaration, A.1.9 class_type ::= ps_class_identifier [ parameter_value_assignment ] { :: class_identifier [ parameter_value_assignment ] } (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md); §26.3 / §26.4 make every declaration of a wildcard-imported package a candidate for the importing scope. 1.0.240 put the escape on class_type, which data_type reaches (class members, type arguments, class-alias typedefs); a block item’s type — a function-body, task-body, constructor, begin-end or fork-join local — is read by block_data_type, whose class-type route (scoped_block_class_type / known_unscoped_block_class_type / provisional_unscoped_block_class_type) carried no escape: uvm_tlm_b_target_socket_base #(int) bt; in a static function under an open import pkg::* was refused on both SV profiles through 1.0.241 (Surelog amiq_eth_ve_top.v line 10592, the dark row 1.0.241 left RESIDUAL and adjudicated PARSER-DEFECT) — the two unscoped class arms parse the parameter list and are rejected by post predicate 'has_fact [type_name, …]', the bare-name escape of 1.0.239 reads the name alone, and the declarator meets #(. IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.4 primary ::= [ class_qualifier | package_scope ] hierarchical_identifier select with class_qualifier ::= [ local :: ] [ implicit_class_handle . | class_scope ] (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-41-data-read-api.md:3126 / :3140 = IEEE 1800-2023 docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:3083 / :3097): id = this.arr[0];, id = this.q[i];, id = super.arr[0];, id = this.arr[1:0];, id = this.obj.z[0]; are one primary each. IEEE 1800-2017 3.13 puts a $unit typedef in the compilation-unit scope name space and a same-named net, function, port or parameter in the module’s, so wire T = 1'b1;, function U;, module m(input T);, the non-ANSI input T;, a tf port input T; and parameter int P = 5, T typed_value = 8'ha5, p::PT pkg_value = 6'h2a each declare a NEW name under an IMPLICIT type (A.2.1.3, A.2.6, A.1.3, A.2.1.2, A.2.7, A.2.4 footnote 18). Through 1.0.229 each read only data_type_or_implicit, whose data_type arm consumed the typedef name and found no declarator (the five iverilog sv_type_identifier_*.v rows). 1.0.230 admits the typed reading only where a declarator follows — data_type_or_implicit_declared := data_type &( declaration_identifier | hash ) | implicit_data_type, one new rule (1648 → 1649) read by the net, port and tf-port declarations, the same guard on var_data_type and the function return type — so the typedef name before = ; , ) is the declarator under the implicit reading (a first candidate spelled implicit-twin ALTERNATIVES; the parse-cost ratchet refused it, because the engine derives every alternative and a twin re-derived each typed declaration it also matched: committed +3.41 %); and it guards the default-less parameter arm with &( comma | rparen | semi ) — complete only there — and the type lists with the same reading. In the engine a lookahead is a positional child that binds []; ten templates in the shipped grammar had not counted it, and every gate had stayed green because the accept set never moved and an identity sweep compares a release with the one before. ⭐ A select on a receiver is an expression, and $ is a primary. IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.4 derives a method call’s receiver as hierarchical_identifier select with bit_select ::= { [ expression ] }, and $ — the last element of a queue (7.10.4) — is a primary. Through 1.0.228 the chains’ index operand carried only constant_primary, so q[$-1].delete and q[$].delete() rejected at the $ while q[0].delete and x = q[$-1] parsed (verilator t_dynarray_multid.v). 1.0.229 adds kw_dollar -> {kind: "dollar"} as that operand’s last alternative — every constant-index receiver keeps its tree. And IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.13 defines the relative tolerance range [A +%- B] beside the absolute [A +/- B]: 1.0.229 adds it to value_range_sv_2023 and to the covergroup twin as {kind: "relative_tolerance"} (the 2017 rules keep no tolerance range, pinned). Two additive kinds; 1648 rules unchanged; no engine, no codegen, no Rust. The answer key pins verilator t_stream_unpack.v’s { >> bit[1:0] {arr2}} = bit6; must_reject — A.8.1’s slice_size is a simple_type or a constant expression, and a type with a packed dimension is neither. Measured on the final bytes: the raw lanes the three raw lanes byte-inert — sv_2017 pass 9 847 / fail 6 489, sv_2023 9 872 / 6 464, verilog_2005 2 313 / 293, every count identical to 1.0.228’s, 0 rows moved (both shapes sit behind macros in the raw corpus); the pipeline lane 1 row fail → pass (verilator t_dynarray_multid.v), 0 the other way; the corpus AST identity sweeps read ast_moved=0 verdict_moved=0 on all three lanes (9 847 / 9 872 / 2 313 accepted trees byte-identical).

⭐ The standard’s notation separates tokens by white space. IEEE 1800-2017 A.6.5 writes the parenthesised implicit event expression as @ (*), and IEEE 1800-2023 A.6.5 spells it out as three tokens, @ ( * ). Through 1.0.227 the sv_2017 / verilog_2005 rule read (* as the attribute opener and derived @*, @(*) and @ (* ) only, so a space after the ( — @( * ), @ ( * ), @ ( *) — rejected at the * (sv2v’s sense_star.sv, which asserts every spelling equivalent, and eight OpenTitan *_pgd.sv files whose always @( * ) begin the pipeline lane reached). 1.0.228 adds lparen star rparen -> {kind: "wildcard_paren"} — the kind the sv_2023 rule already emitted — and factors the @ out of the six alternatives (event_control_sv_2017 := at_sign event_control_after_at_sv_2017 -> $2, a pass-through): the un-factored sixth alternative cost one at_sign attempt per failing position (+78,986 entries over the corpus, refused by the parse-cost ratchet); factored, the whole rule costs one, and the corpus cost falls (entries −0.16 % / memo_hits −0.18 % promoted, committed +88 accepted as the wrapper’s frames (introduced_wrapper_frames), the LR-family share 2.659 → 2.666). An additive kind on one node, every other node byte-identical; 1647 → 1648 rules; no engine, no codegen, no Rust. 1.0.227 / Contract 1.0.227 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.56 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0386, 2026-09-09), ledger SV-0100 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ A lexical fact lives in the terminal’s regex. Two were missing. IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5.1: a macro’s text continues over a newline preceded by a backslash and ends at the first newline that is not — through 1.0.226 the opaque directive line ended at its first newline, so a multi-line `define’s continuation lines were parsed as items (500 failing lane files carry the shape). §5.7.1: a based literal is three tokens — size, apostrophe and base, digits — and the digits “optionally preceded by white space”, where §5.3’s white space is spaces, tabs, newlines and formfeeds, and a comment separates tokens as it does everywhere; through 1.0.226 only spaces and tabs were admitted between the tokens. 1.0.227 spells both in the terminals; the apostrophe and the base stay inseparable (§5.7.1), pinned. And, exposed by that widening — the recognized-union certificate’s witness generator had composed based-literal time literals the glued unit must refuse — a third, LRM-faithful fix: a time literal’s magnitude is unsigned_number or a fixed-point real_number, never a based literal (IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.7). The value node is byte-identical for every real time literal; only the based-literal magnitude (0 corpus rows) is dropped. 1647 rules unchanged; no engine, no codegen, no Rust.

1.0.226 / Contract 1.0.226 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.55 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0385, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0099 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ A time unit after white space is an identifier. IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.7 time_literal ::= unsigned_number time_unit | fixed_point_number time_unit, and Annex A footnote 44 says the number “shall not be followed by white_space”. Through 1.0.225 the unit followed the number through the engine’s layout skip, so 1 s was the time literal 1s: #1 s = 0; lost its variable and trans ##1 s its sequence instance — §16.8 and §16.9.11’s own examples rejected. A whitespace-insensitive grammar had no way to say “no layout between these two tokens”: the engine skips layout before every terminal, a template cannot slice a regex’s capture groups, and the regex crate has no lookaround, so the only grammar spelling would have folded number and unit into one opaque regex and moved every time literal’s typed node. 1.0.226 adds the rule-level @glued: true directive (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.103: the rule’s regex terminals accept no leading layout; read in the one shared layout decision the generated parser and the parse-harness interpreter both query) and spells time_literal := number time_unit_glued with @glued: true on time_unit_glued := /s\b/ | /ms\b/ | /us\b/ | /ns\b/ | /ps\b/ | /fs\b/; the `timescale directive keeps the layout-skipping time_unit (§22.7 allows 1 ns / 1 ps). 1646 → 1647 rules.

1.0.225 / Contract 1.0.225 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.54 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0384, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0098 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ A package name lives in its own name space. IEEE 1800-2017 §3.13 unifies package identifiers in a name space of their own, and A.9.3 package_scope ::= package_identifier :: makes T::VALUE a package scope whenever package T is declared — a typedef named T, wildcard-imported or unit-level, is another name space’s business. Through 1.0.224 the package arm every pkg:: site reaches carried one gate, “the name is no typedef”, so a typedef of the name refused the scope outright and every class-scope arm refused too (T is no class). 1.0.225 makes the exclusion branch-local and adds a second alternative admitting a DECLARED package by its package_name fact under @branch_policy: ordered — tried only when the first alternative fails, its package_scope answered from the memo; both alternatives carry the same template. 1646 rules unchanged; no parser, codegen or engine bytes (the certificate planner’s name-gate derivation is made branch-local beside it, BRANCH-PREDICATE-LOCALITY.3).

1.0.224 / Contract 1.0.224 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.53 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0383, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0097 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ The parenthesised operator assignment is an expression, hence an operand. IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.3 makes ( operator_assignment ) an expression, so it stands wherever expression binary_operator expression puts an operand — §11.4.2’s own example is j = i++ + (i = i - 1);. Through 1.0.223 the grammar admitted the form only at the top of an expression (expression_base), never as a chain operand, so that example rejected at the ( after + (three bar rows); and the alternative was unprofiled, so verilog_2005 — whose IEEE 1364-2005 A.8.3 expression has no assignment inside an expression — accepted j = (i = i - 1);. Grammar tier: an SV-only paren_operator_assignment_operand reached from every chain step through an ordered pass-through expression_chain_operand, as a chain head with expression_chain_step+, and from the index rule; 1644 → 1646 rules; no engine, no codegen, no Rust.

Accept-set impact. sv_2017 / sv_2023: WIDEN by exactly the operand form — the sweep’s verdict movers are the pre-registered rows (ispras 11.04.02_01.sv, sv-tests 11.3.6--two_assign_in_expr.sv and -sim, fail → pass on sv_2017 and sv_2023, verdict_moved=0 on verilog_2005), the bar 41 → 38 on sv_2017 (rejects-valid 39 → 36, accepts-invalid 2), 42 → 39 on sv_2023, verilog_2005 unmoved at 43 (match 6028 → 6031 / 6019 → 6022). verilog_2005: NARROWS by the top-level form; the lane’s 2 606 rows carried no such text (AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP: profile=verilog_2005 files=2606 both_accepted=2310 identical=2310 ast_moved=0 verdict_moved=0 both_nonaccepting=296).

AST impact — none for any file the parser accepted before. The top-level form keeps its {kind: "paren_op_assign", body} node at the base of the expression (the alternative passes the same node through), and every chain step’s triple carries the node it did; ast_moved=0 on every lane. A newly accepted operand arrives as {kind: "paren_op_assign", body} in an operand_chain’s first slot or as a step triple’s third element. Pins control_paren_operator_assignment_operand.sv / control_paren_operator_assignment_top_level.sv / invalid_paren_operator_assignment_v2005.sv.

1.0.223 / Contract 1.0.223 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.49 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0380, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0096 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ A store gate that decides no parse is a resolution check Annex A never asked for. Through 1.0.222 the unscoped checker name carried a has_fact(checker_name) phase: post gate — the 2026-03-21 semantic-fact pilot — so a checker instantiated BEFORE its declaration (the declaration after the module, as Surelog CheckerInst/dut.sv and ispras 14.14_05.sv are written) or declared in another file REJECTED at its second actual whenever the actuals were sequence / property syntax, and test dut(foo); inside a program (iverilog program5b.v) rejected at test. IEEE 1800-2017 §3.2 makes a checker a design element, §23.3.2 lets an instantiated name be “previously declared or one declared later”, and A.4.1.4 / A.9.3 derive checker_instantiation from a bare identifier. The gate never disambiguated anything: with plain actuals the tie goes to module_instantiation by order, declared checker or not. Grammar tier: the annotation is deleted and, where an instantiation-shaped alternative competes, a beside-module twin behind !interface_instantiation keeps the cost flat (the ungated first spelling re-read every plain-actual instantiation as property actuals, committed +33.56 % on the pinned sample, refused by the parse-cost ratchet); 1641 → 1644 rules; no engine, no codegen, no Rust.

Accept-set impact. sv_2017 / sv_2023: WIDENS by exactly the forward / cross-file checker instantiation — the sweep’s verdict movers are the pre-registered rows (Surelog tests/CheckerInst/dut.sv, ispras ieee-1800-2012/14/14.14_05.sv, iverilog ivltests/program5b.v — fail → pass on sv_2017 and sv_2023, 3 / 3 / 0 movers, 0 pass → fail anywhere), the bar 82 → 79 on both SV lanes (unexplained_rejects_valid 80 → 77, accepts-invalid 2). verilog_2005: none (no checker instantiation in IEEE 1364-2005; pin invalid_checker_instantiation_v2005.sv REJECTS).

AST impact — none for any file the parser accepted before. ast_moved=0 on every lane; a newly accepted checker instantiation arrives as the {kind: "checker_instantiation", body: {name, instance, connections}} branch documented since schema 26. Pins control_checker_forward_instantiation.sv, control_checker_instantiation_undeclared.sv, control_checker_instantiation_in_program.sv, invalid_checker_instantiation_v2005.sv.

1.0.222 / Contract 1.0.222 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.50 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0379, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0095 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ A profile-blind arm is an over-acceptance on every profile whose standard lacks it. Through 1.0.221 unpacked_dimension := [ constant_range ] | [ constant_expression ] carried no @profiles on its size arm, so the IEEE 1800 unpacked SIZE form reg x [2]; PARSED under verilog_2005 — IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.5 dimension / range admit [ a : b ] alone (the size form is IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.5 / §7.4.2). Found by SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.48’s own two-sided control: the 1364-2005 twin of control_unpacked_dimension_size.sv was written expecting REJECT and ACCEPTED. Grammar tier: the size arm lifted into unpacked_dimension_size_sv_only under @profiles: ["sv_2017", "sv_2023"] with a pass-through dispatcher alternative (-> $1), 1640 → 1641 rules; no engine, no codegen, no Rust.

Accept-set impact. sv_2017 / sv_2023: none — verdict_moved=0 on both lanes. verilog_2005: NARROWS by the size form alone; the lane’s 2 606 rows carried no such declaration (the census by token read 0 rows, the exhaustive sweep on the final bytes confirmed it: AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP: profile=verilog_2005 files=2606 both_accepted=2310 identical=2310 ast_moved=0 verdict_moved=0 both_nonaccepting=296).

AST impact — none. The size form keeps its {kind: "expression", body} node and the range form its {kind: "range", body} node; the corpus AST identity sweep reads ast_moved=0 on every lane. Pin accepts_invalid_v2005_unpacked_dimension_size.sv flipped ACCEPT / accepts_invalid → REJECT / invalid (the manifest’s round trip); control_unpacked_dimension_size.sv and control_packed_dimension_range.sv unchanged.

1.0.221 / Contract 1.0.221 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.47 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0377, 2026-09-08), ledger SV-0094 (Released), schema 32 unchanged:

⭐ The string literal is split by edition, and measured in both directions. One terminal, /"([^"\\]|\\.)*"/, had served every profile since 1.0.0, and it was wrong for each standard in a different direction. IEEE 1800-2017 / 1800-2023 §5.9’s backslash-newline CONTINUATION — $display("Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall. \ + newline + …");, the standard’s own example — REJECTED at the backslash on every profile, because the regex crate’s . in \\. does not match a newline (five bar rows: Surelog AssumeProp, ispras 05.09_01, sv-tests 5.9-string-broken-line, verible forbid_line_continuations, verilator t_display); a RAW newline inside a string, which both 1800 editions and IEEE 1364-2005 §3.6 / A.8.8 forbid, parsed on every profile ([^"\\] admits it; 0 accepting corpus rows carried one). Grammar tier: three edition twins under @profiles, 1637 → 1640 rules; no engine, no codegen, no Rust.

Accept-set impact. sv_2017 / sv_2023: the continuation is admitted; a bare newline inside a string is refused (the one narrowing — it moves no accepted row). sv_2023 additionally admits IEEE 1800-2023 §5.9’s TRIPLE-QUOTED string """…""" (any character except \ inside; escapes as \ + any character; no look-around in the regex) as {kind: "triple_quoted", body} — verilator t_display_qqq.v, an EDITION CONTRAST keyed must_reject on the 2017 lane and must_accept on the 2023 lane. verilog_2005: unchanged — the 1364-2005 twin refuses both the continuation and the raw newline, and iverilog string12.v (a continuation) is re-keyed must_reject there on §3.6 / A.8.8.

AST impact — none for any string the parser accepted before. Every double-quoted twin carries the shipped {kind: "double_quoted", body} template, body the source text verbatim (quotes excluded; a continuation stays in the text — §5.9’s ignored is the consumer’s reading), so the corpus AST identity sweep reads ast_moved=0 on every lane. Pins control_string_line_continuation.sv / invalid_string_line_continuation_v2005.sv / invalid_string_raw_newline.sv / control_string_escapes.sv / control_string_triple_quoted_sv2023.sv / invalid_string_triple_quoted_under_2017.sv.

1.0.220 / Contract 1.0.220 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.46 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0376, 2026-09-07), ledger SV-0093 (Released), schema 31 → 32:

⭐ The last integer-vector shape without a kind, and the nettype alias-head guard’s blind spot. .3.45 typed the partial-typing residue and measured two items on its way out: block_data_type alternative 1 — the block-scoped integer VECTOR reg [7:0] v; / logic [3:0] t; — had been typed by SV-Slice-96 with the field set {base, signing, dims} and no kind, the only integer-vector shape in the grammar without one once its four siblings took data_type’s kinds in 1.0.219; and nettype wT x with f; — IEEE 1800-2017 §6.6.7’s ALIAS form (a declared-nettype base) carrying a resolution function, a form A.2.1.3 gives NO production — still parsed down the data-type alternative of both edition twins, because the .3.45 alias-head guard required the ; after [ scope ] <declared nettype> <identifier> and with is not one. Grammar tier: one template, one lookahead narrowed; no engine, no codegen, no Rust; 1637 rules unchanged.

AST impact — schema 31 → 32 (a REPLACEMENT). The block_data body of an integer-vector declaration is {kind: "integer_vector", base, signing, dims} — data_type’s own template — where 1.0.219 emitted the same fields without kind. Every other alternative is byte-identical. Migration: a consumer that recognised the vector form by the absence of kind reads kind == "integer_vector"; a data_type reader reads the body unchanged. Pre-registered by the .3.45 raw-envelope census on the 1.0.219 probe (712 nodes in 259 accepting files on sv_2017 and sv_2023, 130 in 73 on the 1364-2005 lane) and measured two-sided by the corpus AST identity sweep: every predicted file moved, no other accepted tree moved a byte, no verdict moved. One AST-shape contract sample (block_data_type_integer_vector) locks the kind; the vector pin’s arm is block_data>integer_vector.

Accept-set impact — one LRM-illegal form stops parsing. nettype <declared nettype> <name> with <fn>; REJECTS on both SV profiles at the with (the guard now refuses the alias head whatever follows; the alias alternative meets with where it needs ;). Every legal form is unchanged and byte-identical: the data-type form with with on a typedef base (nettype T wT with f;, scoped nettype p::T x with p::f;), the alias form (nettype wT x;, scoped), the wildcard-import alias. 0 corpus rows on any lane (14 with declarations in the corpus, every base a typedef). Pins invalid_nettype_alias_with_resolution_function.sv / …_with_scoped_base_resolution_function.sv (REJECT) with control_nettype_data_type_scoped_with.sv / _sv2023.sv (ACCEPT, the one-token twins).

1.0.219 / Contract 1.0.219 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.45 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0374, 2026-09-07), ledger SV-0092 (Released), schema 30 → 31:

⭐ The partial-typing residue is typed. 1.0.218 closed with the class measured — PARTIAL-TYPING-CENSUS: read 38 rules typed on some alternatives and not others, 19 of the untyped alternatives raw Sequence envelopes, in eight rules — and the corpus census on the 1.0.218 probe (RAW-ENVELOPE-CENSUS:, TOOLBOX §1.5h, every lane row) read 2 319 raw envelopes in 1 088 accepting files on sv_2017 (1 779 / 819 on sv_2023, 217 / 120 on the 1364-2005 lane): 873 of them the block-scoped integer atom integer i; / int unsigned x;, 542 the parenthesised clocking event @(posedge clk), 524 the structure-keyed assignment pattern '{a: 1}, 193 the two-value path delay, and so on down to the case … matches / inside forms and the global clocking block. Grammar tier: seventeen return templates, no engine, no codegen; seven test-only Rust dispatch arms so the rules take AST-shape contract samples.

AST impact — schema 30 → 31. Every newly typed alternative carries a kind; every typed sibling keeps its shipped shape byte-identically, so kind absent is the shipped form. assignment_pattern {kind: "structure" | "array", keys, values} (keys[i] pairs with values[i]) and {kind: "replication", count, exprs}; block_data_type takes data_type’s own {kind: "integer_atom" | "struct_union" | "enum" | "virtual_interface", …}; case_statement {kind: "matches" | "inside", unique_priority, keyword, expr, items} (the inside form’s keyword is the literal {kind: "case"}); clocking_declaration {kind: "global", name, event, end_label}; clocking_event_sv_2017 {kind: "expression", body} (the sv_2023 twin’s shape); list_of_path_delay_expressions {kind: "two" | "three" | "six" | "twelve", …} with the LRM’s position names (trise, tfall, tz, t01 … tzx); property_case_item {kind: "default", body}; net_type_declaration_sv_2017 {kind: "nettype", scope, base, name} — IEEE 1800-2017 §6.6.7’s ALIAS form, which was not raw but shadowed: both alternatives succeed on the LRM’s own nettype wTsum nettypeid2; and the longest-match tie went to the data-type form on both SV profiles. 1.0.219 breaks the tie in the LRM’s favour by a negative lookahead on the data-type alternative — it refuses an alias head [ scope ] <declared nettype> <identifier> ; — with the order left as shipped, and routes the alias base, a bare declaration_identifier through 1.0.218, to checked_nettype_identifier | wildcard_escape_nettype_identifier (the SV-0037 / SV-PARSE-STRICT.2 precedent). Two spellings were refuted first: reordering the ungated alternative misread nettype T wT; (T a typedef) as an alias — the two-sided corpus sweep caught it on one file — and reordering the gated one broke the certificate’s own nettype prelude (the generator renders an unplanned declaration with the first of two equally cheap alternatives; union UNKNOWN=2). The winner moves exactly on alias declarations (two per SV lane in the corpus); the one narrowing is the LRM-illegal nettype undeclared_t x; with no wildcard import, accepted through 1.0.218 and now rejected (0 accepting corpus rows, pinned).

Two non-LRM alternatives removed. list_of_path_delay_expressions carried seven alternatives since the grammar’s first promotion where every edition gives five: a second six-value spelling that lost the tie to the LRM’s on every input (Protocol D: selected branch 4/7) and a twelve-value spelling whose middle positions were the literal text tx_path_delay_expression; both gone with their keyword terminal, and the three ungated nettype identifier twins with them: 1641 → 1637 rules.

Verification. 30 pins (control_assignment_pattern_*, control_block_data_type_*, control_case_*, control_clocking_*, control_path_delay_*, control_nettype_* incl. the two wildcard-import alias controls, control_property_case_* — one per alternative, the typed siblings as the controls that cannot move, arms on the new kinds — plus the must_reject invalid_nettype_alias_undeclared_base.sv); 16 AST-shape contract samples (40 → 56); the interpreter A/B on the nineteen reproducers and a seeded corpus sample (87 arms, two-sided clean); PRESCREEN-PINS: jobs=781 verdict_moved=0 ast_moved=38 two-sided; the three lanes’ verdicts and the corpus AST identity sweep against the census’s movers are in the integration contract’s 1.0.219 note. See Typed Partial Alternatives.

1.0.218 / Contract 1.0.218 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.44 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0373, 2026-09-07), ledger SV-0091 (Released), schema 29 → 30:

⭐ function_body_declaration and task_body_declaration are typed on EVERY alternative. IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.6 / A.2.7 give a function or task body two forms — the non-ported type f; … whose ports are tf_item_declaration items inside the body, and the PORTED type f(ports); … with block_item_declaration items — each with an optional out-of-block prefix (I.f / C::f), four alternatives in the grammar. Through 1.0.217 only alternative 1 carried a return template (since SV-Slice-25, release 1.0.25, and every register that counts annotations counted the rule as typed from that day); the other three arrived as the raw positional Sequence envelope — 10 / 8 / 11 elements on a function, 9 / 7 / 10 on a task. The corpus census on the 1.0.217 probe (AST-FIELD-CENSUS: with the new --select-keys lifetime,body selector + TF-BODY-CLASSIFY:) read 2 211 of the 3 411 function / task bodies the parser wrote on sv_2017 as that envelope — 1 646 ported functions, 513 ported tasks, 30 out-of-block functions, 22 out-of-block tasks — in 1 060 of the 1 958 accepting files that declare a function or task at all. The ported form is the most common function in any corpus, and the typed AST could not read it. Grammar tier: six return templates, 1641 rules unchanged, no engine, no codegen; two test-only Rust dispatch arms so the body rules take AST-shape contract samples.

AST impact — schema 29 → 30. Every alternative returns the typed object, mirroring alternative 1’s field set: {return_type, name, ports, items, statements, end_label} (ported), {return_type, scope, name, items, statements, end_label} (out-of-block), {return_type, scope, name, ports, items, statements, end_label} (out-of-block ported); the task twins without return_type. There is no kind — the discriminator is key presence, which is the standard’s own distinction: ports is present exactly on the ported alternatives (the typed tf_port_list array, [] for f()), scope exactly on the out-of-block ones (the out_of_block_tf_scope node — the pair [<interface_identifier>, {kind: "dot"}] or the class_scope node). items holds tf_item_declaration nodes on the non-ported forms and bare block_item_declaration nodes on the ported ones, as A.2.6’s two productions read. Migration: a consumer that indexed body[N] reads the named fields — the same typed nodes in the same order, the ( ) ; endfunction tokens dropped as on alternative 1. Alternative 1 is byte-identical (the two in-block pins on all three profiles; every all-typed corpus file). A REPLACEMENT of a raw envelope by a typed node — the SV-0014…SV-0020 precedent — hence the bump.

Accept set — unchanged, measured. sv_2017 transitions: NONE (pass 9756 / fail 6580 of 16336 rows, 0 timeouts); sv_2023 transitions: NONE (pass 9780 / fail 6556 of 16336 rows, 0 timeouts); verilog_2005 transitions: NONE (pass 2310 / fail 296 of 2606 rows, 0 timeouts). Typed AST — moved exactly where predicted. The corpus AST identity sweep (the 1.0.217 probe vs this release, TOOLBOX §1.5e) reads AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP: profile=sv_2017 files=16336 both_accepted=9756 identical=8696 ast_moved=1060 verdict_moved=0 both_nonaccepting=6580 and AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP: profile=sv_2023 files=16336 both_accepted=9780 identical=8716 ast_moved=1064 verdict_moved=0 both_nonaccepting=6556, and over the verilog_2005 lane AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP: profile=verilog_2005 files=2606 both_accepted=2310 identical=2270 ast_moved=40 verdict_moved=0 both_nonaccepting=296 — two-sided against the census’s prediction (sv_2017: predicted 1060, moved 1060, predicted-but-identical 0, moved-but-not-predicted 0; sv_2023: predicted 1064, moved 1064, predicted-but-identical 0, moved-but-not-predicted 0; verilog_2005: predicted 40, moved 40, predicted-but-identical 0, moved-but-not-predicted 0). The final-probe census re-reads every body typed (sv_2017 nodes 3411 → 3411, typed 1200 → 3411, RAW 2211 → 0, unclassified 0; sv_2023 nodes 3521 → 3521, typed 1300 → 3521, RAW 2221 → 0, unclassified 0; verilog_2005 nodes 470 → 470, typed 379 → 470, RAW 91 → 0, unclassified 0). Pins ADJUDICATION-REPROS: checked=781 armed=149 listed=407 multi_profile_rows=279 failures=0 (eight new control_tf_body_*.sv, one per alternative of each rule, the two in-block ones the controls that cannot move, arms tf_port / !tf_port pinning WHERE the ports live); six AST-shape contract samples parsed AS the body rules; union certificate and 1364-2005 conformance union 1494/10/1469/15 + 1484/0 and 1364-2005 1186/370/802/14 both UNCHANGED and GREEN, deterministic across seeds 0/7/42, identities re-stamped.

⭐ The class is censused and owned. A rule is typed when EVERY alternative carries a template, and nothing censused the alternatives: the new PARTIAL-TYPING-CENSUS: (TOOLBOX §1.5g) reads every multi-alternative rule typed on some alternatives and not others — 40 rules with 25 raw-envelope alternatives on 1.0.217, 38 / 19 after this release. The nineteen (assignment_pattern, block_data_type, case_statement’s matches / inside forms, clocking_declaration, clocking_event_sv_2017, list_of_path_delay_expressions, net_type_declaration_sv_2017, property_case_item) are SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.45. 1.0.217 / Contract 1.0.217 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.39 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0372, 2026-09-07), ledger SV-0090 (Released), schema 28 → 29:

⭐ The thirteen compiler directives IEEE 1800-2017 clause 22 gives a syntax box are TYPED productions, and the parser refuses what the boxes refuse. Through 1.0.216 a tolerated directive line — at file top level and, since 1.0.178, at the in-scope item positions — was ONE opaque token, so compiler_directive.body was the line as a string ("timescale 1ns / 1ps“) and `` timescale frump , unconnected_drive pull2 ``, `` line 1 “f” 3 , a bare pragma ``, `` default_nettype supply0 and begin_keywords "VAMS-2.3" `` all parsed. Every clause-22 box is captioned *"not in Annex A"*, which is why no Annex-A-driven release ever transcribed one; this release transcribes each — `` resetall (§22.3), undef `` / `` undefineall (§22.5.2–3), timescale `` (§22.7), `` default_nettype (§22.8), unconnected_drive `` / `` nounconnected_drive (§22.9), celldefine `` / `` endcelldefine (§22.10), pragma `` (§22.11), `` line (§22.12), begin_keywords `` / `` end_keywords `` (§22.14) — box for box (IEEE 1364-2005 clause 19 reads the same; IEEE 1800-2023 Syntax 22-10 adds "1800-2023", one profiled version token per edition). 1593 → 1641 rules; grammar tier only, no engine, no codegen.

AST impact — schema 28 → 29. compiler_directive.body is a typed node whose kind is the directive’s name — {kind: "timescale", unit: {value, unit: {kind}}, precision: {…}}, {kind: "default_nettype", value: {kind}}, {kind: "unconnected_drive", value: {kind: "pull0" | "pull1"}}, {kind: "undef", name}, {kind: "pragma", name, expressions}, {kind: "line", number, filename, level}, {kind: "begin_keywords", version}, and the six bare kinds — at both containers alike (source_text_item and the non_port_module_item / class_item wrappers); every other backtick line the parser tolerates at file top level is {kind: "opaque", text} carrying the old string. Migration: switch on body.kind; read body.text for "opaque".

Accept set. NARROWS on exactly the illegal forms — measured over the corpus by the parser itself before a byte was generated (AST-FIELD-CENSUS: + the new DIRECTIVE-CLASSIFY:): 26 rows pass → fail on sv_2017, 23 on sv_2023, 0 on verilog_2005, each pre-registered, keyed must_reject with the clause or routed to the Verilog-AMS lane. WIDENS on one form: white space — newlines and comments — between a directive’s arguments is §5.3 white space (only §22.12 binds `line to its line), so iverilog’s GitHub-782 family (br_gh782c/d/e/f.v: `unconnected_drive /* … */ ⏎ pull1) goes fail → pass on all three lanes. Three readings a consumer should know: a bare-name `pragma is bounded to its line (@branch_policy: ordered — the grammar’s default longest-match tournament would let the expression arm eat the next line’s first identifier); the magnitude of a `timescale argument is syntax (1, 10, 100) while timeunit 2ps; stays derivable through Annex A and the precision ordering is a value rule not judged; `begin_keywords "1800-2023" parses under sv_2023 only, and under verilog_2005 `undefineall is an opaque text-macro use. Forty-one pins (invalid_directive_*.sv, control_directive_*.sv). See the schema-29 row of Schema Versioning and the json-carrier’s Typed Compiler Directives.

1.0.216 / Contract 1.0.216 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.43 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0371, 2026-09-06), ledger SV-0089 (Released), schema 28 unchanged:

⭐ IEEE 1800-2017 Annex A footnote 21 / §35.5.5 is grammar: a DPI import function’s RESULT type is one of void, byte, shortint, int, longint, real, shortreal, chandle, string, or a SCALAR bit / logic. A.2.6 dpi_function_proto21 ::= function_prototype carries footnote 21 — “dpi_function_proto return types are restricted to small values, per 35.5.5” — and §35.5.5 (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-35-direct-programming-interface.md:485-493) lists the types; 1800-2023 reads the same (:493-501, footnote 26). Through 1.0.215 the production was transcribed without its footnote, so import "DPI-C" function logic [7:0] f();, bit [1:0], bit [], reg, integer, time, realtime, an enum / struct / union literal, event, a virtual interface, a parameterised class type and a typedef name with packed dimensions all parsed as DPI results. Now dpi_function_proto reaches dpi_function_prototype, a caller split of function_prototype (the .3.31 shape — class-method, extern and pure-virtual prototypes are untouched) whose return slot is dpi_function_result_type: the data_type_or_void shape restricted to §35.5.5, alternative for alternative and template for template (1587 → 1593 rules, six new; grammar tier only, no engine, no codegen; every new rule @profiles: ["sv_2017", "sv_2023"], so verilog_2005 is untouched by construction). A NAMED type without packed dimensions (a typedef, a package- or class-scoped type identifier, a type(…) reference) is admitted exactly as data_type admits it — what it resolves to is semantic; signing on the atom and vector types is admitted (the subclause is silent on it); the export half of the sentence is not grammar.

AST impact — none (schema 28 unchanged). dpi_result_data_type carries data_type’s own templates, so every legal import’s typed tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.0.215: measured under the interpreter on 38 synthetic probes × 2 SV profiles and on the two control pins, and on the final bytes by the HEAD-vs-release AST identity sweep over 16 335 corpus files × 2 SV profiles (ast_moved=0 verdict_moved=2 on each profile — 9 778 / 9 799 accepted trees byte-identical, the two verdict movers the pre-registered files). A consumer reading import_function.proto.body.body.return_type sees the data_type_or_void shapes it already knows; the refused forms never reach it, because the file no longer parses.

⭐ The set-membership operator inside { … } is a chain element of the operand chain, and an inside expression can be the LEFT operand of a binary operator. Until 1.0.212 inside_expression := expression_base inside { … } wrapped its left operand and was reachable only at the top of expression, so y = a inside {2'b10, 2'b11} & ~b; and … && b REJECTED (furthest_position=630, the & after the }; Cores-VeeR-EL2 testbench/ahb_lite_2to1_mux.sv and verilator t_randomize_method_constraints.v:14 x inside {1,2} || x inside {4,5};), while (a inside {…}) & ~b and b & a inside {…} accepted — and the accepted one was mis-grouped: its tree read (b & a) inside {…}, against IEEE 1800-2017 Table 11-2 (11.3.2), which puts inside on the relational row above ==, &, ^, |, &&, ||. expression_base’s chain is now expression_operand expression_chain_step*, a step being the unchanged binary triple or inside_operator; expression, expression_or_cond_pattern and the three inside_expression rules lose the grouped form. 1575 → 1576 rules. Grammar tier only; verilog_2005 untouched (inside is an identifier there, pinned). dist is unchanged — IEEE 1800-2017 18.5 rules “dist expressions cannot appear in other expressions”.

ADDED: an operand_chain.rest entry may be the OBJECT {kind: "sv_2017"|"sv_2023", body: {kind: "inside", ranges}} beside the array triples. Migration: treat an object entry as the postfix inside {set} operator on the relational row; body.ranges is the typed open_range_list / range_list you read before; the left operand is the chain to its left. Every inside-free tree is byte-identical (interpreter AST JSON, HEAD vs 1.0.213, on an inside-free control and across the pin set).

1.0.211 / Contract 1.0.211 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.37 + .13z (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0366, 2026-09-04), ledger SV-0084 (Released):

⭐ Every word IEEE 1800-2017 Annex B reserves is now refused as an identifier — 248 words, derived from the LRM text, where the grammar had reserved a hand-typed 173. new, this, super, null, static, var, const, global, final, local, protected, virtual, every always_*, every assertion operator and every coverage word were admissible identifiers: reg global;, var final;, i.super.i = 1; parsed, and a class constructor written function new; input x; parsed as an ordinary function NAMED new (with C c = new; a reference to it). Two more Annex A footnotes become grammar: footnote 10 — no automatic on a data declaration outside a procedural context (module, package, checker and class sites; the randsequence code block keeps its lifetime) — and footnote 18’s parameter half — a body parameter carries its default (the parameter port list still may omit it; .3.35 closed localparam). A bare null gains the primary alternative A.8.4 names, and local :: (A.8.4 class_qualifier, the LRM’s own §18.7.1 x < local::x example) gains the production it never had; both had parsed only through the identifier hole. 1569 → 1576 rules; grammar tier only. Verilog-2005 tests that name a variable var, global, local or new now REJECT on the SV lanes — correctly — and the adjudicator re-keys each such row by parsing it under verilog_2005 (the edition-keyword pass).

1.0.208 / Contract 1.0.208 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.31 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0357, 2026-09-03), ledger SV-0081 (Released):

⭐ An array-element member access whose index is an increment/decrement or a parenthesised operator assignment now parses. clist[b[0]++].m <= 1; and clist[(b[0] += 1)].m were refused on sv_2017 and sv_2023 while clist[b[0]++] = null; (no member) and clist[b[0]+1].m / clist[f()].m (another index kind) parsed: IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.3 gives expression two operands — inc_or_dec_expression and ( operator_assignment ) — that constant_expression lacks, and the index of an element whose member is then selected was the one index path the grammar spelled through constant_bit_select.

1.0.207 / Contract 1.0.207 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.30 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0349, 2026-09-03), ledger SV-0080 (Released):

⭐ A UDP state table written with adjacent symbols now parses, on every profile. IEEE 1800-2017’s own tables are written that way — (01) (10) 0 : 0 : 1 ; (§29.3.4) — and §29.3.4 separates only the input fields from the output field, by a colon. The grammar’s three table rules had been transcribed from Annex A’s single-character symbol productions as references to the general keyword terminals (trivia /0\b/ …), and a keyword’s word boundary cannot match a symbol followed by another symbol character: every spaced table parsed, every touching one was refused, on sv_2017, sv_2023 and verilog_2005 alike.

inputbeforeafter
(01) 0 : ? : 0 ; — an edge indicator whose symbols touch, any profilerc 1rc 0

the same tables with one space between every symbol (control)rc 0rc 0, AST byte-identical
2 0 : 0 ; / 0 a : 0 ; — a digit or an identifier where only a symbol may stand (invalid pin)rc 1rc 1

How. Fourteen boundary-free terminals (udp_sym_0 := trivia /0/ … udp_sym_n_upper := trivia /N/), one per symbol character, referenced only by level_symbol, output_symbol and edge_symbol; the general keywords keep their boundary everywhere else it is load-bearing (assert #0, $finish(0), init_val, scalar_constant, z_or_x). The first cut named the upper-case twins udp_sym_X and the generated parser did not compile — six E0592, because the generator uppercases rule names into RULE_… constants — after the lint and the interpreter had both said green; renamed udp_sym_<c>_upper, and the missing lint arm is ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.91.

AST impact — shape-neutral. The three rules keep their kind values; every table that parsed before yields a byte-identical typed AST (measured on the spaced control, all three profiles), and a touching table yields the AST its spaced spelling always did (equal once source spans are stripped). Schema 26 unchanged. ⛔ The accept set widens on every profile.

Corpus proof, per-path and two-sided, both lanes: sv_2017 17 rows fail → pass (8 unexplained_rejects_valid → match, 9 already routed or deferred), none the other way; pass 9 813 → 9 830, the axis-2 bar 220 → 212; verilog_2005 6 rows unexplained_rejects_valid → match, pass 2 300 → 2 306. 1.0.206 / Contract 1.0.206 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0347, 2026-09-03), ledger SV-0079 (Released):

⭐ A cross body’s two implicit typedefs, CrossValType and CrossQueueType, now parse as type names inside the cross — and nowhere else. IEEE 1800-2017 §19.6.1.3 says “The types are named CrossValType and CrossQueueType. The scope of the type names is the cross itself and the types are not accessible outside of this scope” and “The cross types shall be considered as implicit typedefs in the body of the cross, even though the syntax does not allow typedefs to appear there explicitly.” Annex A declares them nowhere, so the parser’s sound store gate — right about every name a file must declare — refused a name the standard declares. The standard’s own §19.6.1.4 example (function CrossQueueType myFunc1(int f_lim); … bins one = myFunc1(cg_lim);) is vendored twice in the corpus, and both rows were in the axis-2 bar.

Three spellings were built and refused first, each by an instrument rather than an opinion: emitting the two names as facts into the scope leaked them after the scope closed, because has_fact is store-wide (routed to the engine as ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.89, with the book’s semantic-store chapter corrected); a lookahead recognizer could not be witnessed by the certificate; a dispatcher tried first, and then a pre scope gate, were refused by the parse-cost ratchet.

1.0.205 / Contract 1.0.205 — EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION.6 (PGEN-EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION-0002, 2026-09-03), ledger SV-0078 (Released):

⛔ From the entry systemverilog_parseable_file (--entry-rule), an import p::*;, a timeunit 1ns; or a `timescale item no longer parses — on any profile. parseable_source_item := semi is the whole rule; the three lines after it in the grammar are // comments (since 2026-04-25), and grammars/ebnf.ebnf:583-586 defines // as a line comment. The hand-written EBNF frontend knew only #, read those lines as live alternatives, and every release carried them. The rule is proven unreachable from the registered entry (rule_fire_partition), so from the default entry nothing changes; the generated parser moves in this one rule and the other ten generated parsers are byte-identical. The same fix stops indented comments after inline return annotations from riding inside the annotation token (14 payloads in 11 rules), so a comment-only edit no longer moves the semantic digest this contract is keyed on. AST shape unchanged for every legal input.

1.0.204 / Contract 1.0.204 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13p (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0322, 2026-09-02), ledger SV-0077 (Released):

⛔ A third delay value on an n-input or n-output gate, a pass-enable switch or a UDP instance no longer parses — on any profile. IEEE 1800-2017 §28.4 / §28.5 say of those gates “The delay specification shall be zero, one, or two delays”, and Annex A spells [ delay2 ] there; three delays belong to enable gates and switches ([ delay3 ], §28.6). IEEE 1364-2005 §7.2 / §7.3 say the same. The grammar had one delay rule with the three-value alternative at every site, because the LRM extractor’s footnote canonicaliser had merged Annex A’s delay2 and delay3 into one rule — the right keywords in the wrong arity, which no keyword census can see.

1.0.203 / Contract 1.0.203 — SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13o (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0319, 2026-09-01), ledger SV-0076 (Released):
